Tests test_closure_consuming_own_non_copy_param_is_multi_callable (+Map.insert) and test_closure_consuming_outer_non_copy_capture_still_once_callable; ownership 353 / typechecker 2043 / interpreter 1225 / closures 14 / codegen 2386; fmt+clippy clean. E2E: String closure + a unit-returning Map closure build+run AOT==interp, valgrind-clean. RESIDUAL (separate, filed B-2026-07-15-17): a closure that RETURNS m.insert(...)`s Option result hits a pre-existing closure-return-type codegen verifier error — surfaced, not caused, by this checker fix.
investigation: 2026-07-15: surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-15-13. A closure `let mut append = |s| buf.push_str(s)` called twice reports `append` moved-then-used (UseAfterMove) at `karac check`, but `let mut push = |x| acc.push(x)` called twice (Vec) is check-clean, as is a single push_str/insert call. Per design.md line 4876 a `mut ref self` receiver borrow is multi-callable, so a String/Map-mutating closure should be callable repeatedly. Root cause (to confirm): the use-classifier infers the closure's callability from its captures' modes, and push_str/insert (compiler builtins, not declared `mut ref self` in stdlib .kara the way Vec.push is) are classified as consuming the receiver, making the closure once-callable. The Vec.push path resolves to a `mut ref self` signature (e.g. column.kara / builtin) and stays reusable. Fix direction: ensure the builtin String/Map/Set mutators (push_str, insert, insert_str, remove, clear, …) carry a `mut ref self` receiver mode in whatever table the closure-callability inference consults (mirroring ast::is_mutating_collection_method), so a multi-call mut-capturing closure over them is accepted. Impact: a common idiom (a string-builder / accumulator closure called in a loop) is rejected today; the runtime already handles it correctly (B-2026-07-15-13). Filed separately because it is an ownership-checker fix, not a codegen/interp runtime fix.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round 13 (while fixing B-2026-07-15-13) — `karac check` rejects a closure that calls `buf.push_str` / `m.insert` more than once, but accepts the identical shape over `acc.push` (Vec) — SURFACE NOTE: ownership / use-classifier (method receiver-mode classification for compiler-builtin collection mutators: push_str / insert / …)

title: `Option.ok_or(e)` panics the compiler (ExtractOutOfRange at pattern_binding.rs) — it builds the result value in the OPTION layout {tag,w0..w2} (4 fields) but the value is a Result {tag,w0..w4} (6 fields); a downstream `match Ok(v)/Err(e)` extracts 5 payload words from the 4-field value and overruns
investigation: 2026-07-15: reduced from an Option/Result combinator probe. calls.rs's `ok_or` arm constructed both the Ok and Err aggregates with `struct_ty = recv_struct.get_type()` — the OPTION receiver's LLVM type `{i64 tag, i64 w0, i64 w1, i64 w2}` (4 fields, 3 payload words). But the method's result type is `Result[T,E]`, whose seeded layout is `{i64 tag, i64 w0..w4}` (6 fields, 5 payload words) with Ok/Err field_word_offsets both `(0, 5)`. So a downstream `match r { Ok(v)/Err(e) }` reads (0,5) and its bind loop does `build_extract_value(sv, start_word+j+1)` for j in 0..5 → field index 5 on a 4-field value = ExtractOutOfRange → inkwell `.unwrap()` panics the backend. This broke `ok_or` for EVERY payload type: both `ok_or(-99)` (i64 Err) and `ok_or("missing")` (String Err) ICE (the heap-safety gate only checks the OPTION's payload T = the Ok type, so a trivially-copyable Ok slips through to the broken construction). Fix: build the result in the Result layout — get `enum_layouts["Result"].llvm_type`, pack `e` into the Err slots (coerce_to_payload_words up to the Result payload width, 5), and copy the receiver's Some payload words into the Ok slots (the Ok binding reads only its natural width downstream, so trailing Result slots stay undef). Verified interp==JIT==native and leak-clean across Some→Ok, None→Err (String and i64), unwrap_or on the result, and a None/Some loop; the String Err payload round-trips leak-clean (asan). Regression: tests/codegen.rs test_e2e_option_ok_or_builds_result_layout (proven to reproduce the exact ExtractOutOfRange panic pre-fix); tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_option_ok_or_string_err_no_leak. NOTE: a heap Ok payload (`Option[String].ok_or`) and `map_err` over a String payload remain documented loud-bail deferrals (separate from this ICE). Fixed in b287a24.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round 16 (Result/Option combinators) — `o.ok_or("missing")` matched as Result panicked the compiler (ExtractOutOfRange) under karac build; interp correct — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (calls.rs Option/Result combinator lowering — the `ok_or` arm builds the result value in the Option layout)

title: Closure-param inference is missing for direct collection/Result methods that take a closure (`Vec.retain(|x| …)`, `Result.and_then(|x| …)`) — the param `x` stays `?T` and any use (`x != 3`) fails, while the `.iter().map/filter/any` adaptor path infers the element type fine
investigation: 2026-07-15: `v.retain(|x| x != 3)` on a `Vec[i64]` reports `cannot compare '?T0' and 'i64'` — the closure param `x` is never bound to the element type `i64`, so the body's comparison fails. Same for `c.and_then(|x| if x > 0 { … })` on a `Result[i64,_]` (`?T8` vs i64). By contrast the iterator-adaptor path threads element types correctly: `v.iter().map(|x| x+1).sum()`, `.filter(|x| x>2).count()`, `.any(|x| x>2)` all infer without annotation, as does `Option.filter(|x| x>3)`. So the gap is specific to DIRECT collection/Result methods whose closure param should be seeded from the receiver's element / Ok type (retain, and_then; likely also sort_by's comparator params, dedup_by, etc.) — the expected-type is not pushed into the closure param during check. Workaround: annotate (`|x: i64|`). Impact: ergonomic only — a common idiom needs an explicit annotation; no wrong output, both backends agree. Fix direction: when checking a method-call argument that is a closure against a `Fn(A) -> R` parameter type, push `A` into the closure's param inference (the same expected-type propagation the iterator-adaptor path already does) for the direct-method dispatch surface.
resolution: 2026-07-15 (c4820b1): fixed by seeding the closure's un-annotated param from the receiver's payload BEFORE inferring the body, then inferring the body freely. Two coordinated changes: (1) `infer_closure_ret` (expr_method_call.rs, the and_then / or_else / map / map_or / map_err path) now publishes a per-closure param seed keyed by the closure span (`closure_param_seeds`) and drops the old infer-body-then-unify-param order (a bare `Ok(..)`/`Some(..)` body was un-adoptable under a check-mode fresh return var); the synth-mode closure arm in exprs.rs consumes the seed by index instead of minting a fresh var. (2) `Vec[T]/VecDeque[T].retain(pred)` gets a dedicated typechecker arm (concrete `Fn(T) -> bool` check-mode pushdown) plus an interpreter impl (snapshot-filter-writeback, mirroring sort_by). Verified interp==AOT for and_then/map; retain runs in interp. An explicit param annotation still wins. AOT codegen for `retain` itself still loud-bails (interp-first) — tracked separately as B-2026-07-15-19.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe rounds 17-18 — `v.retain(|x| x != 3)` and `r.and_then(|x| ...)` fail typecheck (`cannot compare '?T0' and 'i64'`) while `v.iter().filter(|x| x > 2)` infers fine — SURFACE NOTE: typechecker (closure-parameter type inference for direct collection / Result methods that take a predicate/mapper closure)

title: A closure whose tail expression is an Option-returning method call miscompiles: `let put = |k, v| m.insert(k, v)` (Map.insert -> Option[V]) fails codegen with `Module verification failed: Function return type does not match operand type of return inst! ret {i64,i64,i64,i64} ... i64` — the closure fn is declared to return i64 (or a narrower shape) while its body returns the 4-word Option layout. The interpreter runs it correctly. FIXED 2026-07-15 (286636f) — infer_closure_return_type (src/codegen/closures.rs) had a MethodCall arm only for `cmp`; every other method-call tail fell to the i64 default, so an Option/Result-returning method tail (Map.insert -> Option[V], Vec.pop -> Option[T]) declared the closure fn `-> i64` against the 4-word Option body -> LLVM verifier failure. Added a general MethodCall arm that consults the lowering pass`s span-recorded enum_inst_type_exprs (via enum_inst_type_from_span) and returns the matching enum`s type-erased layout — the same treatment the Some/Ok/Err constructor arms already get; non-enum method results keep the i64 default unchanged. Verified AOT==JIT==interp, valgrind-clean, across building the closure AND consuming the returned Option via match, for both Map.insert and Vec.pop. Test test_e2e_closure_option_returning_method_tail; codegen 2388 / par_codegen 159; fmt+clippy clean. RESIDUAL (not this bug): a closure tail that is a String/Vec-returning method (`|s| s.to_uppercase()`) is a separate un-recorded shape that still falls to the i64 default — not covered here (enum-only).
investigation: 2026-07-15: surfaced immediately after B-2026-07-15-14 removed the spurious ownership rejection of `let mut put = |k: String, v: i64| m.insert(k, v)`. With check now passing, codegen emits a closure fn whose declared return type does not match the Option[i64] (`{i64,i64,i64,i64}`) the tail `m.insert(k,v)` returns -> LLVM module-verifier error, build fails loud. Narrowing the closure to a UNIT-returning body (`|k,v| { m.insert(k,v); }`) builds and runs clean (AOT==interp==2, valgrind-clean), confirming the ownership fix is sound and the gap is purely the closure return-type inference for an Option-returning tail. The sibling `infer_closure_return_type` (src/codegen/closures.rs) already special-cases a bare `None` tail and `cmp`/Ordering; it must also infer the Option[V] layout for a method-call tail whose result type is Option (Map.insert, Vec.pop, etc.), matching the typechecker`s inferred closure return type at the closure span. Fix direction: consult the typecheck result`s expr_types[closure_body_span] (or the recorded Fn(..) return type) to size the closure fn`s return type, rather than the shallow structural inference that defaults such a tail to i64. LOUD bail (no miscompile); interpreter is the correct oracle. Low severity: a rare shape (closure returning a collection-mutator`s Option result); the common unit-returning mutator closure is unaffected.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-15-14 — once the ownership checker stopped false-rejecting a Map-mutating closure, codegen was reached and failed — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (closure return-type inference — a closure whose body/tail is a method call returning Option, e.g. Map.insert -> Option[V])

title: A `<generic-struct>.field.method()` receiver reads the WRONG field for a multi-heap-field generic struct: `Pair[Vec,Vec].second.len()` returns the first field's length — the field GEP used the base (erased-i64) struct type, so field-1 landed at byte 8 (word 1 of field 0) instead of after field 0's full width
investigation: 2026-07-15: reduced from a nested-generic probe. lower_field_access_ptr (calls.rs) resolves a `<struct>.field.method()` receiver by GEPing the field off the receiver pointer, but the plain-struct branch used `struct_types[type_name]` — the BASE generic struct type, where every generic-param field is erased to i64 (1 word). For `Pair[A,B]` instantiated `Pair[Vec[i64], Vec[i64]]`, the real mono layout is `{vec(3 words), vec(3 words)}`, but the base type is `{i64, i64}`, so `build_struct_gep(base, ptr, 1)` computes the field-1 offset as 8 bytes (word 1 of field 0's `{ptr,len,cap}`) instead of 24. Reading a Vec back through that misaligned pointer, `p.second.len()` returned field 0's length (pg1: interp 5 / codegen 2), `Pair[String,String].second.len()` returned 0 (misread first's cap=0 for a static literal), `Trip[Vec,i64,Vec].c.len()` read the middle scalar (5). A SINGLE wide field or a scalar field was fine — the scalar-field print path goes through compile_field_access (extractvalue on the loaded MONO value) and binding the field first (`let s = p.second; s.len()`) also extracts correctly; only the field-receiver method-dispatch GEP was wrong. It also crashed outright on `p.second[i]` index-through-field. Fix: GEP with the per-monomorph struct type — resolve the receiver's recorded instantiation (`enum_inst_type_of_expr`) and `mono_struct_type(name, args)`, falling back to the base type for a non-generic struct. Verified interp==JIT==native for read (.len()), mutate (.push() write-through), index-through-field, and 3-field/2-type-param interleaves (Pair[Vec,Vec], Pair[String,String], Trip[Vec,i64,Vec], Rec[Vec,String]). Regression: tests/codegen.rs test_e2e_generic_struct_multi_heap_field_method_receiver (proven to reproduce empty/wrong output pre-fix). NOTE: the struct still LEAKS its heap fields at scope exit — the separate, already-filed B-2026-07-15-11 generic-struct-drop gap — so this is an output-only correctness fix (was wrong-value + leak; now correct-value + leak, the leak tracked by B-11). (NOTE: the shipped code comment / commit reference this as B-2026-07-15-17 due to a concurrent ID collision with another agent's unrelated -17; the ledger ID is B-2026-07-15-18.) Fixed in bf4b002.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round 21 (nested generics) — `Pair[Vec[i64], Vec[i64]]`.second.len() returned the FIRST field's length under JIT/native; interp correct — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (field-receiver method dispatch — calls.rs lower_field_access_ptr plain-struct GEP)

title: `Vec[T]/VecDeque[T].retain(|x| pred)` has no AOT codegen lowering — typechecks and runs correctly in the interpreter (B-2026-07-15-16 added both), but `karac build` loud-bails 'method retain not yet supported in codegen'; needs the same snapshot-filter-writeback shape the interpreter uses, lowered to LLVM (allocate kept-buffer, invoke the predicate closure per element, compact in place)
investigation: 2026-07-15: B-2026-07-15-16 wired `Vec.retain` through the typechecker (Fn(T)->bool param seed) and the interpreter (snapshot the backing Vec, invoke the predicate per element, keep the Bool(true) elements, write back). AOT codegen has no arm for `retain`, so it hits the generic unsupported-method bail — clean and loud, no wrong output. Interp / `karac run` / `--interp` all execute it correctly. Fix direction: add a codegen arm mirroring the interpreter shape — read the Vec header (ptr,len,cap), allocate/compact a kept region (or compact in place with a write cursor), invoke the predicate closure value per element (same closure-invocation path map/filter adaptors already use in codegen), drop non-kept heap elements to avoid leaks, and update the len. Element drop-glue must run for filtered-out non-Copy elements (leak-class care — cross-check under LSan). Until then the interpreter is the oracle for retain programs.
resolution: 2026-07-15 (93c8c0d): added an AOT codegen arm in compile_vec_method (vec_method.rs) mirroring the interpreter's snapshot-filter-writeback as a single in-place linear pass with a write cursor: for r in 0..len, load data[r], bind the inline predicate's param and evaluate it; on keep, byte-move data[r]->data[w] and w++; on reject, free the element via emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr (the same per-element drop truncate uses, skipped for trivially-copyable elements); finally len=w (buffer+cap unchanged so a later push reuses cap). The param is bound by SHADOWING (take/restore_var_metadata + a slot save/restore) so a capturing predicate still sees the outer scope and a param shadowing an outer binding is reinstated intact; register_var_from_type_expr wires .len()/.field dispatch on the element. Compaction is drop-safe: len=w excludes the stale byte-duplicate tail [w,len) from the Vec's own scope-exit drop, so every buffer frees exactly once (a self-store at w==r is a no-op) — a bug there would be a double-free (SIGABRT), not a leak, and the LSan test would catch it. Only the INLINE-closure form is lowered (codegen owns the element drop glue a runtime callback couldn't emit); a captured-closure VALUE / fn-ref receiver falls through to a clean, actionable deferral bail pointing at --interp (interp stays the oracle for that shape). Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind-clean across scalar, heap Vec[String] (filtered buffers freed), captured-predicate, keep-all, remove-all, nested Vec[Vec], struct-with-heap-field elements, retain-then-push (cap reuse), and VecDeque (routes through the same path). Full suite green (codegen 2392+1, memory_sanitizer 729+1, interpreter 1226, typechecker 2044; clippy+fmt clean). Adds a codegen E2E test (scalar+heap+capture) and an LSan test (heap + nested filtered-element freeing). Deferred: the captured-closure-value form (still interp-only).
detail: SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while fixing B-2026-07-15-16 — `Vec.retain(|x| pred)` now typechecks and runs in the interpreter, but `karac build` (AOT) loud-bails — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (Vec/VecDeque.retain in-place predicate filter — no LLVM lowering)

title: A generic-struct field-receiver method loud-bails for a ref-param receiver (`p: ref Pair[Vec,Vec]` → `p.second.len()`) or an indexed receiver (`v[i].second.len()` over `Vec[Pair[Vec,Vec]]`): the synth field-element binding is registered with the bare generic param type, not the concrete `Vec[i64]`, so `.len()` finds no handler
investigation: 2026-07-15: sibling of B-2026-07-15-18 (which fixed the DIRECT local-identifier receiver `p.second.len()` — both the GEP struct type and, via resolve_generic_field_te, the synth element type). lower_field_access_ptr resolves the field's TypeExpr through resolve_generic_field_te(container, ...), which pulls the concrete instantiation from enum_inst_type_of_expr(container). For a DIRECT local `p` that reads enum_inst_var_types['p'] and resolves `second: B` → `Vec[i64]`. But for (a) a `ref Pair[..]` PARAMETER receiver and (b) an `v[i]` INDEXED receiver over `Vec[Pair[..]]`, enum_inst_type_of_expr returns None (params aren't recorded there; an Index expr is span-keyed and empty), so field_te stays the bare param `B`; compile_method_via_synth_elem_ptr then register_var_from_type_expr's the synth `__field_elem_N` as a non-Vec, and `.len()` falls through with `no handler for method 'len' on variable '__field_elem_0'` (a clean codegen error + `--interp` hint). Direct-local (post-B-18), field-store (`p.second = v`), and index-store (`p.second[i] = x`) all work; gs1/gs2 verified. LATENT RISK: my B-18 GEP fix keys the mono struct type off the SAME enum_inst_type_of_expr(inner); for the indexed/ref-param receiver that also returns None → the GEP would fall back to the erased base struct type, so if a future change wired the dispatch without also resolving the instantiation, the field GEP would SILENTLY read the wrong field (the B-18 hazard). Fix path (do both together): teach the field-receiver instantiation resolution to source the concrete args from (1) a ref/owned PARAM's declared type (the signature is known at compile time) and (2) a Vec/Slice/Array element's recorded instantiation (var_elem_type_exprs[container]) for an indexed receiver — then both resolve_generic_field_te (dispatch) and mono_struct_type (GEP) get the concrete `Pair[Vec,Vec]`. Loud-bail, so no correctness hazard today; medium because generic-struct-by-ref and Vec-of-generic-struct are common shapes. (NOTE: filed under B-2026-07-15-20; a concurrent agent used -19 for an unrelated retain-codegen gap.)
resolution: 2026-07-15 (355d5da): resolved the field-receiver instantiation for all three loud-bailing receiver shapes via two paired sources feeding BOTH the dispatch resolution (resolve_generic_field_te) and the mono-struct field GEP (calls.rs lower_field_access_ptr). (1) functions.rs param-bind: record a concretely-instantiated generic-STRUCT param into enum_inst_var_types (sibling to the existing generic-enum param record) — registration_te already peels ref/mut ref, so the OWNED param (`b: Box[String]` → `b.v.len()`) and the ref param (`p: ref Pair[Vec,Vec]` → `p.second.len()`) are both covered by the same record. This is the piece the mono-path record (mono.rs concrete_generic_struct_inst) skipped: it returns None for a fully-concrete instantiation (any_bound=false), so a non-generic function's param was never recorded. (2) expr_ops.rs new receiver_struct_inst helper wraps enum_inst_type_of_expr with an INDEXED-container fallback — the instantiation of `v[i]` is the container's recorded element TypeExpr (var_elem_type_exprs), gated to a genuine generic struct/enum inst and excluding a range index; routed into resolve_generic_field_te and the calls.rs GEP lookup so `v[i].second.len()` over Vec[Pair[Vec,Vec]] resolves. LATENT B-18 GEP hazard the investigation flagged is closed in the same stroke: both dispatch and GEP now source the same instantiation, so the field GEP uses the correct mono struct type for param/indexed receivers (no silent wrong-field read). Interp was already correct; this closes the AOT loud-bail (build failure, not a miscompile). Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind/LSan-clean across all three shapes plus a mono self-receiver, a non-generic-struct param, and a Box[Vec] owned param (all unaffected). Full suite green (codegen 2390, memory_sanitizer 727+2, typechecker 2044, ownership 353, interpreter 1226, par_codegen 159; clippy+fmt clean). Adds a codegen E2E test (Pair[Vec,Vec] ref-param + indexed, output correctness) and an LSan test (single-field Box[String] across the three receiver shapes). NOTE: a MULTI-field generic struct (`Pair[Vec,Vec]`) still leaks BOTH bare-T fields at scope exit — that is the pre-existing B-2026-07-15-11 offset-erasure residual (present with no method call at all), orthogonal to this dispatch fix; the LSan test uses single-field wrappers to isolate the dispatch signal.

fix: a8d47f2 (Part A: RC-elision default-ON) + 36748bb (Part B: Some-binding elision + TCO) + Part C (borrow-forward relaxation of condition 1, folds in the wrapper/helper shape #110)
title: Read-only `Option[shared]` tree traversal ran ~1.8x behind equal-safety Rust — the residual was per-node REFCOUNT TRAFFIC (the balanced retain/release pair, NOT elided; the earlier 'RC is free / already elided' note was wrong) plus its TCO-blocking release epilogue. FIXED: the rc-elision convention (`rc_elide.rs`) is now default-ON (Part A: param + child-arg retains) and the Some(n)-binding acquire/RcDec is elided on an elidable-param scrutinee (Part B), which unblocks LLVM tailcallelim. #112 has_path_sum: 2.16x -> 1.13x behind C (parity with equal-safety Rust); zero rc ops per node + tail recursion loop-ified
investigation: 2026-07-15: minimal probe — `fn sum(node: Option[TreeNode]) -> i64 { match node { None => 0, Some(n) => n.val + sum(n.left) + sum(n.right) } }` over 8 pooled balanced 31-node trees, K=3,000,000 reps (the #104/#110/#111 read-only-traversal shape). Best-of-5 wall clock, same container: kara by-value 0.49s, kara ref-borrow (`ref Option[TreeNode]`) 0.49s, C clang-O3 0.22s, rustc -O 0.17s, rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on 0.34s. THREE findings. (1) RC IS FREE: by-value and ref-borrow are identical to the millisecond, so the retain/release on a non-escaping shared traversal is already elided (borrow_elision.rs) — the long-standing '~11% RC pass-by-value' figure (originally measured for kata #100 and copied into #104/#110/#111 READMEs) is STALE; there is no measurable refcount cost on this shape today. (2) ~HALF the headline 2.1x (kara 0.49 vs stock rustc 0.17) is OVERFLOW-CHECKING, which kara does by default and stock `rustc -O` skips: the equal-safety baseline is rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on at 0.34s (on this add-heavy micro-traversal overflow checks alone ~2x Rust; on a real kata ~25% — #111 rust 275ms -> rust-ovf 344ms). kara emits the same `sadd.with.overflow` + branch as Rust's checked build (src/codegen/expr_ops.rs emit_checked_int_arith), so this component is at parity and is a deliberate safety choice, not a defect. (3) RESIDUAL ~1.45x: kara 0.49 / rust-ovf 0.34 = 1.44x on the probe, corroborated by kata #111 (kara 504ms / rust-ovf 344ms = 1.47x). This is the genuine codegen headroom — per-node Option[shared] niche decode + match + field GEP + the two recursive calls lower heavier than C/Rust's raw null-check-load-recurse. IMPACT: only bites PURE read-only traversals (no allocation, no compute per node) — the exposed worst case shared by #100/#104/#110/#111. Allocation- or compute-bound siblings amortize it away and land kara at-or-ahead of Rust (#107 kara 30% ahead of Rust; #108/#109 tie or ahead). So it is a real but narrow perf item. FIX DIRECTION: leaner Option[shared] match/field lowering (fold the niche null-check with the field load; avoid redundant reloads of the shared pointer across the two child recursions) and tighter recursion codegen; measure against this probe. NOT urgent, NOT a correctness issue. FOLLOW-UP for the corpus: correct the stale '~11% RC' wording in the traversal-kata READMEs (kara-katas #104/#110/#111/#100) to the measured decomposition above (RC free; gap = overflow-safety vs stock rustc + ~1.45x Option[shared]-lowering residual vs equal-safety rustc). 2026-07-16 CORRECTION + measured decomposition (perf pass, container figures): kara sequential 0.448s vs rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on 0.346s = 1.29x on the probe. (1) The 'RC IS FREE / retain-release already elided (borrow_elision.rs)' claim was WRONG: borrow_elision.rs is the Vec-index CLONE elision, not shared-RC elision; the by-value==ref-borrow timing equality showed EQUAL rc cost in both modes, not zero. The compiled `sum` carries FIVE plain rc RMWs per Some-node visit: +1 Some-binding acquire (pattern_binding.rs), +1 per n.left/n.right chain arg (share_option_shared_field_ref_for_arg), -1 binding cleanup, -1 param exit dec (track_rc_option_var); the caller retains the pool element per rep. (2) IR-surgery experiment (strip those rc ops from the captured module, identical opt -O2 + llc pipeline both sides): 0.453 -> 0.390 best-of-7 = -14%, ~2/3 of the residual closed; output exact, valgrind clean — an rc-silent borrowed traversal is semantically sound on this shape. Remaining ~9% vs rust-ovf is genuine niche/match/recursion lowering density. (3) CONCRETE FIX DIRECTION: interprocedural borrowed-param convention for read-only non-escaping Option[shared] params — ownership-side analysis emitting a plain-data fn->per-param-borrow-flags map (whitelist: param used only as match scrutinee; Some-binding used only for scalar field reads and Option[shared] field args to borrowed positions; no stores of any kind; no calls other than borrowed-position calls (fixed-point over candidates, self-recursion included); every call site's arg a borrowable place (identifier/field/index/None), no fresh temps; fn never reified; pass disabled for REPL/test-module/declare-only compiles to keep cross-module conventions consistent), consumed at exactly four codegen sites: skip the share_option_shared_{ref,field,index}_ref_for_arg trio for borrowed positions in the call arg loop; skip track_rc_option_var's cleanup for borrowed params in the fn prologue (keep the var_option_shared_heap registration); skip the Some-binding acquire+cleanup when the match scrutinee is a borrowed param (pattern_binding.rs — sibling of the existing b2_skips_counts C2a count-free role gate). (4) The probe now lowers sequentially BY NECESSITY: the auto-par reduction on this loop shape was an unsound data race (B-2026-07-16-3, fixed b057501); re-parallelizing read-only shared traversals requires the rc-silent convention FIRST plus a reduction-gate relaxation that proves rc-silence of the emitted body. 2026-07-16 RESOLUTION (Part A landed): the fix direction in point (3) above — the interprocedural borrowed-param convention for read-only non-escaping Option[shared] params — ALREADY EXISTS as `src/rc_elide.rs` (`safe_elidable_ref_params`, four soundness conditions + condition-4 payload-escape guard, `docs/spikes/rc-elide-ref-params.md`); it had shipped GATED OFF behind `KARAC_RC_ELIDE_REF_PARAMS`. Disassembly of the #112 hot `has_path_sum` confirmed the earlier 'RC is free / already elided' framing was FALSE at HEAD: the by-value walk emits 2 retains + 2 releases per visited node (Some-binding acquire + one child-arg retain per recursion + two exit decs), and by-value (0.53s) is actually FASTER than ref-borrow (0.64s), not equal — the ref form adds indirection. FLIPPED the convention DEFAULT-ON (ownership.rs, opt out `=0`) after re-validating at HEAD: memory_sanitizer 736/0/1 == elide-off, codegen E2E 2400/0, par_codegen 173/0, lib 1025/0, clippy clean; corpus re-bench #100/#104/#111/#112 = 1.32x/1.23x/1.29x/1.18x faster, byte-identical output, #110 correctly excluded, +0 compile time. This elides the child-arg retains + the param-exit dec (the C2b borrow-skip channel) — ~2/3 of the per-node RC, matching the earlier IR-surgery -14%. REMAINING (Part B, this session): the surviving Some(n)-binding retain/release (pattern_binding.rs) keeps the right-recursion out of tail position, blocking the tail-call→loop that C/Rust get (C runs 1 real call/node + a loop on the right spine; kara runs 2 real calls). Eliding it — sound by the SAME condition-4 proof (the payload is projection-only) — should let LLVM tailcallelim fire; realistic ceiling ~0.33-0.38s (≈1.2-1.3x equal-safety Rust; the per-node overflow-check `jo` remains, which C omits). Status stays open until Part B lands or is shown infeasible. 2026-07-16 PART B + RESOLUTION: after Part A one RC pair survived — the Some(n)-binding acquire + scope-exit RcDec (pattern_binding.rs:198). For an elidable param condition 4 already proves the payload is projection-only (a non-escaping alias kept alive by the caller-held param), so the pair is the same balanced no-op; elided it via a new pattern_binding_scrutinee_is_elidable_param flag (compile_match sets it from scrutinee_is_elidable_param, a bare-ident-names-an-elidable-param classifier). Second-order payoff: that RcDec was a POST-CALL RELEASE EPILOGUE keeping the tail recursion out of tail position — removing it lets LLVM tailcallelim loop-ify the self-recursion (the C/Rust structure). Object-code confirmed: #112 has_path_sum now has ZERO rc ops per node and the right recursion is a `jne` back-edge, not a `call`. Measured (bench K=6M best-of-7 median): baseline(=0) 0.559s -> Part A 0.453s -> Part B 0.291s = 1.92x, vs C 0.258s (2.16x -> 1.13x behind C; at parity with rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on, the lone residual being the per-node overflow-check `jo` C omits). Corpus: short-circuit shapes TCO and ~double (#100 is_same/and 2.20x, #112 or 1.90x); combine-both shapes shed the RC but can't tail-call (#111 min 1.37x, #104 max 1.31x); #110 correctly excluded. Validated default-path: memory_sanitizer 736/0/1 == elide-off, codegen E2E 2400/0, par_codegen 173/0, lib 1025/0, clippy clean; #112 byte-identical interp/JIT/AOT/auto-par/=0 + valgrind-clean; new pin asan_rc_elide_some_binding_or_recursion_walk_no_leak. Fixed in a8d47f2 (Part A) + 36748bb (Part B). Escape hatch KARAC_RC_ELIDE_REF_PARAMS=0. RESIDUAL: the combine-both (max/min) shapes still make two real calls — a further TCO would need accumulator-passing or a different lowering, not pursued. 2026-07-16 PART C: Part B left one shape excluded — a thin wrapper delegating to a recursive helper, `fn is_balanced(root) -> bool { check(root) != -1 }` (#110). `check` passed conditions 2-4 but condition 1 rejected it because the wrapper calls `check(root)` with a BARE IDENTIFIER (scored as a move). It isn't a move: `root` is a `Ref`-mode param (confirmed via `karac query ownership`), so its referent is kept alive by the enclosing frame for the whole call. Relaxed condition 1 to accept a BORROW-FORWARD — a bare identifier naming a `Ref`-mode parameter of the function being walked — alongside the projection form (rc_elide.rs Scan.cur_ref_params, set per-body from param_modes; disabled inside closures, fail-closed; a bare OWNED local is still a move). Soundness is the same outlives-the-call guarantee a projection gives and does NOT require the enclosing fn to elide (a non-elided is_balanced still holds root's +1 across the check(root) call). Result: `check` now elides ({"check": [("node",0)]}); #110 goes from the sweep's holdout to 1.67x faster (elide-off 0.597s -> 0.357s, zero rc ops per node; no TCO since 1+max(l,r) combines both children). Validated default path: memory_sanitizer 738/0/1, codegen E2E 2400/0, par_codegen 173/0, rc_elide unit 7/0 (+2 new: borrow_forward_of_ref_param_keeps_helper_elidable, bare_local_forward_still_excludes_helper); #110 byte-identical interp/JIT/AOT/auto-par/=0 + valgrind-clean; new asan pin asan_rc_elide_borrow_forward_ref_param_no_leak. So the whole read-only-traversal sweep (#100/#104/#110/#111/#112) now elides. RESIDUAL unchanged: combine-both (max/min) shapes still make two real calls (no TCO) — an accumulator-passing lowering could add it, not pursued.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: kata-corpus perf investigation (owner asked whether the ~1.8x read-only-tree-traversal gap vs C/Rust is fixable or expected) — measured decomposition on a minimal tree-sum probe — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (per-node Option[shared] traversal lowering: niche-match + field GEP + recursion)

title: `let bound = o.inner` moving a struct-typed heap-bearing field out of an owned struct double-frees the inner Vec buffer at scope exit — both `bound`'s and `o`'s StructDrop free it (`free(): double free detected`, exit 134). The struct-var tracking path in the Let arm suppressed only Identifier (`let g = f`) and TupleIndex (`let inr = h.ps.0`) move-out RHS, never a FieldAccess struct-typed field, so no cap-zero disarmed the source's drop.
investigation: df3 (generic Outer[T]{inner:Inner[T]{data:Vec[T]}}) and df4 (non-generic equivalent) both double-free on `let bound = o.inner`; both pass `karac check`. Root cause: in stmts.rs the struct-var tracking path (`track_struct_var_inst` for a `var_type_names`-annotated struct binding) applies move-suppression only for `ExprKind::Identifier` (suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg_ex) and `ExprKind::TupleIndex` (suppress_tuple_index_move_source) RHS — there was no `ExprKind::FieldAccess` arm, so moving a struct-typed field out of an owned struct left the source field's Vec caps live and `o`'s StructDrop freed the same buffer `bound` had taken over. Fix: add the FieldAccess arm calling `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal(value)` (guarded on a non-owned_struct_params source, mirroring the Vec-field #17-gap-2 and enum-field #19 peer sites); its nested-aggregate arm (`zero_aggregate_field_caps`) recurses into the moved-out struct's Vec/String leaves and cap-zeroes them in the source slot. Only the `Vec.new()+push`-into-a-tracked-local construction reproduces — an inline array-literal field materializes its temp directly into the field on an already-balanced path (v1/v3 probes clean pre-fix), so the regression tests build each Vec via a local. The double-free fires at scope exit AFTER all prints, so the output-only codegen harness cannot witness it (verified: E2E program printed correct output with exit 134 pre-fix); the ASAN sibling is the memory guard. Verified clean post-fix under valgrind (df3/df4/deep-nest/multi-field/self.field-in-method/sibling-heap-field) and via `asan_nested_struct_field_move_out_no_double_free` (ASAN-dirty pre-fix, clean post). Distinct from the deferred B-2026-07-15-11 generic-struct-drop leak (which is a mono-awareness gap in move-out cap-zeroing for a whole-struct move-out); this is a plain missing-arm gap that reproduces for non-generic structs too, and is fixed without touching the mono-suppression machinery.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round (nested-struct move-out) — `let bound = o.inner` moving a struct-typed heap-bearing field out of an owned struct; native (karac build) double-freed the inner Vec buffer (exit 134), interpreter oracle correct. Both generic and non-generic reproduce; both `karac check`-clean. — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (stmts.rs Let-arm struct-var move-suppression — the FieldAccess RHS case was missing)

title: Moving a struct with a Map/Set handle field or an enum-with-heap-payload field double-frees the handle/enum buffer at scope exit (SIGSEGV for Map/Set, `free(): double free` for enum). A Map/Set field is a bare `ptr` the struct's `FieldDrop::MapOrSet` frees UNCONDITIONALLY via `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec`; `zero_struct_move_caps` had no Map/Set arm and the nested-field suppressor's LLVM-type walk saw neither the ptr handle nor the enum's i64 words, so the SOURCE stayed live and double-freed against the destination's drop.
investigation: Found while probing siblings of the B-2026-07-15-22 nested-struct-field move-out fix. dfA (`let g = f`, Holder{m: Map[i64,i64]}) SIGSEGVs (exit 139); dfE (Set field) same; df9/dfB/dfC (nested-field move of a struct carrying Map/Set) SIGSEGV; dfD (nested-field move of a struct with an enum-with-String-payload field) `free(): double free` (exit 134). All karac check-clean, interpreter correct. Root cause: `zero_struct_move_caps` (call_dispatch.rs) — the type-name-driven whole-struct move-suppressor — handles Vec/VecDeque/String (cap+len zero), Option (tag zero), enum (payload caps), nested struct (recurse), tuple, and the HTTP handle, but has NO Map/Set arm; the field's `FieldDrop::MapOrSet` (synth_drop.rs) frees the handle UNCONDITIONALLY (no `handle != 0` guard, unlike HttpHandleFree). And `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal` (param_own.rs, the nested-field move-out suppressor used by B-22's FieldAccess arm) matched only vec-struct fields and `aggregate_has_heap_field` structs via the LLVM-type-driven `zero_aggregate_field_caps`, which cannot classify a Map/Set ptr handle nor an enum's all-i64 tagged-union words. The line-4350 comment in `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg_ex` had flagged the Map/Set gap as 'needs a separate runtime change (null-marker convention through karac_map_free)' — STALE: `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` (map.rs:432) and every map-free variant already early-return on `map.is_null()`, so nulling the source handle is a pure codegen null-store. Fix: (1) add a Map/Set arm to `zero_struct_move_caps` storing a null ptr into the handle slot; (2) route named non-shared struct fields through `zero_struct_move_caps` in `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal` (comprehensive: Vec/String/Map/Set/enum/nested), keeping `zero_aggregate_field_caps` for mono-correct Vec/String cap-zero (idempotent overlap on Vec). Verified: Map+Set whole-struct move, Map nested-field move (non-generic + generic Map[K,V]), Vec+Map mixed, enum-with-String nested move — all output-correct + valgrind/ASAN clean (asan test was 2500-error dirty pre-fix). Regression tests: test_e2e_struct_move_out_map_set_enum_field_no_crash + asan_struct_move_out_map_set_enum_field_no_double_free. KNOWN REMAINING (filed as B-2026-07-15-24): a bare generic-param heap field positioned BEFORE a Map field in the same struct still mis-GEPs the Map handle at the base-layout offset (mono-blind) — pre-existing, unchanged by this fix.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round (Map/Set/enum move-out) — moving a struct carrying a Map/Set handle field or an enum-with-heap-payload field (whole-struct move `let g = f` OR nested-field move `let bound = o.inner`) crashed native (karac build): SIGSEGV for Map/Set, `free(): double free` for enum. Interpreter oracle correct; all karac check-clean. — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (call_dispatch.rs `zero_struct_move_caps` had no Map/Set arm; param_own.rs `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal` relied on LLVM-type-driven `zero_aggregate_field_caps` blind to Map/Set ptr handles and enum all-i64 leaves)

title: `zero_struct_move_caps` GEPs a Map/Set handle field at the BASE struct-layout offset; when a PRECEDING field is a bare generic param mono'd to a wider heap type (e.g. `Inner[T]{a: T, m: Map[i64,i64]}`, T=Vec[i64]), the base layout erases `a` to i64 (1 word) but the mono widens it (Vec = 3 words), so the Map handle's null-store (B-23) lands at the wrong offset and the real handle stays live → double-free / SIGSEGV on move-out.
investigation: dfI: `struct GInner[T]{a: T, m: Map[i64,i64]}` / `struct GOuter[T]{inner: GInner[T]}`, `let bound = o.inner` — SIGSEGVs (exit 139) on native, both before and after the B-2026-07-15-23 Map/Set move-suppression fix AND after the concurrent B-2026-07-15-11 bare-T mono-drop fix (5843cb9). Root cause: `zero_struct_move_caps` (and the enum/Vec arms too) build their field GEPs with the BASE `struct_types[name]` layout, in which a bare generic-param field is erased to a single i64 word; a monomorph that binds that param to a heap type (Vec = 3 words / String = 3 words) widens the field, shifting every following field's offset. So the B-23 Map-handle null-store targets the base offset (inside the widened bare-T field) instead of the real mono offset, leaving the handle live → double-free. This is the same mono-blindness class as B-2026-07-15-11 (which fixed the DROP classifier's bare-T resolution via mono-subst but did NOT thread the mono layout into `zero_struct_move_caps`'s move-suppression GEPs). Fix-path: make `zero_struct_move_caps` mono-aware — accept the per-monomorph LLVM struct type (available at the call site from the binding's slot `.ty` / `enum_inst_var_types`) and GEP fields with it instead of the base `struct_types` type, mirroring the B-11 drop-classifier subst threading. Deferred (not fixed with B-23) because it touches the delicate move-suppression GEP machinery shared by Vec/String/enum/Map arms and the shape is extremely contrived (a bare generic-param heap field placed before a Map field in the same struct, then moved). No non-generic or concrete-generic Map/Set/enum move-out is affected — those are all fixed by B-23. | 2026-07-15 UPDATE (investigation, still open): confirmed the root cause is BROADER than move-suppression alone — the STRUCT-DROP field GEPs (synth_drop.rs emit_struct_drop_synthesis_impl, `let st = struct_types[name]`) also use the BASE erased layout, so a NO-MOVE program that merely drops such a struct at scope exit ALSO crashes: probe `struct GInner[T]{a:T, m:Map[i64,i64]}; let g = GInner{a:vec, m:map}; ...` (no move) SIGSEGVs on g's scope-exit drop; reordering the fields so Map precedes the bare-T field (`{m:Map, a:T}`) is clean (offset unshifted), pinning it to the widened-preceding-field offset shift. A full fix must thread the per-monomorph struct type into (1) emit_struct_drop_synthesis field GEPs, (2) zero_struct_move_caps_mono field GEPs, (3) the nested GOuter recursion + o.inner move-suppression, and (4) the `let bound = o.inner` bound-binding instantiation record (so bound's own drop is mono) — AND is entangled with the B-2026-07-15-11 MULTI-field bare-T leak residual (the offset-0 `a:T` field is not dropped even once the Map offset is correct, so the drop path leaks 32B where it used to crash). A trial patch (mono-GEP in the drop synthesis + move-suppression + bound record via plain_field_type_expr) turned the no-move `droponly` SIGSEGV into the B-11 leak but did NOT resolve the nested `moveout` repro (GOuter drop + recursion still base-layout). Deferred as a focused multi-site pass co-scheduled with the B-11 multi-field bare-T drop; low severity + contrived, no non-generic / concrete-generic shape affected.
resolution: 2026-07-16 (7a2bfce): FIXED across all four sites the investigation flagged. Root cause was the mono-blindness class (cf. B-2026-07-15-11): the drop-synthesis and move-suppression field GEPs used the BASE `struct_types` layout, which erases a bare generic-param field to one i64 word; a monomorph binding that param to a wider heap type (Vec/String = a 3-word {ptr,len,cap} triple) widens the field and shifts every following field's offset, so the Map handle null-store / following-Vec cap-zero landed at the wrong offset (reads already used the mono layout, so only the drop crashed). Fix: (1) new `mono_struct_type_from_subst` (types_lowering.rs) builds the per-monomorph LLVM struct type from each field's subst-resolved TypeExpr; (2) `emit_struct_drop_synthesis_impl` (synth_drop.rs) and `zero_struct_move_caps_mono` (call_dispatch.rs) override their base `st` with it under a real subst, so ALL field GEPs + get_field_type_at_index become mono-correct in one place; (3) the bare-T heap-field classifier (drop VecOrString + move-suppression len/cap zero) is generalized from single-field to ANY position — the original B-11 `kinds.len()==1` / `field_names.len()==1` gates existed ONLY because the base layout mis-offset a mid bare-T field; (4) `field_move_out_struct_inst` (param_own.rs) derives the moved-out binding's concrete instantiation (GInner[Vec[i64]]) from the object's recorded inst + the field's declared type, feeding both `bound`'s own mono drop (enum_inst_var_types, stmts.rs let-inst recording) and the mono source-suppression (suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal now calls zero_struct_move_caps_mono with the derived subst). The entangled B-11 multi-field leak residual the prior trial patch turned up is ALSO resolved: generalizing the classifier drains the offset-0 bare-T field too (no leak where it used to crash). All gated to subst.is_some() — non-generic and concrete-generic structs are byte-identical. Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind-clean (0 errors, 0 leaked) across: String bare-T before Map (no move); Vec[String] bare-T before Map (drains inner elements); two bare-T Vec fields before Map with a whole-struct move (`let g = f`); and a nested field move-out (`let bound = o.inner`). Full suite green (codegen 2397, memory_sanitizer 734; clippy+fmt clean). Adds test_e2e_mono_bare_t_heap_field_before_map_no_crash + asan_mono_bare_t_heap_field_before_map_no_double_free. NOTE: while testing, a SEPARATE pre-existing double-free surfaced (a struct FIELD of type Map[K, heap-value] like Map[i64, String] double-frees at scope-exit drop, non-generic AND generic, confirmed on the clean tree — orthogonal to this mono-layout bug); filed as B-2026-07-16-1. The B-24 tests deliberately use Map[i64,i64] scalar-value maps to isolate the layout fix from that unrelated bug.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: probe dfI, found while fixing B-2026-07-15-23 — a bare generic-param heap field positioned BEFORE a Map field in the same struct, then moved (whole-struct or nested-field), SIGSEGVs; both the interpreter and the B-23 fix leave it crashing (unchanged pre/post B-23 and pre/post the B-2026-07-15-11 mono-drop fix). — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (call_dispatch.rs `zero_struct_move_caps` GEPs the Map handle field using the BASE erased struct layout, not the per-monomorph layout — the mono-blindness class, cf. B-2026-07-15-11)

title: Reassigning a struct's heap-owning field (`o.f = x`) never drops the OLD field value: leaks it for a fresh RHS (`h.v = [9,8,7]` strands the old Vec buffer), or double-frees / SIGSEGVs for a moved-binding RHS (`h.v = v2`, `h.s = heap_str`, `h.m = m2`) because the source's own scope-exit cleanup isn't suppressed. Separately, Map/Set VARIABLE reassignment (`m = m2`, `set_a = set_b`) leaks the old handle AND double-frees the source — the Assign arm's eager-free + move-suppression are Vec/String-only (`lhs_is_tracked_vec`); Vec/String var reassignment works.
investigation: MATRIX (native): Vec VAR reassign (`a = b`) CLEAN; String VAR reassign CLEAN; Vec FIELD reassign fresh-RHS (`h.v = [9,8,7]`) LEAK 32B (exit 0); Vec FIELD reassign moved-RHS (`h.v = v2`) DOUBLE-FREE exit 134 + 32B leak; String FIELD reassign heap-RHS (`h.s = heap_str`) DOUBLE-FREE exit 134 + 56B leak; Map FIELD reassign (`h.m = m2`) SIGSEGV exit 139 + 72B leak; Map VAR reassign (`m = m2`) SIGSEGV exit 139 + 72B leak; Set VAR reassign SIGSEGV exit 139. (Note: a String FIELD reassign with STATIC-LITERAL operands is clean only because cap=0 literals own no heap — not a real pass.) All karac check-clean, interpreter correct; confirmed pre-existing on baseline e0d1fea (not caused by the B-22/B-23 move-suppression fixes, which are separate paths). ROOT CAUSE — two gaps: (1) `compile_field_store` (expr_ops.rs:981-1358) stores the new value into a plain-struct field slot with NO drop of the old field value and NO source-suppression — it handles union/SoA/indexed-shared/option-shared field stores specially but the plain heap-field (Vec/String/Map/Set) case just overwrites, so the old buffer/handle leaks and (for a moved-binding RHS) the source's scope-exit cleanup double-frees the now-shared buffer. (2) The stmts.rs Assign-arm eager-free (~5293) + `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg` (~5356) that make Vec/String VAR reassignment correct are gated on `lhs_is_tracked_vec = vec_elem_types.contains_key(name)`, which is false for Map/Set vars — so `m = m2` neither frees the old handle nor suppresses m2's `FreeMapHandle`. FIX-PATH: (a) in `compile_field_store`'s plain-struct-field branch, before the store, load the old field value and drop it via the same per-field-type machinery the struct-drop uses (Vec/String `emit_free_vec_buffer_if_owned` / cap-guarded free; Map/Set `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` — already null-safe; enum `zero_enum_payload_caps`-free; nested struct recursive drop), gated to non-shared/non-option/non-SoA fields (those paths already handle their own old-side release — do NOT double it); then suppress the source binding's cleanup when the RHS is a moved Identifier (Vec via `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg`, Map/Set via `suppress_map_cleanup_for_tail_identifier`). (b) In the Assign var-reassign arm, add a `lhs_is_tracked_map`/Set parallel to the `lhs_is_tracked_vec` eager-free: free the loaded old handle and suppress the source's `FreeMapHandle`. Both legs are needed; each is verifiable with an ASAN loop test (leak accumulates) plus an output test. Risk: the field-store path has many special-cased branches (shared struct, Option[shared], SoA, HTTP handle) that already manage old-side release — the drop-old must be added ONLY on the plain-struct-field fall-through to avoid double-freeing those. Deferred from immediate fix because it touches the hot `compile_field_store` + Assign core with heavy special-casing and warrants a focused, carefully-tested pass rather than a late-session change.
resolution: 2026-07-15 (c588e30): fixed both root-cause gaps. (a) expr_ops.rs compile_field_store — the plain-owned-struct-field store (the fall-through past shared/Option[shared]/SoA/union/indexed-shared, each of which returns early and manages its own old-side release) now runs drop_old_plain_struct_field before overwriting: GEP the field slot and drop the old value via emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr (Vec/String buffer free, Map/Set type-erased per-entry free, enum payload, nested-struct recursion; scalar no-op), with the field TypeExpr resolved through the receiver's generic instantiation first. plain_field_type_expr classifies the field so the Assign FieldAccess arm suppresses the moved source (Vec/String via suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg, Map/Set via suppress_map_cleanup_for_tail_identifier). Only the plain fall-through calls the drop, so the special-cased branches never double-drop. (b) stmts.rs Assign var-reassign arm + call_dispatch.rs eager_free_old_map_var_handle — a lhs_is_tracked_map/Set parallel to the Vec eager-free reuses the var's queued FreeMapHandle per-entry drop params via emit_free_one_map_handle on the current handle, then suppresses the moved source's FreeMapHandle; the var's own FreeMapHandle stays and frees the new handle at scope exit. Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind-clean across every matrix entry (Vec/String/Map field reassign fresh+moved, Map/Set var reassign) plus self-alias (m=m no-op), Map[i64,String] var reassign, and repeated field reassign. Full suite green (codegen 2393+1, memory_sanitizer 730+1, typechecker 2044, ownership 353, interpreter 1226, par_codegen 159; clippy+fmt clean). Adds a codegen E2E output test + a loop-driven LSan test across all shapes. TWO pre-existing, ORTHOGONAL issues surfaced while testing (NOT caused by this fix, NOT touched here): (1) Map[K, String].get().unwrap() double-frees the value INDEPENDENT of any reassignment (filed separately); (2) `v = v` Vec self-alias leaks 32B via the existing (pre-fix) suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg firing on a self-assign (the eager-free is already self-alias-gated; the suppress is not). Both are minor/contrived relative to the reassignment class fixed here.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: overnight probe round (reassignment of heap-owning vars/fields) — reassigning a struct's heap field (`o.f = x`) or a Map/Set variable (`m = m2`) leaks the old value and (when the RHS is a moved binding) double-frees the source; native crashes / leaks, interpreter oracle correct, all karac check-clean. — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (expr_ops.rs `compile_field_store` never drops the old field value for a plain-struct heap field; stmts.rs Assign arm eager-free + `suppress_source_vec_cleanup_for_arg` are gated to `lhs_is_tracked_vec` only, so Map/Set var reassignment is uncovered)

title: An INLINE `map.get(k).unwrap()` whose value is heap-owning (`Map[i64, String]` / `Map[i64, Vec[..]]`) double-frees: `println(m.get(2).unwrap())` and `m.get(2).unwrap().len()` free the bucket's buffer as an inline temporary AND again at the map's scope-exit per-entry free. Binding first (`let v = m.get(2).unwrap(); println(v)`) is CLEAN — the residual is only the directly-consumed temporary path.
investigation: 2026-07-15: probes a/b/c. (a) `println(m.get(2).unwrap())` over Map[i64,String] → free(): double free (exit 134). (b) `let v = m.get(2).unwrap(); println(v)` → CLEAN. (c) `m.get(2).unwrap().len()` over Map[i64,Vec[i64]] → double free. Interpreter correct for all. So the bound-binding leg (B-2026-07-14-15, FIXED) reconstructs/clones the value for the `let`, but the INLINE-temporary consumption path (value fed straight into println / a method call) still hands out an ALIAS of the map's live bucket {ptr,len,cap} rather than an owned clone; the temporary's drop then frees the buffer the map still owns and re-frees at the map's scope-exit per-entry free. Pre-existing and ORTHOGONAL to the B-2026-07-15-25 reassignment fix (surfaced only because a B-25 test happened to print an inline get().unwrap()). Fix-path: in the Map get().unwrap() lowering, deep-clone the heap value for the inline-temporary case the same way the bound-binding leg does (or route the inline temp through the bound-binding reconstruction), gated to heap value types (String/Vec/nested); scalar values are unaffected. Verifiable with an ASAN one-liner (`println(m.get(k).unwrap())`) plus an output test.
resolution: 2026-07-15 (e465acb): fixed by zeroing the borrow view's `cap` at the unwrap payload reconstruction (calls.rs try_compile_option_result_method, after rebuild_value_from_payload_words) when the receiver is `<map>.get(k)` on a non-shared heap value — gated by the new unwrap_receiver_is_nonshared_heap_value_map_get (stmts.rs, the receiver-form sibling of is_nonshared_heap_value_map_get_unwrap). map.get(k) packs a BORROW of the bucket's {ptr,len,cap} (the map owns the buffer); consumed inline, the temporary's own `cap > 0` free-guard (print's emit_print_and_free_string, method-receiver/arg drop) freed it, and the map's scope-exit per-entry drop freed it again → double-free. Zeroing cap makes the value a {ptr,len,0} read-only borrow view: EVERY consumer's `cap > 0` guard skips the free (uniform, no per-site handling, no clone), the map stays sole owner, and reads (len/print/index) use ptr+len unaffected. Harmless for the let-bound case (borrow-elided, reads only) and it also closes that binding's latent move-out double-free. Gated to the map.get shape, so a genuinely-owned unwrap payload keeps its real cap and still frees (verified: an owned Option[String] unwrap in a loop stays leak-clean). Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind-clean across println / method-receiver / fn-arg / bound consumption over String and Vec values, in a 60-iter loop (map still frees its values — no leak). Full suite green (codegen 2394+1, memory_sanitizer 731+1, typechecker 2044, ownership 353, interpreter 1226, par_codegen 159; clippy+fmt clean). Adds a codegen E2E + LSan test. NOTE: a separate pre-existing gap surfaced — inline-indexing an unwrapped map-get Vec (`m.get(k).unwrap()[i]`) loud-bails 'Index operator applied to non-array type' (an inline-index-on-temporary limitation, orthogonal to this double-free; binding first works); filed as B-2026-07-15-27.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while testing B-2026-07-15-25 — an INLINE `m.get(k).unwrap()` of a heap-typed Map value (String/Vec) double-frees; binding to a `let` first is clean. — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (Map `get(k).unwrap()` inline-temporary path for a heap value — the unwrapped value aliases the map's live bucket buffer instead of cloning, so the inline temp's drop AND the map's scope-exit per-entry free hit the same buffer)

title: Inline-indexing a temporary Vec (`m.get(k).unwrap()[i]`, and likely any `<method-chain>[i]`) loud-bails 'Index operator applied to non-array type'; binding the temporary first (`let v = m.get(k).unwrap(); v[i]`) works. Interp correct.
investigation: 2026-07-15: `let mut m: Map[i64, Vec[i64]] = Map.new(); m.insert(1,[10,20,30]); println(m.get(1).unwrap()[1])` — interp prints 20, AOT `karac build` bails 'codegen failed: Index operator applied to non-array type'. Binding first (`let v = m.get(1).unwrap(); println(v[1])`) is clean (20). So codegen's Index lowering only recognises an identifier/known-array receiver, not an inline temporary Vec produced by a method-call chain; the compile_index arm doesn't materialise a synth binding for a non-identifier Vec-typed receiver the way the field/for paths do. Orthogonal to the B-2026-07-15-26 double-free (that was fixed independently; this is a missing lowering, not a memory bug). Fix-path: in compile_index, when the object is a non-identifier expression whose value is a Vec {ptr,len,cap}, compile it to a temp, mint a synth Vec identifier (register vec_elem_types/var_elem_type_exprs from the inferred element type), and recurse — the same synth-identifier hoist compile_nested_index_read / compile_for_indexed_iter already use. Low severity — the bound form is a one-line workaround and the interpreter is the oracle.
resolution: 2026-07-16 (354b4df): fixed by materializing the borrow view and indexing it. `map.get(k)` returns `Option[ref V]`, so `m.get(k).unwrap()` is a BORROW of the map's bucket buffer — a `{ptr,len,cap=0}` view (B-2026-07-15-26 zeroed the cap). compile_index now routes the shape through compile_inline_temp_vec_index_ex(.., owns_temp=false): materialize the view into a synth Vec local, read the element (deep-cloning a heap element so the read stands alone), and — unlike the fresh-owned temp path (`make()[i]`/`shape()[k]`, owns_temp=true) — do NOT drop the temp (the map owns the buffer AND its elements; because emit_vec_drop_fn drains 0..len before the cap-guarded buffer free, a drop would double-free every heap element). New gate map_get_unwrap_vec_value_te (non-shared Vec value, bare-identifier map receiver). The consuming position frees the deep-cloned heap element: expr_is_inline_temp_vec_heap_index now recognises the borrow shape too. Also threads the same borrow-container hoist through compile_indexed_receiver_method so `m.get(k).unwrap()[i].method()` (e.g. `.len()`) lowers instead of bailing 'requires the indexed container to be a named variable'. Verified interp==JIT==AOT and valgrind-clean (definitely/indirectly lost = 0, no double-free) across a scalar-elem value (`Vec[i64]`, the reported repro), a heap-elem value (`Vec[String]`) as a println/fn-arg/let/`[i].method()` consumer, and a nested `Vec[Vec[i64]]`, in a 60-iter loop; fresh-owned `make()[i]` still drops (no regression). Full suite green (codegen 2396, memory_sanitizer 733; clippy+fmt clean). Adds test_e2e_inline_index_map_get_unwrap_vec_value + asan_inline_index_map_get_unwrap_vec_value_no_leak. NOTE: a `<map>.get(k).unwrap()[i]` String VALUE (char-index) and a VecDeque value are out of scope (Vec value only); a genuinely non-borrow method-chain returning an OWNED Vec by value (a user method `obj.make()[i]`) remains routed only through inline_temp_vec_te's free-fn-Call arm — unchanged here.
detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while fixing B-2026-07-15-26 — inline-indexing an unwrapped map-get Vec loud-bails in codegen; binding first works. — SURFACE NOTE: codegen (index operator on a non-identifier temporary — `<expr>[i]` where <expr> is a method-call chain like `m.get(k).unwrap()`)

title: `<struct-field-map>.get(k).unwrap()` of a heap value (a `Map[_, String]`/`Map[_, Vec]` FIELD) double-frees the value buffer, both bound (`let v = h.ms.get(1).unwrap()`) AND inline (`println(h.ms.get(1).unwrap())`), against the struct's scope-exit map drop. `map.get(k)` returns `Option[ref V]` (a borrow), but the borrow-elision detectors (B-2026-07-14-15 bound registration, B-2026-07-15-26 inline cap-zero) only matched a bare-IDENTIFIER map receiver — a field-access receiver (`h.ms`/`self.ms`) fell through. A bare `Map[_, String]` LOCAL is clean; only a struct-field map crashes. REVISED from the initial 'struct-field Map drop' framing — the double-free is the field-access get().unwrap() consumer, not the field drop (a no-get struct with a `Map[_, String]` field drops clean). Interp correct; codegen-only.
investigation: 2026-07-16: initially filed as a struct-field `Map[K, heap-value]` drop double-free, but valgrind pinned the true root cause: the `world` String value (5 bytes) was freed FIRST inline in main (the `println(mv.sm.get(3).unwrap())` consumer's cap>0 free-guard) and AGAIN by `karac_map_free_with_drop_vec` (the map drop). Isolation: (a) a struct with a `Map[_, String]` field but NO get().unwrap() drops CLEAN — so it is the get/unwrap consumer, not the field drop; (b) `let v = h.ms.get(1).unwrap(); println(v)` ALSO double-frees (unlike B-26, where the bound form was clean) — so BOTH the bound and inline legs are broken for a field receiver; (c) a bare `Map[_, String]` LOCAL get().unwrap() is clean. So the get/unwrap borrow-elision detectors (`is_nonshared_heap_value_map_get_unwrap` bound, `unwrap_receiver_is_nonshared_heap_value_map_get` inline cap-zero) both require a bare `Identifier(map_var)` receiver and look up `var_elem_type_exprs[map_var]`; a field-access receiver (`h.ms`, `self.ms`) is not an Identifier, so neither fires, the unwrapped value keeps its real cap, and the consumer's free-guard double-frees the map's stored buffer.
resolution: 2026-07-16 (3a44455): fixed by a shared `map_receiver_value_type_expr` (stmts.rs) that resolves the map VALUE type for either a bare-identifier receiver (`var_elem_type_exprs`) OR a struct-field receiver (`mv.sm`/`self.sm` — from the field's declared `Map[K,V]` type via `var_type_names`+`struct_field_type_exprs`, with the owning struct's mono subst from `enum_inst_var_types` applied so a generic `Map[K,V]` field resolves to the concrete value). The B-26 inline cap-zero detector routes through it, so `<field-map>.get(k).unwrap()` produces a `{ptr,len,0}` borrow view — which fixes BOTH the inline consumer AND the bound binding (its drop skips on cap=0), leaving the map the sole owner. `map_get_unwrap_vec_value_te` (the B-2026-07-15-27 index helper) routes through it too, so `h.mv.get(k).unwrap()[i]` (previously a loud 'Index operator applied to non-array type' bail — the field-access sibling of B-27) now lowers. title: #[par_unordered] collect combine helper used get_store_size for its byte-offset GEPs and its size-keyed symbol, but Vec push/index GEPs stride by elem_ty.size_of() = ALLOC size — for a tail-padded struct element ({i64,i32}: store 12, alloc 16) every element past the first worker's chunk was memcpy'd at the wrong offset (shifted 4·chunk_index bytes), silently corrupting the collected Vec.
investigation: 2026-07-16: found by reading, confirmed by construction — the collect generalization (81377276, one day earlier) introduced get_store_size keying; all its test elements ({f64,i64}=16/16, f64=8/8, i64=8/8, {f32 x9}=36/36) have store==alloc so the suite stayed green. LLVM guarantees alloc size is a multiple of ABI alignment; store size is alloc minus tail padding, so any element type with tail padding diverges. Port-side classification: LATENT — selfhost/src/main.kara has zero #[par_unordered] uses and no kata collects padded structs; first user to collect a {i64,i32}-shaped struct in a par loop would have hit silent corruption (append path) or a corrupt final Vec (grow path).
resolution: 2026-07-16 (fix commit 70fd850a, post-rebase): switched the elem_size source to ensure_target_data().get_abi_size() (the established API elsewhere in codegen — cabi.rs, types_lowering.rs) so combine offsets, the size-keyed helper symbol, the tabulate view stride, and Vec's own GEP strides all agree on alloc size. Pinned twice: IR test asserts a {i64,i32} element emits __karac_reduce_combine_collect_b16 and NOT b12; E2E pre-seeds the accumulator so the caller-side install takes combine's append path (the byte-offset memcpy the IR pin can't validate) and verifies all 1000 elements + the seed against their index formulas.

title: lljit_prototype::lljit_gdb_registration_listener_registers_dwarf_module fails on macOS (M5 Pro, Darwin 25.5): after installing + materializing a DWARF-carrying module, the process-global __jit_debug_descriptor carries no registered entry ('the listener did not fire'). CI never catches it: the llvm-feature CI jobs run a targeted suite list that excludes lljit_prototype, and the plain `cargo test --all` job compiles without --features llvm.
investigation: 2026-07-16: fails identically at three endpoints — the collect-tabulate worktree, pristine origin/main (e62061f4), AND 73bc02a3 (the commit that last touched tests/lljit_prototype.rs, whose author shipped it green on 2026-07-12; also fails at a914475f). Same code green-then-red with no intervening commit touching the surface ⇒ environmental: most plausibly an Xcode CLT/macOS update changed how the test binary's __jit_debug_descriptor global interposes against LLVM's own copy of the GDB JIT interface symbols on Darwin (the listener may be registering into LLVM's descriptor while the test reads the test binary's). The other 18 lljit_prototype tests (materialization, lookups, execution) all pass — JIT itself is healthy; only the debug-registration OBSERVATION fails. Fails in isolation (not test-ordering). 2026-07-16 (Linux session): FIX LANDED 913ec89, entry kept OPEN pending Darwin re-verification. Two legs: (1) the test's observation now resolves __jit_debug_descriptor from the IMAGE THAT HOSTS LLVM at runtime (dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, LLVMContextCreate) -> dladdr -> dlsym that image), matching the diagnosed mechanism — the listener writes dylib-hosted LLVM's own copy of the interface globals while the link-time extern bound elsewhere; the static-LLVM configuration (Linux CI, default dev) falls back to the link-time extern (Rust test binaries export no LLVM symbols to RTLD_DEFAULT), which there IS the single unified copy — verified 19/19 on Linux, behavior identical. (2) the CI gap is closed: lljit_prototype added to the codegen-e2e job's --features llvm suite list, so the Linux leg of the GDB-registration smoke test is now enforced on every change. REMAINING (why still open): the dylib leg cannot be exercised from this Linux container (static LLVM); OWNER ACTION on the affected Mac (M5 Pro, Darwin 25.5): `cargo test --features llvm --test lljit_prototype`. If it still reds there, the next hypothesis is the dylib not exporting the descriptor at all (hidden visibility in the new toolchain's libLLVM) — in which case the dlsym probe returns null and falls back to the mis-bound extern; the follow-up would be reading the descriptor via the dylib's local symbol table or gating the assertion on descriptor-resolvability.
resolution: FIXED 8579cdac (Darwin leg) atop 913ec89 (Linux CI enrollment + descriptor-resolution helper). Darwin re-verify on the affected machine (M5 Pro, Darwin 25.5) showed 913ec89's dylib leg STILL fails: the GDB JIT descriptor is a SINGLE copy here — the link-time `extern` binding, the LLVM-hosting-image dlsym resolution, and `llvm_hosted_descriptor()` all agree on one address — so 913ec89's 'multiple descriptor copies' premise does not hold on the affected machine. Temporary instrumentation confirmed the wiring is correct (our RTDyld object-layer creator runs, `LLVMCreateGDBRegistrationListener` returns non-null, the register call succeeds), yet LLVM 18.1.8's GDBRegistrationListener does NOT populate `__jit_debug_descriptor` for JIT'd Mach-O objects on this toolchain — a best-effort debugger-integration limitation of the LLVM build, NOT a kara regression (JIT execution + DWARF emission unaffected; sibling `lljit_dwarf_debug_info_preserved_through_jit` passes). Fix: gate the strong end-to-end 'descriptor carries an entry' assertion to Linux/ELF (where LLVM populates the interface; the codegen-e2e CI leg 913ec89 added enforces it) and assert the reachable-interface check (version==1, single resolved descriptor) on macOS. Darwin now GREEN: 19/19 lljit_prototype on M5 Pro.

title: Auto-par reduction lowers a loop whose body carries plain `shared` RC traffic into a multi-threaded worker — racing non-atomic rc-inc/rc-dec across workers frees live objects (UAF reads surfacing as spurious 'integer overflow' panics + glibc heap-corruption aborts)
investigation: 2026-07-16: `while rep < K { total = total + sum(pool[rep % 8]); rep = rep + 1; }` over `pool: Vec[Option[TreeNode]]` (TreeNode plain `shared`) was recognized as a scalar Add reduction and lowered to `karac_par_reduce` (`__karac_reduce_worker_0`). The worker body retains the pool element per iteration (plain load/add/store on the rc header — `opt.chain.inc.real`), and `sum`'s owned param releases at exit; every tree-internal retain/release in `sum` is plain too. With N workers over the SAME 8 trees, lost rc updates drive counts to 0 while live: reps>=~500 abort with `free(): unaligned chunk` / `double free or corruption`, reps>=~2000 read recycled memory (garbage `n.val` -> panic 'integer overflow' at the sum line). Race triad: KARAC_PAR_WORKERS=1 always correct; multi-worker corrupt; valgrind (serialized threads) clean. Neither recognize_reductions nor the reduce.rs lowering consulted shared-ness anywhere; the explicit-boundary machinery (`src/cross_task_safe.rs`, enforced at spawn/par{}/send) was never applied to the COMPILER-CREATED task boundary. FIX: recognize_reductions declines any loop whose body contains a typed expression failing `is_cross_task_safe` — implemented as a span sweep over `TypeCheckResult.expr_types` entries inside the body block (shape-blind: a future ExprKind cannot reopen the hole), so the loop falls back to sequential codegen. Untyped analysis callers unchanged (every lowering path runs typed). `par` (atomic Arc) types remain eligible; int/Vec[scalar] reductions unaffected (par_codegen 165/165 green, incl. the 8137727 struct/float collect fan-out tests). Deliberately conservative: a body-local FRESH shared object (thread-local, technically race-free) also declines — the cost is a sequential loop, never a miscompile; re-enabling read-only shared traversal under auto-par requires the rc-silent borrowed-param convention (B-2026-07-15-21 fix direction) plus a gate relaxation that PROVES rc-silence of the emitted body. Also fixed en passant: `is_cross_task_safe`'s struct/enum expansion had no cycle guard — a recursive owned aggregate (`struct A { xs: Vec[A] }`) reachable from any boundary check recursed forever; expansion now carries a seen-set. Regression tests: typed-analysis decline/keep pair (tests/concurrency.rs), sequential-correctness E2E (tests/codegen.rs test_e2e_reduction_over_shared_pool_declined_and_correct), ASAN race regression (tests/memory_sanitizer.rs asan_reduction_over_shared_pool_no_race_uaf).

title: Storing a `ref String`/`ref Vec` borrow into a value position — `Some(s)` with `s: ref String`, or passing a declared `ref String` struct field to a `ref` param — materializes the LENDER's full {ptr,len,cap} triple, so the consumer's cap-guarded cleanup frees the borrowed buffer and the lender's own drop double-frees (AOT aborts; interp correct — silent run/build divergence)
investigation: 2026-07-16: two legs, one discipline violation. LEG 1 (`asan_option_ref_from_param`): `fn wrap(s: ref String) -> Option[ref String] { Option.Some(s) }` — build_nonshared_enum_value packs the deref'd triple (real cap) into the payload words; the match arm reconstructs `n` and its binding cleanup (`cleanup.cap > 0 -> free`) frees s's buffer; `println(s)` then reads freed memory and s's scope-exit free doubles it. Valgrind: both frees inline in main, block alloc'd by push_str. LEG 2 (`asan_borrowed_field_into_ref_param`): `Parser { source: ref String }` lowers the field as a BORROW-POINTER slot by design (design.md Feature 4 Part 3), but the ref-arg path's field intercept (B-2026-07-12-1) only recognized owned Vec/String fields (`field_ty == vec_struct_type`); a declared-`ref` field fell to the rvalue path, which deref'd the borrow into a `ref_rvalue_arg` temp and queued the cap-guarded free — the 'cap>0 guard keeps registration safe' assumption is FALSE for borrows (the temp's cap is the lender's). FIX (two scoped arms + shared helper): (1) `zero_cap_if_ref_heap_borrow` — at both enum-construction pack sites, a payload arg that is a ref-heap borrow (Identifier naming a ref/mut-ref param with triple pointee, or a field access whose DECLARED type is ref/mut-ref String/str/Vec/VecDeque) gets its cap word zeroed: the payload becomes a read-only view (same borrow-view discipline as the map get/unwrap family, B-2026-07-14-15/-26 lineage), every downstream cap-guarded free skips, the lender stays sole owner. (2) the ref-arg field intercept gains a declared-`ref`-field arm: the slot already holds the exact `ptr` ABI the callee's `ref T` param expects, so forward the stored borrow pointer directly — no temp, no cleanup. Both probes: interp==JIT==AOT, valgrind 0 errors. safety_design runtime_confirmation 54/54 (was 52+2). E2E output regression: tests/codegen.rs test_e2e_ref_borrow_stored_positions_no_double_free. ID NOTE: the fix commit's message cites B-2026-07-16-4 and the concurrency-gate commit's code comments originally cited B-2026-07-16-2 — both numbers were taken by a sibling session's entries mid-flight; the authoritative IDs are this entry and B-2026-07-16-6 (comments renumbered in the ledger commit). Residual (documented, not fixed here): `Option[ref T]` payloads still pack 3 words rather than a single borrow-pointer word — a layout follow-on, orthogonal to safety now that the view discipline holds.

title: rc-elide conditions 1-4 do not constrain where a payload PROJECTION flows: an elided fn passing `n.parent` (any projection) to a mutating callee can release the only count keeping the borrowed node alive (the elided frame holds no +1 of its own) — UAF mid-arm on up/back-pointer shared graphs; condition 5 is a priority fast-follow now that the default-ON flip (a8d47f2) has landed
investigation: 2026-07-16: found by review, not by a failing test — no current elided shape passes projections to a mutating callee (is_mirror/sum recurse only into themselves), the corpus has no elided back-pointer traversal, and no kata/test writes that shape — but since a8d47f2 flipped the elision DEFAULT-ON, the gap is no longer shielded by the env gate. Mechanism: under elision the current frame borrows its param's referent with NO own +1 (the caller's root is the shield). Conditions 1-4 permit the arm to pass any projection (`n.parent`) to an arbitrary callee; that callee, following the ordinary OWNED protocol (its own counts balance), may field-assign through the alias (`parent.left = None`), releasing the parent-field +1 — which for an interior node is the ONLY count — freeing the borrowed node while the arm still reads it. Also holds via let-aliases of projections (`let x = n.parent; mutate(x)`) since PayloadScan does not add let-bound projections to the lineage. The un-elided protocol shields this exact shape (the frame's transferred +1 keeps the node >= 1 for the call duration). FIX DIRECTION (condition 5, all cheap syntactic fail-closed checks — design in docs/spikes/rc-elide-ref-params.md § 'Flip-blocker'): 5a elidable fns contain no field/index store and no lineage-rooted method call; 5b every shared/Option[shared] param of an elidable fn is itself elided; 5c lineage projections (and their let-aliases, which must join the lineage) may be passed only at elided positions of 5-satisfying fns — the elided call web becomes hermetically read-only over shared state, so no release can occur while any borrow in the web is live. is_mirror/is_symmetric/sum all satisfy 5a-5c (the known wins survive). TIMELINE: found during the Part B (binding-pair) review in one session while a sibling session flipped default-ON (a8d47f2) with criteria 1-4 met — the two crossed mid-flight; condition 5 was not in the criteria list. Until it lands, the exposure is bounded by the shape requirement (back-pointer graph + mutation through a projection-fed callee), which no current corpus program has; KARAC_RC_ELIDE_REF_PARAMS=0 is the opt-out if a user hits it. 2026-07-16 REPRODUCED + FIXED (same session, follow-up pass): the hazard is REAL and WORSE than filed — on the default path the make/walk/detach probe (walk elidable under 1-4; arm passes n.back to detach which does m.left = None, releasing the borrowed node's only count) produced a SILENT WRONG ANSWER (printed 674712875783995725 instead of 8 — no crash) plus a valgrind invalid-read; interp and KARAC_RC_ELIDE_REF_PARAMS=0 were correct (a silent run/build divergence). FIX (2639536): condition 5 as designed, implemented as a fixed-point refinement in safe_elidable_ref_params over the condition-1-4 set — 5a no field/index-target stores and no lineage-rooted method calls or for-iterations; 5b every shared-carrying param must itself be elided; 5c lineage projections flow only to elided positions of surviving fns or nested destructures, with let-aliases of projections joining the lineage (closing the PayloadScan tracking gap). Lineage is TYPE-TRACKED (binding -> payload struct) via a shared-carrying-types fixpoint + per-(struct,field) classification, so scalar reads (n.val) stay unrestricted while handle-bearing hops stay confined; tuple/enum/dyn hops fail closed; removals cascade to callers. All known winners survive (sum, has_path_sum, is_mirror/is_symmetric cross-fn; treesum 0.383s vs 0.443s opt-out best-of-9). Verified: probe prints 8 + valgrind 0 errors under default and =0; rc_elide unit tests 11/11 (6 new); new ASAN pin asan_rc_elide_mutation_through_alias_projection_guarded; codegen 2400 / memory_sanitizer 739 / par_codegen 173 / safety_design 54 green on the default path; clippy + fmt clean.
