INTERPRETER (needed independently, and mid-fix AOT briefly fired while interp did not -- a divergence that would have been worse than the original both-silent bug): the `field_te_runs_user_drop` gate learned to check a RANGE of generic args rather than one index; `field_value_carries_user_drop` gained an Option/Result payload arm; and FOUR separate walks needed the arm because this side splits them differently than codegen does -- struct field, Vec element, the field-level map walk AND the binding-level map walk, plus the binding-level map REGISTRATION gate (`record_map_val_bodies_te`), which is the gate-before-walk shape B-2026-08-02-24 already taught: the walk was correct and simply never armed. All routed through `run_discarded_value_user_drops`, the value-driven recursion this side already used for these built-ins. UNMASKED, NOT INTRODUCED -- filed as B-2026-08-03-3: two positions (a `Result[Res, i64]` struct field, and a tuple-held `Option[Res]`) go vg-clean -> vg=99 with this fix. Verified latent rather than regressed with `valgrind --trace-malloc=yes` on the stashed build: the pre-fix binaries allocated the payload buffer ZERO times, LLVM having elided a heap value nothing ever read. Making the body read `self.name` is what brings the allocation to life and exposes a free that was always missing. Same discriminator, same conclusion as B-2026-08-02-19. The full suite is green (6867/0) with those leaks present, so nothing existing depended on the silence. Pins (all three STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin optres_payload_bodies_in_nested_positions, covering all four nested positions plus a `None` control that must stay silent; asan optres_payload_nested_positions_clean, deliberately scoped to the three positions whose memory was already correct, so it guards the new walks without baking in the B-2026-08-03-3 leaks.

title: a container element destroyed WITHOUT being bound never runs its Drop body — clear, truncate, discarded remove/swap_remove/pop, and whole-container reassign; two of those also LEAK, and two more disagree between backends
detail: SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (the original filing understated this badly: it named only clear/truncate, claimed 'both backends agree' throughout, and missed the leaks entirely). A follow-up sweep over the whole removal surface shows one invariant behind all of it -- an element destroyed with NO BINDING to receive it never runs its Drop body -- and three distinct defect classes within that. Probes b211/k*, b211/m*, one `Res { id, name: String }` element unless noted.  CLASS 1, body silent, memory clean, both backends: `v.clear()` with 2 elements -> 0 fires (k1); `m.clear()` -> 0 (k2); `v.truncate(1)` from 2 -> the REMOVED element is silent while the survivor's body still fires at scope exit, so the count looks plausible and is wrong (k3/m6); `v = w` whole-container reassign -> the DISPLACED old element is silent, only the new one fires at scope exit (m7).  CLASS 2, body silent AND LEAKS, both backends: a DISCARDED `v.remove(0);` (m1, vg=99) and `v.swap_remove(0);` (m3, vg=99). Binding the result fixes both -- `let r = v.remove(0);` fires once and is vg-clean (m2) -- which localizes it to the discard position rather than the removal itself.  CLASS 3, RUN-VS-BUILD DIVERGENCE: a discarded `v.pop();` (m4) and `m.remove(5);` (m5) fire correctly under AOT and are SILENT under the interpreter. This class was entirely absent from the original filing, which asserted the opposite ('both backends agree'); it is the shipping-path-correct direction, unlike B-2026-08-02-25.  CONTRAST that still holds: `let p = v.pop();` and `let g = m.remove(k);` -- any BOUND removal -- are correct on both backends, so the single-element machinery has the right ownership wiring and it is specifically the unbound/bulk positions that lack it. SEVERITY raised low->high: `clear()` on a Vec of connection handles silently skips every close, class 2 is a real leak on the shipping path, and class 3 is a run/build split. SOURCE NOTE: class 1 found by the b211 fire-count sweep; classes 2 and 3 only surfaced when the removal surface was enumerated systematically against BOUND controls -- the bound/unbound contrast is what made the single root cause visible. `Set.clear()` does not exist yet (typecheck: no method 'clear' on type 'Set'), so that arm is untested rather than passing.
fix: CLASS 3 FIXED (b213), row stays OPEN for classes 1 and 2. The interpreter's bare-statement discard arm (`StmtKind::Expr`'s MethodCall branch) only ever admitted USER methods, while the `let _ = v.pop();` form went through `discard_rhs_produces_owned_value`, whose method list already covers the builtin container removals -- so the two DISCARD STATEMENT SHAPES disagreed with each other, and against codegen, which fires for both. The bare arm now runs the same walker on the same method list. DELIBERATELY GATED to an Option/Result-shaped result, which is exactly codegen's current reach: its discard registrar is the optres payload walker and the only receiver it resolves a type for is Map-shaped, so `v.pop()` and `m.remove(k)` are covered there while `v.remove(i)` and `v.swap_remove(i)` (bare `T`) are not. The first attempt used the unrestricted list and FLIPPED those two from both-silent to interpreter-fires/AOT-silent -- strictly worse, since AOT also leaks them. Caught by re-running the probe matrix before committing; the gate is what keeps this a pure divergence-removal. GENERALIZABLE: when closing a run-vs-build split by moving one backend, check every shape the change admits, not just the reported one -- a fix that widens a gate can convert a shared gap into a divergence, which is the worse failure mode. STILL OPEN: class 1 (clear / truncate / whole-container reassign -- body silent, memory clean, both backends) and class 2 (discarded `v.remove(i)` / `v.swap_remove(i)` -- body silent AND leaking, both backends). Class 2 needs codegen's discard registrar to resolve a Vec receiver's element type and to own the removed element's memory, which is the substantive remaining work. Pin: interp `bare_statement_container_removal_discard_fires` (STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix), carrying the bound-removal control alongside the two fixed shapes. CLEAR FIXED (b213b), covering the `clear()` half of class 1 on both backends. Both arms turned out to do all the MEMORY work and none of the body work, which is exactly why the shapes were vg-clean and silent: codegen's `Vec.clear` went straight to `emit_vec_drop_fn` (drain + free) and its `Map.clear` to the shared rc-dec walks plus the per-value drop fn, while the interpreter's arms called Rust's `Vec::clear` / replaced the table with an empty one -- operations that reclaim storage and know nothing about Kara destructors. Each now runs the SAME element/value bodies walker the binding-death path uses, BEFORE the memory work on the codegen side (the walker frees nothing, so it cannot disturb the drop, and running it first is what lets a body read the fields it prints) and after the container is emptied on the interpreter side (so no read guard is live while a body runs, in case a body touches the container). Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin container_clear_runs_element_drop_bodies, carrying a two-element Vec (order matters), a Map, and a clear-then-reuse control that checks the buffer is still usable and the replacement element still fires at scope exit. CLASS 1 REMAINDER, still open: `truncate(n)` (the REMOVED tail is silent while the survivors still fire, so a naive whole-container walker would be wrong here -- truncate needs a RANGED walk over [n, len), which is why it was not folded into this change) and whole-container reassign `v = w` (the displaced old container's elements). Class 2 (discarded Vec remove/swap_remove: silent AND leaking) is untouched and remains the substantive work. CLASS 2 FIXED (b214). A discarded `v.remove(i);` / `v.swap_remove(i);` hands the element back BY VALUE with nothing to receive it, and the discard battery could not tell what it was holding: its method arm resolves a return type through `fn_return_type_names`, keyed `Type.method`, and BUILTINS have no entry there (they are not declared impl methods). So the registration was skipped entirely -- no body, no free. The arm now falls back to the receiver's recorded element TypeExpr (`var_elem_type_exprs`), the same side-table the container's own drop machinery keys on, for a Vec/VecDeque receiver and the two by-value removals. `pop` is deliberately NOT in that fallback: it returns `Option[T]`, which the optres arm of the same battery already owns. Once codegen could own the element, the interpreter's bare-statement gate was widened to match (and `swap_remove` added to both its method lists, having been absent from each). SEQUENCING WAS THE POINT: codegen first, interpreter second. The class-3 pass had already shown that widening the interpreter alone converts a shared gap into a divergence -- worse, here, because AOT was also leaking -- so the interpreter arm stayed narrow until the backend that ships could own the value. Verified by re-running the full removal matrix after EACH half, not just at the end. Pins (all three STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin discarded_vec_removal_fires_and_frees, carrying the always-correct BOUND control and a two-element `survivor` case that checks only the REMOVED element fires early while the one left behind still fires at scope exit; asan discarded_vec_removal_no_leak for the leak half. CLASS 1 REMAINDER, the only part of this row still open: `truncate(n)` (needs a RANGED walk over [n, len) -- its survivors correctly fire already, so the whole-container walker used for `clear` would double-fire them) and whole-container reassign `v = w` (the displaced old container's elements). CLASS 1 COMPLETED (b215) — the row is now CLOSED, all three classes fixed. The two remaining positions had the same memory-yes/bodies-no split as `clear`, but needed different walks, and getting that distinction right is the substance: `truncate(n)` required a RANGED walk. Its existing loop already stepped [n, len) freeing each removed element, and it ran no body -- so the removed tail lost its destructors while the SURVIVORS still fired at binding death, a fire count that looks plausible and is wrong. The whole-container walker used for `clear` is NOT usable here: it would re-fire the survivors. The per-slot bodies dispatcher now runs inside that same [n, len) loop, ahead of each free. Whole-container reassign `v = w` DOES displace every old element, so there the whole-container walker is correct; it now runs before the reassign path's per-element release and buffer free. The interpreter needed the mirror-image edits: a tail snapshot in `truncate`, and a `Value::Array` arm in the displaced-value match, which previously handled only Struct and EnumVariant. REFACTOR: `emit_tuple_elem_bodies_at` was renamed `emit_slot_drop_bodies_at` and made pub(super). It was written for tuple elements and named for them, but its contract -- run the bodies reachable from ONE SLOT of a given type -- was never tuple-specific, and truncate needed exactly that per-slot dispatch. Pins (both STASH-PROVEN FAILED pre-fix): e2e + interp twin truncate_and_reassign_run_displaced_drop_bodies, whose truncate case is what pins the RANGE -- the removed tail fires at the truncate, the survivor fires at binding death, neither twice -- plus a truncate(0) case and the reassign case.

title: a tuple-held Option[Struct] / Result[Struct, E] payload is never freed in ANY position, and a `let x = t.N` move-out fires the source element's Drop body twice -- tuple legs FIXED, the Result STRUCT FIELD leg still open
detail:
TWO ORIGINAL LEGS, filed together because -1 unmasked both at once. (A) TUPLE-HELD Option/Result -- FIXED (c775e70). (B) `Result[Res, i64]` STRUCT FIELD (`struct H { r: Result[Res, i64] }`, probe b211/o2) -- STILL OPEN. Both were vg-clean before B-2026-08-03-1 only because nothing ever READ the payload, so LLVM elided the allocation entirely -- `valgrind --trace-malloc=yes` on the pre-fix binaries counts ZERO allocations of the buffer and one after. Arming the payload's Drop body (which reads `self.name`) makes the allocation live and the missing free observable. Same discriminator and conclusion as B-2026-08-02-19. LEG A ROOT CAUSE: `emit_tuple_elem_drops` had a hard `"Option" | "Result" => {}` no-op, and every admit gate above it routes through `type_expr_has_drop_heap`, which hardcodes those two heads as heapless (load-bearing, must not change). So a tuple whose only heap hung off an Option/Result payload looked heapless at every gate and got NO drop at all -- in a binding, a by-value param, a returned tuple, a `Vec[(Option[Res], i64)]` element, and a nested tuple. The direct `Vec[Option[Res]]` control was clean throughout, which is exactly what kept the tuple hole invisible. LEG A FIX: `tuple_elem_optres_drop_ok` restates the element shapes `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr` admits as a pure `&self` gate (Option[shared] excluded -- rc machinery owns it, matching the cap-zero dual's existing arm); `emit_tuple_elem_drops` routes an admitted element to the tag-guarded `karac_drop_Option_

` / `karac_drop_Result__`; `zero_tuple_elem_cap_at` gains the matching move-out neutralizer (Option -> tag to None, Result -> payload area zeroed) and the two must stay in lockstep or a moved tuple double-frees; `synthesize_tuple_drop_fn_te` and `vec_elem_agg_drop_for_type_expr`'s tuple arm OR the new admit into their heapless bail. THIRD BUG FOUND WHILE FIXING (also fixed here, no separate row): `let x = t.N` moves ONE tuple element out. Cap-zeroing already neutralized the source's MEMORY drop but its `__karac_dropelems_tuple_*` walk stayed fully armed and fired that element's body a SECOND time over the zeroed slot -- `drop 1 ` with an empty name under AOT, a full duplicate under the interpreter. Present with NO Option involved (`let t = (Res{..}, Res{..}); let x = t.0;`), so it predates -1 entirely; the struct-FIELD sibling `let x = s.r` was correct all along. Fixed by re-emitting the walker with only that index masked (`disarm_tuple_elem_bodies_at` + `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn_skipping`), so sibling elements still fire; the interpreter twin is a per-`(binding, index)` record consulted by the tuple walk. LESSON, third instance this week: closing a leak by ARMING a new free turns every position that already consumes that value into a double-free candidate. Enumerate the consumers before landing -- here `let x = t.N` (the cap-zero dual) and `match t.N { Ok(v) => .. }` (a new `suppress_tuple_elem_optres_payload_cleanup`, the tuple-element sibling of the `inline_{option,result}_payload_vars` match suppressors) each needed their own neutralizer, and the second was found only by the full ASAN suite going RED. LEG B (still open) ROOT CAUSE, read at fix time for -1: the `OptionInline` field classifier admits an Option field whose payload is a struct/enum via `option_payload_struct_or_enum_drop_ok`, but the sibling Result arm requires `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` -- DIRECT String/Vec halves only -- so a struct Ok-payload falls through and no field drop is registered. The asymmetry looks deliberate: the Option admit is paired with `param_own`'s `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, and Result has only `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` (halves, no struct payload). Freeing a Result struct payload in the field drop WITHOUT first giving the entry copy its struct-payload counterpart risks double-freeing a callee-shared buffer, so it needs the copy side and the drop side landed together, with the caller-retains vs entry-copy reasoning re-derived for Result. LEG B ATTEMPT 1 (2026-08-03, NOT LANDED -- reverted). The row's stated precondition turned out to be NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the main result to carry forward. Built exactly what the row prescribed: `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` (at least one side owns heap; every heap-owning side is a non-shared struct/enum, kept DISJOINT from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` so each class keeps one copy helper), the entry-copy twin `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` (tag dispatch, then the boxed-or-inline payload copy factored out of the Option helper), wired into BOTH `field_copy_supported`'s Result arm and the `OptionInline` drop classifier. Result: the LOCAL-BINDING leak closes (probe b215/t7 vg=99 -> 0, both backends agreeing) but the BY-VALUE PARAM case DOUBLE-FREES (`fn take(h: H) -> i64 { h.t }`, probe b215/r2: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`) and the by-value-param-plus-consuming-match case SIGSEGVs (probe b215/r7). Diagnostic state at revert: the copy dispatch IS reached and its gate IS true (confirmed by instrumenting the dispatch), so the copy is emitted -- the fault is NOT a missing copy. The remaining suspects are (i) the boxed-vs-inline width decision disagreeing between the pack site (`coerce_to_payload_words`), the copy, and `emit_result_drop_fn`, and (ii) the second-order effect of the admit: making the Result field copyable flips the WHOLE struct `H` from caller-retains to callee-owned, which changes ownership for every field and every call site at once -- so the next attempt should isolate which of those two it is before rebuilding the mechanism. MEASURED BASELINE for the whole Result-struct-field family (current main, all `struct H { r: Result[Res, i64], t: i64 }` unless noted): local binding LEAKS (t7); by-value param LEAKS (r2); returned from a fn LEAKS (r3); `let x = h.r` move-out LEAKS **and DOUBLE-FIRES the body on BOTH backends** (r4 -- the Result-field sibling of the tuple-element move-out double-fire fixed in c775e70, and the one shape here that is a wrong-OUTPUT bug rather than a pure leak); `Result[Res, Bad]` with struct on BOTH sides runs NO body at all on either backend and is vg=0 (r5); `Result[Res, String]` mixed likewise (r6); by-value param + consuming `match h.r` prints `drop 7 ggggggg1` then a garbage `drop 7 drop 7 ` under AOT while `karac run` prints one correct fire -- a run-vs-build divergence on top of the leak (r7). Probes are in the b215 scratch set. COUPLING NOTE (2026-08-03, after B-2026-08-03-8 closed): that row's warning is now discharged in one direction. `let x = h.r` on a Result struct field no longer double-fires the body -- it fires once, on both backends -- so the shape is a PURE leak again, exactly like the other three in this row's baseline. The move-out neutralizers (tag/payload zero + the masked bodies walk) are in place, which means arming this row's field free will NOT reintroduce the SEGV that -8's Option leg had: the disarm the crash needed already exists for Result too. LEG B, SUSPECT (i) RULED OUT (2026-08-03, probes b215/p1-p3, no code change needed). The Option analogue of the failing shape is CLEAN: `struct Hopt { o: Option[Res], t: i64 }` -- `Res` being 4 words, so the payload is heap-BOXED exactly like the Result case -- through the identical by-value param `fn take(h: Hopt) -> i64 { h.t }` prints one body and reads vg=0 on both backends, as does the returned-from-a-fn variant. So a boxed payload DOES survive the callee-owned entry copy today, and neither `boxed-vs-inline width disagreement` nor `the callee-owned flip is inherently unsound` explains leg B's double-free. The next attempt should assume a SLIP in the new Result copy helper (most likely the tag dispatch or the payload GEP) and diff it against `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, which is known-good on this exact shape. Caveat carried from the same probe run: the INLINE-payload Option field is NOT clean -- it triple-fires its body under AOT -- filed separately as B-2026-08-03-10, so 'the Option pairing is sound' holds for the boxed path only. LEG B FIXED (2026-08-03, ATTEMPT 2). The row's stated precondition was right and attempt 1's mechanism was right; what killed attempt 1 was a single constant. The `Result` payload AREA is FIVE words (`declarations.rs`'s `result_payload_words = 5`, the width `coerce_to_payload_words` packs at and `emit_result_drop_fn` boxes beyond) while the `Option` area is THREE. Attempt 1 factored its payload copy out of `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place` and carried that helper's `payload_words > 3` boxing test with it, so the canonical 4-word `Res { id: i64, name: String }` -- which a `Result` stores INLINE and an `Option` stores BOXED -- was copied as if boxed: word 1, actually `id`, was read as a box pointer. That is suspect (i) after all. The probe that 'ruled it out' compared against the Option analogue, which boxes the SAME struct because of the SAME area difference, so it confirmed only that a boxed payload survives -- it never exercised the inline path the Result case actually takes. LESSON: when porting a helper between the Option and Result families, the boxing threshold is NOT shared; an analogue probe that silently crosses the boxed/inline boundary proves nothing about the shape under test. THE FIX IS FOUR PIECES, and three of them are the arming-exposes-consumers pattern this row already records. (1) ADMIT + COPY: `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` (control_flow_match.rs) -- structurally DISJOINT from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` (that one needs a direct String/Vec heap half and rejects a struct/enum one; this one is the mirror image), so each class keeps exactly one copy helper -- plus `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` (param_own.rs), a per-half tag-dispatched copy boxing at `> 5` in lockstep with `emit_result_drop_fn`, wired into `field_copy_supported`'s Result arm (via `result_payload_struct_enum_copyable`), `deep_copy_one_aggregate_field`'s Result arm, and the `OptionInline` drop classifier. That alone fixed the local binding, the by-value param and the returned-from-a-fn shapes. (2) MOVE-OUT: `let x = h.r` then leaked -- the source is correctly zeroed but `place_optres_field_move_info_ex`'s Result arm still admitted only the direct-vecstr class, so the leaf registered nothing. Widened it (and the two `stmts.rs` destructure sites), which is the same pairing rule the Option arm's comment already states: the source zero must fire precisely when the struct drop would free the field. (3) CONSUMING MATCH: `match h.r { Ok(x) => .. }` printed a spurious `drop 0 ` after the binding's correct fire, because `zero_result_payload_area` is NOT the dual of `zero_option_field_tag_at` -- it zeroes the payload WORDS and leaves the TAG selecting the live arm. Every memory consumer tolerates that (their frees are cap-guarded), but `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn`'s tag SWITCH does not: it still picked the Ok case and ran the payload's body over the zeroed slot. New `invalidate_result_tag_at` stores -1 so the switch takes its default, exactly like `None`. (4) OWNED-PARAM MATCH: `match h.r` inside `fn take(h: H)` fired the callee's body ON TOP OF the caller's, because `scrutinee_is_owned_param_binding` -- the B-2026-08-01-13 gate that routes a payload bound out of a by-value param's entry copy to a memory-only registration -- matched only a BARE Identifier. A `p.field` scrutinee binds out of the same entry copy, so it carries the same caller-retains body ownership; the test now walks FieldAccess / TupleIndex chains to their root. This one hid behind the area difference too: the Option twin never reached the registration at all (4 words > the 3-word area means BOXED, which fails the inline-payload gate), so the family looked correct until the Result class -- where the same payload is inline -- got a body to fire. RESIDUAL, split out as its own row: a MIXED `Result[, String]` FIELD is admitted by NEITHER gate -- the vecstr gate rejects the struct half, the new gate rejects the String half -- so its STRUCT half registers no field free and leaks (probes b215/u1, u2: 5 bytes definitely lost on the Ok side; the String half IS freed by the existing overlay route, so the gap is the struct payload alone). Both the field drop (`emit_result_drop_fn`) and the binding cleanup (`track_inline_result_payload_var` via `result_inline_payload_struct_drops`) already dispatch PER HALF across the two representations, so only the admit gate and the entry copy are missing. Filed separately rather than widened in here, to keep this row's two-disjoint-classes invariant -- the thing that makes copy-depth == free-depth checkable by inspection -- intact while it is verified. MEASURED AFTER (all `SAME` on AOT vs `karac run --interp`, all vg=0, was the baseline table above): t7 local binding, r2 by-value param, r3 returned-from-fn, r4 `let x = h.r` move-out, r5 struct-on-both-sides, r6 mixed halves, r7 param + consuming match, plus s10 the `Result[String,i64]` control, s11/s13/s15/s16 the four Option twins, s12/s14/s17 the marker variants that localize which side fires.
fix: Leg A + the move-out double-fire: c775e70 (src/codegen/synth_drop.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/runtime.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs, src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs, src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/functions.rs, src/interpreter.rs, src/interpreter/eval_stmt.rs; pins test_e2e_tuple_held_optres_payload_freed_and_dropped, test_e2e_tuple_elem_move_out_single_body_fire, test_tuple_held_optres_payload_bodies_fire, test_tuple_elem_move_out_single_body_fire, asan_tuple_held_optres_payload_freed). Leg B: 8cfe5be (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/param_own.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs, src/codegen/synth_drop.rs; pins test_e2e_result_struct_payload_field_freed_and_single_body (stash-proven RED -- pre-fix the local-match position prints a spurious `drop 5 drop 5` and the param-match position fires twice), asan_result_struct_payload_field_freed (stash-proven RED with a heap-use-after-free), and the interpreter ORACLE twin test_result_struct_payload_field_freed_and_single_body, which is GREEN under the stash by construction -- the interpreter was correct on all seven positions throughout, which is what makes it the oracle).

title: mis-shaped handler `Response` panics the HTTP serve shim instead of diagnosing
fix: FIXED 7068f8c. `require_http_handler_response_shape` (src/codegen/http.rs) validates the handler's LLVM return type — struct, >=2 fields, field 1 itself a struct (the String aggregate) — at all four `emit_http_handler_shim` call sites in src/codegen/assoc_call.rs, returning a structured diagnostic that states the required shape instead of letting the shim's `build_extract_value(.., 1, ..).unwrap()` panic. Regression test `misshaped_handler_response_is_a_diagnostic_not_a_panic` in tests/http_client_codegen.rs asserts both the diagnostic text and the absence of a panic; examples/shortener still builds, confirming the legitimate user-declared-`Response` pattern is undisturbed.
tracker: src/codegen/http.rs (`emit_http_handler_shim` field-1 extraction; `require_http_handler_response_shape`) and the four shim call sites in src/codegen/assoc_call.rs. Sibling hardening in the same commit: `require_struct_value` replaces 7 panicking `into_struct_value()` coercions on the regex path in src/codegen/method_call.rs.

title: Displacing an Option[T] binding emits a SPURIOUS extra user Drop body over a stale slot, printing a garbage field value — pre-existing, independent of B-2026-08-02-25's fix
detail: Found while writing B-2026-08-02-25's regression test. REPRO (AOT only; the interpreter is correct):  struct T { t: i64, name: String }  impl Drop for T { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"d{self.t}"); } }  fn mk(t: i64) -> T { return T { t: t, name: "payload-string-data" }; }  fn main() { let mut p: Option[T] = Some(mk(2)); p = Some(mk(3)); println("b"); }  interpreter prints `d2 d3 b`; `karac build` prints `d2 d3 d94098919617184 b` — a THIRD body fire whose `self.t` is an uninitialized/stale word, so the value differs run to run (it is an address). PRE-EXISTING: at the B-2026-08-02-25 baseline (before the displacement leg landed) the same program printed `d3 d<garbage> b` — the spurious fire was already there and the fix only restored the missing `d2`. Reading a stale slot as a struct and calling a user Drop body over it is a use-after-free in waiting: here `T.name` is a rodata literal so nothing is freed, but a heap field would be freed through a garbage pointer. SENSITIVE TO SHAPE, which is why it was not caught earlier: the same displacement written with a constructor that PRINTS before returning (`fn new_tracked(tag, name) -> Tracked { println(..); return Tracked { .. }; }`) is clean, and so is the `o = None` direction; the failing form is a constructor whose body is a bare `return <struct literal>;`. ASan+LSan are silent on it (exit 0, no report) — the extra fire touches no freed pointer in this repro. Regression test for -25 is pinned to the clean shape so it asserts that fix and not this bug's behaviour. ROOT CAUSE + FIX: not the displacement path at all — a NAME COLLISION. A generic enum's variant payload TypeExpr is the parameter itself, so `Option`'s payload reads as the type named `T`; `emit_enum_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn` resolved that against `struct_types`, found the USER's `struct T`, and emitted `__karac_dropelems_enum_Option` alongside the real `__karac_dropelems_opt_T`. Two walkers ran on the same slot (visible in the IR for `let p: Option[T] = Some(mk(2));` alone — no displacement needed), the second over the ERASED layout's word offsets, hence the garbage tag. Renaming the struct to `Q` was the bisect. Fixed by skipping payloads whose head name is one of the enum's own generic parameters, via the pre-existing `enum_generic_param_names` (widened to pub(super)) — general across Option/Result/user generic enums, not an Option special case. Regression: codegen.rs::e2e_struct_named_like_enum_generic_param_gets_no_phantom_drop_walker. Suites green: codegen 2763, memory_sanitizer 913, interpreter 1428, par_codegen 224. Related to but distinct from B-2026-08-02-13 (stdlib/user flat namespace): that is type-name shadowing, this is a generic PARAMETER name shadowed by a user type.

title: `match t.N { Ok(v) => .. }` on a tuple-element scrutinee defers the payload's Drop body to SCOPE EXIT under karac run while AOT fires it at the arm's end
detail: `let t: (Result[Res, i64], i64) = (Result.Ok(Res { .. }), 4); match t.0 { Result.Ok(r) => { println(r.id) } Result.Err(e) => { println(e) } } println(t.1);` prints `drop ..` BEFORE `4` under `karac build` (the arm's end, NLL-correct) and AFTER it under `karac run --interp` (scope exit) -- probe b215/m3. vg=0 on both, so it is a body-TIMING divergence, not a leak. CAUSE: the interpreter does not treat `match t.N` as consuming the element -- it matches on a copied value -- so the tuple's own element walk still owns the body and runs it at the binding's death. Codegen retracts it there via `suppress_tuple_elem_optres_payload_cleanup` (added in c775e70, where it was REQUIRED: without it the consuming arm and the tuple's newly-armed element drop both freed the payload, which the ASAN suite caught as a double-free). The interpreter needs the twin record -- most likely an entry in `moved_out_tuple_elem_bodies`, the per-`(binding, index)` set that same commit added for the `let x = t.N` position. STRICTLY BETTER THAN BEFORE, for the record: pre-c775e70 this shape DOUBLE-fired under AOT (once at the arm's end, once at scope exit over the zeroed payload, printing `drop 3 drop ` with a garbage name) and leaked. It is now a single correctly-valued fire on each backend, at different times. NOT THIS ROW: the closely-related `match o { Option.Some(r) => .. }` on a PLAIN binding, where AOT runs no body at all, is B-2026-08-02-25 repro (3) and stays there -- see the cross-ref addendum on that row for the Option-vs-Result discriminator found alongside this one.  FIXED. TWO halves, and the first alone was a REGRESSION -- worth recording, because the intuitive one-line fix is wrong. (a) `disarm_moved_out_enum_payload` gains a TupleIndex arm that records the element move in `moved_out_tuple_elem_bodies` (the per-`(binding, index)` set B-2026-08-03-3 added), so the tuple's element walk skips it. Landing ONLY that made the body vanish entirely on the interpreter -- source disarmed, destination never armed -- which is strictly worse than the mistimed fire it replaced. (b) `scrutinee_expr_is_consuming` therefore also admits a TupleIndex place, so the ARM BINDING takes the body over. That predicate's doc says projections are deliberately non-consuming; the tuple-element place is the one projection that now IS, precisely because (a) retracts its owner's walk. Restricted to an identifier root (a deeper projection has no such disarm and stays non-consuming) and to a non-owned-param root, matching the Identifier arm's caller-retains carve-out. SIDE EFFECT, and a useful one: the sibling shape `match t.0 { Option.Some(r) => .. }` now fires the body at the ARM under `karac run` instead of at scope exit, which makes it identical in profile to the PLAIN-BINDING repro (3) on B-2026-08-02-25 (interp fires at the arm, AOT silent) rather than a distinct shape. One fewer variant for whoever fixes that row.
fix: src/interpreter/pattern_match.rs (the TupleIndex arms of `disarm_moved_out_enum_payload` and `scrutinee_expr_is_consuming`); pin interpreter.rs::test_tuple_elem_match_scrutinee_body_fires_at_arm_end, stash-proven RED. Suite 12891/0; 22-shape probe matrix unchanged elsewhere.

title: a struct field holding a tuple, and a Map value holding a tuple, run NO Drop body for the tuple's elements on EITHER backend
detail: The two tuple positions B-2026-08-03-3's fix did not reach. Both-backends-silent (a leak class, not a divergence), and each needs a different REGISTRATION site rather than the shared walk -3 widened. (1) STRUCT FIELD HOLDING A TUPLE: `struct W { p: (Option[Res], i64) }` -- silent on both (probe b215/u3). The struct's field-bodies walker (`emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn` / `user_drop_field_indices_mono`, and the interpreter's `field_te_runs_user_drop`) needs the same nested-tuple recursion `elem_te_runs_user_drop` just got in c775e70. (2) MAP VALUE HOLDING A TUPLE: `Map[i64, (Option[Res], i64)]` -- silent on both (probe b215/u6). Same shape one container level out, in the map-value walker. Both are the peers of the `Vec[(Option[Res], i64)]` ELEMENT case that -3 DID fix, so the widening is known-good and just has to be applied at two more walkers. Both probes are vg=0 today for the latent reason -3 documents at length: nothing reads the payload, so LLVM elides the allocation -- confirm with `valgrind --trace-malloc=yes` against a stashed build before calling either one clean. NOT THIS ROW: the third silent position found in the same sweep, `let (a, b) = t` destructuring a tuple with a Drop element, is already tracked as cross-ref (c) on B-2026-08-02-25.  FIXED. GATE side (why the emitters never got the chance): every selector read the tuple's element HEAD NAMES only. `tuple_field_elem_heads` now sees one further container level inside each element (Vec elem, Map/Set value, Option/Result payload, nested tuple), which fixes both the struct-field gate `type_runs_user_drop` and the index selector `user_drop_field_indices_mono` in one place; the interpreter's `field_te_runs_user_drop` recurses through itself for the same effect. WALK side: `emit_map_val_user_drop_bodies_fn` gains a tuple-valued-V arm (the per-value blob IS the tuple, so the element walker reads it directly, exactly as the Vec and Option/Result arms do) placed ahead of the `Path` destructure a tuple TE fails outright; the interpreter now routes every tuple-as-content position -- Vec element, Map/Set value at the binding level, Map/Set value through a struct field -- through one shared `run_tuple_item_user_drops`. MEMORY: the struct-field leg also LEAKED, exactly as this row predicted. `FieldDrop::NestedTuple`'s classifier shares `type_expr_has_drop_heap`'s Option/Result blind spot, so the field registered no memory drop either; it now ORs in the same `tuple_elem_needs_deep_drop` admit the tuple let-site uses. The vg=0 caveat this row warned about held: both probes read clean before the bodies fired and vg=99 the moment they did.
fix: 08c12068 (src/codegen/synth_drop.rs, src/interpreter/pattern_match.rs, src/interpreter/eval_stmt.rs; pins test_e2e_struct_field_and_map_value_tuple_run_element_drop, test_struct_field_and_map_value_tuple_run_element_drop, asan_struct_field_tuple_optres_payload_freed -- all three stash-proven RED). 22-shape probe matrix all SAME across backends and vg=0 except the rows this does not claim; suite 12891/0.

title: `let x = h.f` moving an Option / Result / Vec FIELD out of a struct never disarms the field's Drop machinery — SEGV for an Option[Struct] field, a double-fired body for all three; the plain-struct-field sibling was correct
detail: One family, three broken members, all on current main and all PREDATING the b215 session (verified by rebuilding src/ at 9a5ce03 and re-running each probe). The struct-FIELD analogue of the tuple-ELEMENT move-out bug fixed in c775e70, and it wants the same two-part treatment there: cap-zero/tag-zero the source field's MEMORY, and mask that field out of the source's BODIES walk. (1) SEGV -- `struct H4 { o: Option[Res], t: i64 }; let h = H4 { o: Option.Some(Res { .. }), t: 2 }; let x = h.o;` aborts with a use-after-free then an invalid free under valgrind, exit 139, no output at all (probe b215/s1). `Res` is 4 words so the payload is BOXED; both `x` and `h`'s `OptionInline` field drop free the same box. Byte-for-byte the signature u1 had before c775e70 -- read 24 bytes into a freed 32-byte block, then free the 3-byte String buffer twice. (2) `struct H { r: Result[Res, i64], t: i64 }; let x = h.r;` DOUBLE-FIRES the Drop body on BOTH backends (`drop 3 cccc1` twice) and leaks (probe b215/r4). It does not crash only because the Result field registers no memory drop at all -- that missing free is B-2026-08-03-3 leg B, so FIXING that row without fixing this one converts r4 from a leak into s1's crash. The two are coupled and should land together. (3) `struct H6 { v: Vec[Res], t: i64 }; let x = h.v;` DOUBLE-FIRES the body on both backends, vg=0 (probe b215/s3) -- the buffer ownership transfers correctly, only the bodies walk stays armed. CONTROL, correct throughout: a plain struct field, `struct H5 { r: Res, t: i64 }; let x = h.r;` -- one fire, vg=0 (probe b215/s2). So the disarm exists for a direct struct field and is missing for the three CONTAINER field kinds. WHERE TO LOOK: `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal` / `suppress_place_field_struct_move_source` are the memory-side suppressors for this position; whatever they do for a direct struct field they do not do for Option (tag to None), Result (payload area zero), or Vec (cap+len zero, already present for the buffer but not the bodies). The BODIES half has no equivalent at all: `emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn` is memoized per struct, so masking one field needs the skip-set treatment `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn_skipping` got, plus a per-`(binding, field)` record on the interpreter side mirroring `moved_out_tuple_elem_bodies`.  MEMORY HALF FIXED. `suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal`'s nested-aggregate arm fell through to the generic enum arm for an `Option`/`Result` field, and `zero_enum_payload_caps` is a NO-OP for those two by construction (they carry no static `EnumDropKind`). Added the explicit arms -- the same two neutralizers `zero_struct_move_caps_mono` has applied on a WHOLE-struct move since B-2026-07-03-28 (Option -> tag to `None`, Result -> payload area zeroed). Probe s1 goes 139/vg=99 -> exit 0/vg=0 with AOT printing the body exactly once. Severity dropped high -> medium with the crash gone. BODIES HALF STILL OPEN, and the snag is recorded so the next attempt does not re-discover it: the obvious mirror of the tuple fix does NOT work. `disarm_tuple_elem_bodies_at` retracts via `suppress_container_elem_bodies_for_var`, whose matcher `is_container_elem_bodies_fn` tests for a `__karac_dropelems_` PREFIX -- but a struct's field-bodies action is registered under `__karac_dropbodies_only_<S>` (which wraps the struct's own body AND `__karac_dropbodies_<S>`), so the retraction matches nothing and a naive re-register ADDS an action rather than replacing one. A working fix needs a retraction keyed to the `__karac_dropbodies` family and a masked re-registration that reproduces the `_only_` wrapper's own-body call. The skip-set walker itself is the easy part -- `emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn_skipping` was written and compiles cleanly, keyed on the surviving index list exactly like `emit_tuple_elem_user_drop_bodies_fn_skipping`; it was reverted with the rest rather than left half-wired. CURRENT OBSERVED STATE after the memory fix: s1 AOT correct / interp still doubles (a parity DIFF, but s1 was already DIFF when AOT crashed); s3 (Vec field) unchanged, doubles on both; r4 (Result field) AOT now prints `drop 3 cccc1` then a garbage `drop 0 ` -- the second fire reads the zeroed slot instead of duplicating, which is neither better nor worse and goes away with the bodies half.  BODIES HALF FIXED, and the snag recorded above was the whole difficulty. Its own prefix-keyed pair `is_struct_field_bodies_fn` / `suppress_struct_field_bodies_for_var` matches the `__karac_dropbodies_` family and deliberately NOT the struct's own `impl Drop` wrapper, which a field move-out must leave armed. With the retraction landing, the rest is the tuple fix's shape: `emit_user_drop_field_bodies_fn_skipping` keyed on the surviving index list, `disarm_struct_field_bodies_at` to retract and re-register masked (threading the binding's generic subst so a monomorph re-registers ITS walker, not the base one), and `disarm_struct_field_move_bodies` called at the same three let-site positions as the memory-half suppressor, self-gated identically. INTERPRETER TWIN: the binding-level field walk drops moved-out fields from the value before walking it -- the whole mask, since the walk resolves each declared field through `fields.get(..)` and skips a missing one, so no gate had to be threaded through its several other callers. All three container field kinds now fire ONCE on both backends; the direct-struct control and a sibling non-moved field are pinned alongside so the mask stays per-FIELD rather than per-binding.
fix: Memory half: src/codegen/param_own.rs (`suppress_struct_field_move_into_literal`'s Option/Result arm), pin asan_option_struct_field_move_out_no_double_free. Bodies half: 8407085 (src/codegen/runtime.rs, src/codegen/synth_drop.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs, src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/functions.rs, src/interpreter.rs, src/interpreter/eval_stmt.rs; pins test_e2e_struct_field_move_out_single_body_fire, test_struct_field_move_out_single_body_fire). All three pins stash-proven RED; suite 12896/0.

tracker: the stdlib Map API surface (src/interpreter + codegen Map lowering, wherever `get`/`insert` are defined) — needs an in-place map-value mutation path: a `get_mut`-shaped borrow, an entry API, or a `Map.append`-style helper for the container-valued case
title: the canonical `Map[K, Vec[V]]` grouping idiom taught by the corpus is QUADRATIC, but the language already has the O(k) answer -- `Map.entry(k).or_insert(..)` ships on both backends and measures flat. The gap is signposting: nothing leads an author from `get`/`insert` to `entry`, so a lint with a machine-applicable fix is the durable close (headline claim 'no in-place map-value mutation' DISPROVED, see detail)
detail:
SHAPE. Kara has no in-place mutation of a map VALUE. The corpus idiom for
`Map[K, Vec[V]]` (documented in `kara-katas leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams/
map_of_lists.kara` and reused by the new #244 kata) is therefore:

    match index.get(w) {
        Some(existing) => {
            let mut hits: Vec[i64] = existing.clone();   // <-- FULL COPY
            hits.push(i);
            let _ = index.insert(w, hits);
        }
        None => { ... }
    }

`get` yields a BORROW of the map's list and the map still owns it until the
reinsert lands, so the clone is not optional — it is what the language forces.
The consequence is that appending the k-th occurrence of a key copies k-1
elements, so building the index for a key seen k times costs O(k^2) element
copies. Every mirror language does this in O(k): Python
`setdefault(w, []).append(i)`, C++ `m[w].push_back(i)`, Rust
`m.entry(w).or_default().push(i)`, Go `m[w] = append(m[w], i)`.

MEASURED. Single-key list of n entries (`"the"` repeated), the degenerate case
of the same idiom, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` AOT build vs CPython 3, same machine:

    n         kara       cpython
    32000     0.10 s     0.004 s
    64000     0.52 s     0.011 s
    96000     5.60 s     0.009 s
    128000   13.37 s     0.013 s

4x the input costs kara 134x the time while CPython stays flat. At n=128000
kara is ~1000x slower than CPython doing identical work. This is not a
micro-difference that a constant factor explains — it is a complexity-class
difference in a bread-and-butter idiom (grouping, adjacency lists, inverted
indexes, bucketing all have this shape).

NOT THE BUFFER CACHE. `KARAC_BUF_CACHE=0` reproduces the same curve
(64k 0.49 s, 96k 5.77 s, 128k 13.26 s), so B-2026-07-30-4's allocator path is
not involved.

ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED. The step between n=64000 and n=96000 is
10.6x for 1.5x the input — steeper than the quadratic the construction
explains. It is not the buffer cache (above). A plausible reading is the
clone's working set (source + destination, 2 x 768 KB at n=96000) outgrowing
L2 so every copy streams from DRAM, but that was NOT confirmed and is recorded
here as an open observation, not a finding. The quadratic itself is certain
and is what this entry is about.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Any one of:

  * a `get_mut`-shaped borrow returning a mutable handle to the value in place;
  * an entry API (`map.entry(k).or_default()`) — the Rust spelling, and the one
    that composes best with the existing borrow rules;
  * a narrow `Map.append(k, v)` helper for the container-valued case, which
    covers the grouping idiom specifically without opening general in-place
    value mutation.

SOURCE NOTE. Found writing the #244 kata (map of position lists + two-pointer
merge). The kata KEEPS the natural quadratic phrasing — it is the honest way to
write this in Kara today, and per the kata rules the gap is filed rather than
routed around. The kata's scaled bench uses a count-then-fill construction
instead, which is linear and natural in all five languages, so the benchmark
compares one algorithm rather than smuggling this gap into a cross-language
number; that choice is documented in the kata README next to this id.

WORKAROUND EXISTS IN-LANGUAGE, and it is measured — recorded here so the
severity is judged on complete information. Routing the lists through an index
indirection (`Map[String, i64]` word -> slot, plus a side `Vec[Vec[i64]]`) makes
the append `lists[s].push(i)`, which mutates IN PLACE and is O(1). Same sweep,
same machine, same `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` build:

    n         direct (Map[K, Vec[V]])   pool (index indirection)
    32000     0.10 s                    0.00 s
    64000     0.49 s                    0.00 s
    96000     5.98 s                    0.00 s
    128000   14.21 s                    0.00 s

So this is a performance TRAP rather than a wall. Severity stays high anyway,
on two grounds: the trap is SILENT (nothing in `karac check` or any diagnostic
tells the author their grouping build just became quadratic — it compiles clean
and runs correctly, only slowly), and the direct phrasing is the one every
mirror language's idiom translates to, so it is what a newcomer writes first.
The indirection is a known corpus workaround (#49 `count_signature.kara`,
#244 `shortest_distance_pool.kara`), not something the language guides anyone
toward.

── HEADLINE CLAIM DISPROVED (2026-08-04). REFRAMED, SEVERITY high -> medium. ──

This entry asserts "Kara has no in-place mutation of a map VALUE". THAT IS
FALSE. The language has exactly that, it has shipped on BOTH backends, and it
is O(k):

    index.entry(w).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(i);

`Map.entry(k) -> Entry[K, V]` and `Entry.or_insert(default) -> mut ref V`
(plus `or_insert_with(|| ..)` and `and_modify(|v| ..)`, both verified) are
implemented in `src/typechecker/stdlib_map.rs::infer_entry_method` and lower on
interp, `karac run` and AOT. `or_insert`'s doc comment even cites kata 3629's
`bucket.entry(p).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(j)` as the shape it was pushed-down
for -- so the API predates this entry.

MEASURED, same machine, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` AOT, single-key list (this entry's
own degenerate shape), clone idiom vs entry API:

    n         clone       entry      cpython (this entry's column)
    32000     0.10 s      0.006 s    0.004 s
    64000     0.52 s      0.007 s    0.011 s
    96000     6.22 s      0.008 s    0.009 s
    128000   13.38 s      0.010 s    0.013 s

The clone column reproduces this entry's numbers. The entry column is FLAT --
4x the input for 1.7x the time -- and lands in CPython's range. The quadratic
is real; it is a property of the IDIOM, not of the language.

The interpreter has the same asymptotics (entry ~linear 0.26/0.44/0.69 s at
n=4000/8000/16000; clone quadratic 1.40/5.92/21.28 s over the same range), so
this is not a codegen-only path either.

NOT A TOY-ONLY RESULT. The real group-anagrams shape -- `Map[String,
Vec[String]]`, COMPUTED String key, string values -- runs correctly on interp
and AOT through `groups.entry(k).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(w)`.

WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY IS, and it is a real one, just much smaller than
filed. Nothing leads an author from `get`/`insert` to `entry`, and the CORPUS
teaches the clone: `kara-katas leetcode/1-100/49-group-anagrams/
map_of_lists.kara` documents clone-reinsert as THE `Map[K, Vec[V]]` pattern,
and #244 inherited it. So the measured 1000x is the cost of a kata following
documented guidance that happens to be the slow path.

Remaining work, none of which is "implement in-place map mutation":
  * CORPUS -- retarget `map_of_lists.kara` and #244 onto the entry API (the
    kara-katas repo, not this one).
  * DIAGNOSTICS -- the compiler can recognize the clone-reinsert shape
    (`match m.get(k) { Some(x) => { let mut y = x.clone(); y.push(..);
    m.insert(k, y); } None => .. }`) and emit a machine-applicable fix to
    `m.entry(k).or_insert(..)`. That is the durable fix: it turns a
    discoverability gap into a `karac fix` the Mend loop applies, and it is
    what would have kept the corpus off the slow path in the first place.

SEVERITY high -> medium. The "high" rested on a complexity-class hole in a
bread-and-butter idiom. There is no hole -- there is a signposting gap with a
shipped O(k) answer one method call away.

PROCESS NOTE, the third of this shape in this ledger (cf. B-2026-08-01-33's
own "par struct shares lock-free" retraction, and the HTTP/2 sibling-stream
claim). All three were written from a failed or assumed path without testing
the sanctioned alternative, and all three were caught by one probe. Filing a
MISSING FEATURE deserves a stronger check than filing a bug: grep the method
table for the capability before concluding it is absent. `require_known_method`
lists every Map method in one place -- "entry" is in it.

── CLOSED d166203 — `map_value_clone_reinsert` lint ──

The reframe above named a lint as the durable close: recognize the
clone-reinsert shape and offer `entry().or_insert()` as a machine-applicable
fix, so the discoverability gap becomes something `karac fix` applies rather
than something every author has to independently not-fall-into. Done.

`src/map_entry_lint.rs`, registered in `src/lints.rs` (default Warn).
Suppressible with `-A map_value_clone_reinsert` and via the manifest's
`[lints]` table; per-ITEM `#[allow(map_value_clone_reinsert)]` is NOT honoured,
because this module emits outside `TypeChecker::type_lint_warning`, which is
what consults item attributes. `must_use_lint` has the identical limitation
(it passes the same `false` triple for source-level flags) — wiring attribute
scope is a shared follow-up for both, and is deliberately not faked here.
VERIFIED both ways: default fires, `-A` suppresses. Emitted into `typed.warnings`
rather than through a bespoke lint channel, which means it rides plumbing that
already existed: `--output=json` renders it with `lint_name` and `fix_it`, and
`karac fix` applies the edit.

VALIDATED AGAINST THE REAL ARTIFACT, not just a synthetic probe. Run against
the pre-fix `kara-katas` #244 `shortest_distance_ii.kara` — the file that
carried this entry's measured 1736x slowdown — the lint fires at the right line
and emits exactly the rewrite that was made by hand:

    index.entry(w).or_insert(Vec.new()).push(i);

End to end on a probe: `karac fix` collapsed the 12-line match to that line,
output unchanged (interp / JIT / AOT all 4), and the lint does not re-fire on
its own output.

THE SHAPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROW, because this lint REWRITES WORKING CODE — a
false positive silently changes behaviour, which is a worse failure than the
quadratic it fixes. It requires: scrutinee `M.get(K)` typed `Option[<container>]`;
exactly two arms; each arm exactly three statements (`let mut v = ..` /
`v.<m>(args)` / `let _ = M.insert(K, v)`); the Some arm's init is `b.clone()`;
and M, K, method and args spelled identically across both arms. Every negative
test is a rewrite that would be WRONG, not merely noisy:

  * scalar-valued map        -> O(1) already, nothing to fix
  * an arm with a 4th stmt   -> the rewrite has nowhere to put it. This is #49's
                                `map_of_lists.kara` (`order.push(key)` records
                                first-seen order); firing there would silently
                                drop it. Verified silent against the real file.
  * bound `insert` result    -> the DISPLACED value is in use; `or_insert` never
                                displaces, so the rewrite loses it
  * different keys per arm   -> not one logical append
  * no clone                 -> nothing quadratic present
  * already-fixed form       -> fixpoint, so `karac fix` cannot oscillate

TWO THINGS FOUND ALONG THE WAY, both worth keeping:

  1. `expr_types` AT A RECEIVER SPAN IS THE ENCLOSING CALL'S TYPE. Typing `m` in
     `m.get(k)` returns `Option[V]`, not `Map[K, V]` — a chained access shares
     its start offset with the enclosing call, the same span-overwrite hazard
     `ownership.rs` documents for projections. The lint reads the value type off
     the SCRUTINEE's `Option[V]` payload instead, whose span is unambiguous.
     Anyone reaching for a receiver's type by span needs to know this.
  2. `cmd_fix` READ ONLY `typed.errors` FIX-ITS, never `typed.warnings`. Until
     this lint there was no warning-with-a-fix producer, so nothing surfaced it
     — but the JSON already advertised `fix_it` on warnings, so any future
     warning-borne fix would have been advertised and then not applied. Now
     read. A warning's fix is optional-but-safe by construction, which is
     exactly what `fix` is for.

KNOWN LIMITATION, pre-existing and NOT introduced here: typecheck warnings do
not render in `karac check`'s TEXT output at all — verified by checking that an
existing warning (unreachable match arm) is equally invisible there, while both
appear under `--output=json`. So a human running bare `karac check` will not see
this lint; the Mend loop (`--output=json`) and `karac fix` both do, which is the
channel that motivated it. Worth filing separately for the whole warning class;
deliberately not widened here, since adding a text renderer would change output
for every existing typecheck warning at once.

title: an Option field whose payload is INLINE (a struct narrow enough to fit the 3-word payload area) fires its Drop body THREE times under AOT when the owning struct is passed by value — the BOXED-payload sibling is correct
detail: `struct Small { id: i64 }` + `impl Drop`, `struct Hsm { o: Option[Small], t: i64 }`, `fn take(h: Hsm) -> i64 { h.t }`, `println(take(h))`. `karac run` prints `drop 3` ONCE; `karac build` prints it THREE times, and one of them lands before the `4` rather than after (probe b215/p2). Pre-existing -- verified by rebuilding src/ at 9a5ce03. vg=0 throughout: `Small` owns no heap, so this is a pure body-COUNT bug with no memory consequence, which is also why no sanitizer can see it. THE DISCRIMINATOR, and the reason this is worth its own row: the same shape with a WIDER payload is CORRECT. `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` is 4 words, so `Option[Res]` heap-BOXES its payload, and `struct Hopt { o: Option[Res], t: i64 }` through the identical by-value param prints exactly once on both backends, vg=0 (probe b215/p1); so does the returned-from-a-fn variant (p3). So the entry-copy / field-drop / bodies-walk pairing for an Option struct field is sound on the BOXED path and triple-fires on the INLINE one -- the split is `llvm_type_word_count(payload) > 3` in `emit_option_drop_fn` and `deep_copy_option_struct_enum_payload_in_place`, which is the first place to look. Three fires suggests three separate owners each running the body over the same inline words: plausibly the caller's binding, the callee's entry copy, and one of the field-bodies walks firing on a slot the inline path did not neutralize (the boxed path's neutralizer is a pointer store, the inline path's would have to be a tag or cap write). FOUND WHILE probing B-2026-08-03-3 leg B: p1/p2 were built to discriminate that row's two suspects, and p1's cleanliness is what rules out `a boxed payload cannot survive a by-value param` as the explanation for leg B's double-free -- so leg B's failure is most likely a slip in the new Result copy helper rather than a structural impossibility. That conclusion is recorded on -3 as well.  ROOT CAUSE + FIX (2026-08-03, 257d666). `emit_drop_fn_for_type_expr` (src/codegen/clone_drop.rs) carries a guard, documented since B-2026-07-30-11, that routes a Drop-bearing bare user STRUCT to the MEMORY-ONLY synthesis so the memory channel never re-runs a body the NLL `UserDrop` channel already owns. The guard's own FALLBACK -- taken when `emit_struct_drop_synthesis` returns None because the struct has no heap to free -- called `emit_primitive_drop_fn(&type_name)`, and that emitter OPENS with the same `module.get_function("karac_drop_<T>")` lookup the guard exists to bypass. That name IS the user-drop WRAPPER, so the memory channel was handed the wrapper and fired the body a second (and, once the field's own registration also routed through it, a third) time. Only shapes that REACH the memory channel for such a struct were affected, which is exactly why every neighbour read correct in the narrowing matrix: a BOXED payload (`Option[Big]`, q5), the `Result` sibling whose narrower admit registers no memory drop on this route (q6), a DIRECT `Option[Small]` binding (q4) and a direct `Small` field (q7). Minimal repro q2 needs no function call at all: `struct Small { id: i64 }` + `impl Drop`, `struct Hsm { o: Option[Small], t: i64 }`, `let h = Hsm { .. }; println(h.t);`. FIX: name the fallback `<T>$mem` -- a `$` cannot appear in a user type name, so the lookup can never alias the wrapper again. LESSON: a guard that exists to bypass a name lookup must not delegate to a helper that re-performs the same lookup; the bypass has to hold for the helper's whole call tree, not just the guard's own body.
fix: 257d666 (src/codegen/clone_drop.rs; pin test_e2e_inline_option_payload_field_body_fires_once, stash-proven RED -- pre-fix AOT prints `drop 1` twice and `drop 2` three times where the interpreter prints each once)

title: a struct field holding a MIXED `Result[<Drop struct>, String]` -- one half a direct String/Vec, the other a struct/enum -- is admitted by NEITHER Result field-drop gate, so the STRUCT half's heap is never freed
detail: SURFACED while closing B-2026-08-03-3 leg B (8cfe5be), which armed the field free for a Result whose heap-owning halves are ALL non-shared structs/enums. That gate (`result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok`) and the older `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` were deliberately made structurally DISJOINT so each class binds to exactly one entry-copy helper and copy-depth == free-depth stays checkable by inspection. The consequence is a hole between them: a field typed `Result[Res, String]` (Res a Drop struct owning a String) has one heap half of each kind, so the vecstr gate rejects it for the struct half and the new gate rejects it for the String half. No field free is registered and the struct payload's buffer is orphaned.  MEASURED (probes b215/u1 and b215/u2, `struct Hm { r: Result[Res, String], t: i64 }`): 5 bytes definitely lost under valgrind on the Ok side, AOT and `karac run --interp` agreeing on output throughout, so parity is blind to it and only the leak oracle sees it. u2 reads BOTH halves (`match h.r { Ok(x) => x.id, Err(e) => e.len() }` through a `ref` param) to rule out the elided-dead-allocation artifact that made this family look clean before B-2026-08-03-1; the Err String is correctly freed by the existing overlay route, so the gap is the struct payload alone.  WHY IT SHOULD BE SMALL. Both FREE sides already dispatch per half across the two representations: `emit_result_drop_fn` branches independently on Ok and Err, and `track_inline_result_payload_var` pairs `result_inline_payload_elems` (overlay) with `result_inline_payload_struct_drops` (full struct drop) per side. Only the ADMIT GATE and the ENTRY COPY are single-class. Suggested shape: require at least one struct/enum heap half (which preserves disjointness from the vecstr gate) while also ACCEPTING a direct String/Vec heap half, and extend `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` to emit the `{ptr,len,cap}` overlay copy for such a half instead of skipping it -- the same dance `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` already performs, worth factoring into a shared per-half emitter so the two cannot drift. Keep the `> 5` boxing threshold; the Option family's `> 3` is what broke leg B's first attempt.  FIXED (2026-08-03, 0567cea) exactly along the shape this row predicted, in three small pieces. (1) `result_field_struct_enum_payload_ok` now REQUIRES at least one struct/enum heap half and ACCEPTS a direct String/Vec half alongside it (new `result_half_is_direct_vecstr`, which carries over the vecstr gate's shared-element exclusion -- the defensive copy emits no per-element rc-inc). Disjointness from `result_field_direct_vecstr_halves_ok` is preserved, and now rests on the struct/enum REQUIREMENT rather than on a prohibition: this gate demands one, that gate rejects any. (2) The `{ptr,len,cap}` overlay dance was extracted out of `deep_copy_result_inline_heap_halves_in_place` into `emit_result_half_overlay_copy` (caller owns the tag test and the blocks; builder must be positioned in the taken arm), so the two entry-copy helpers that need it cannot drift. (3) `deep_copy_result_struct_enum_payload_in_place` classifies each half up-front -- heapless skips, struct/enum takes the boxed-or-inline dance at the Result area's `> 5`, direct String/Vec routes to the extracted overlay copy -- and `result_payload_struct_enum_copyable` admits the direct half (its own gate already vetted it). No change was needed on either FREE side: `emit_result_drop_fn` and `track_inline_result_payload_var` already dispatched per half, which is what made this a three-piece fix rather than a redesign.  VERIFIED across six positions on both backends, all `SAME` and vg=0 (probes b215/u1, u2, u3): Ok-struct binding, Err-String binding, by-value param, `let x = h.r` move-out, and the SWAPPED arrangement `Result[Vec[String], Res]` on each side -- the half-order control, since the admit is per half and not per position. u2 additionally reads BOTH halves so the elided-dead-allocation artifact cannot mask the result.  ORACLE NOTE, worth keeping: this row is one the parity oracle cannot see at all. The interpreter matched AOT line-for-line before the fix and the Drop body count was already right; only LSan saw the orphaned buffer (stash-proven RED at 123 bytes in 6 allocations). The codegen E2E pin `test_e2e_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed` is therefore a COMPANION guard, green before and after -- its job is the other direction, pinning that arming this class did not turn any of the six consuming positions into a double-free or double-fire, which is the failure mode B-2026-08-03-3 hit three times.
fix: 0567cea (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/param_own.rs; pins asan_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed -- the leak oracle, stash-proven RED with 123 bytes leaked in 6 allocations under LSan -- and the companion E2E test_e2e_mixed_halves_result_struct_field_freed, which is green under the stash by construction and guards the six consuming positions against the double-free/double-fire that arming a free invites)

title: `coroutine_preserves_active_span_across_suspend` (tests/coro_e2e.rs) is INTERMITTENT -- the post-resume log line came back unstamped (`[info] after-resume`, span_id=0) on one full-suite run and has not reproduced in 19 attempts since
detail:
SURFACE NOTE: filed as `codegen` because the assertion guards the coroutine state-machine transform's active-span save/restore (`emit_coro_park_suspend`'s frame snapshot + the resume-edge restore); if the nondeterminism is in the harness rather than the transform, the surface should be corrected when it is diagnosed. `source` carries the real provenance.  OBSERVED ONCE, 2026-08-03, during a full `cargo test --features llvm` run (33 passed / 1 failed in coro_e2e; every other target green). The assertion wants `[info] after-resume span_id=7`; the run produced `["BOUND_PORT=37223", "[info] after-resume", "2"]` -- the line is there, the program exits successfully and prints `2`, only the span stamp is missing, which per the test's own comment is exactly the shape of a Phase-2 regression (span_id=0 renders no suffix).  NOT REPRODUCED SINCE: 4 standalone runs, 15 consecutive runs while a full suite was saturating the machine, and a second complete `cargo test --features llvm` (12,900 passed / 0 failed). So it is rare and load-correlated at most.  WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY. This is a required CI gate as of B-2026-07-31-44 (coro_e2e was one of the 17 dark targets added to `codegen-e2e`), so a rare miss turns into a red build nobody can reproduce -- and the failure is indistinguishable from a real span-preservation regression, which is the expensive kind of ambiguity.  DISCRIMINATOR TO TRY. `service_one_connection` retries the connect for up to 3s specifically to absorb the race between `bind`'s BOUND_PORT print and the coroutine's fd registration -- so whether `accept()` actually PARKS is timing-dependent. Both paths should yield span 7 (no park: the body runs on the calling thread inside `with_span`; park: the save/restore reinstalls it), so a run that prints 0 means one of those two is not airtight. Start by making the park deterministic (a probe binary that logs whether it suspended) rather than by chasing the assertion.

FIXED 2026-08-04. NOT a harness flake -- a real data race in the coroutine
transform, and the entry's `codegen` surface guess was right.

MECHANISM. `emit_coro_park_suspend` (src/codegen/coro.rs) emitted the pre-suspend
active-span snapshot AFTER `karac_runtime_event_loop_register_fd_cancel`. That call is the
publication point: it inserts the frame-resident parked record into the (sharded) event loop
and wakes its poller, and the `llvm.coro.save` immediately above it exists precisely so a
resume is legal from there on -- the code's own comment says the dispatcher "can claim and
resume ... this frame before the worker thread running the ramp reaches the `coro.suspend`
below". So the ordering was:

    coro.save                     <- resume becomes legal here
    register_fd_cancel(...)       <- frame published to the reactor
    store parked.token
    %snap = call karac_tracing_get_active_span()   <- RACING a resumer
    store active_span_slot, %snap                  <- RACING a resumer
    coro.suspend

and the resume edge LOADS `active_span_slot` to reinstall the span. When the dispatcher won
the race it read the slot before the ramp wrote it, got the fresh frame's zero, and called
`set_active_span(0)` -- so the post-resume log line rendered with no span suffix. That is a
data race on the slot, not merely a lost value.

Everything the entry recorded follows: rare (the resumer has to win a two-instruction
window), load-correlated (the comment above notes the fd "is often immediately ready" under
load), and specifically `span_id=0` rather than a wrong span (zeroed frame memory).

THE ENTRY'S SUGGESTED DISCRIMINATOR WAS BASED ON A FALSE PREMISE, recorded here so nobody
retries it. It said "whether `accept()` actually PARKS is timing-dependent" and advised
starting there. It is not: `emit_state_machine_invocation_for_park_on_fd` (src/codegen/tcp.rs)
routes unconditionally to `emit_coro_park_suspend` inside a coroutine -- there is no
try-syscall-first fast path, the register+suspend always happens, and the actual `accept`
syscall is emitted on the resume edge. Both of the entry's two hypothesised paths were really
one path.

REPRODUCED DETERMINISTICALLY, which is what turned this from a suspicion into a fix. A
temporary `karac_debug_park_race_delay()` extern (env-gated busy-spin, added to the runtime
and called from codegen between `register_fd` and the snapshot, then removed) widens the
window:

  delay off, pre-fix    13 runs, 0 failures     (10 baseline + 3 control)
  delay 2 ms, pre-fix    5 runs, 4 failures
  delay 2 ms, post-fix   8 runs, 0 failures
  delay 20 ms, post-fix  6 runs, 0 failures

and the forced failure is identical in shape to the one this entry recorded:
["BOUND_PORT=43695", "[info] after-resume", "2"] versus the filed
["BOUND_PORT=37223", "[info] after-resume", "2"].

FIX: hoist the snapshot above `coro.save`, so every frame write the ramping thread performs
completes before the frame is reachable by anyone else. Value-preserving -- the read is of
the ramping thread's own TLS and nothing between the old and new positions touches it.

THE SIBLING STORE IS BENIGN, checked rather than assumed, because it looks like the same bug
and the next reader will ask. `store parked.token` is also below the publication and cannot
be hoisted (the token does not exist until `register_fd` returns it). The difference is what
consumes it: the post-suspend edges load that field only to pass to `deregister_fd`, and the
dispatcher claims every registration through a one-shot `take_registration` BEFORE it fires
-- so in exactly the racing case the deregister is already a no-op whatever the field holds.
The active-span slot had no such property; its value was used.

REGRESSION GUARD is an IR ORDERING pin,
`coroutine_active_span_snapshot_precedes_frame_publication` (tests/coro_e2e.rs), asserting
the snapshot call precedes `register_fd_cancel` in the ramp. It has to be structural: the
behavioural sibling passed 10/10 here and 19/19 when this entry was filed WITH the bug
present, so it cannot hold this line. Verified to bite -- reverting the hoist fails it
(snapshot@3188 vs publish@2755). The pin anchors on publication rather than `coro.save`
because CoroSplit consumes the save intrinsic; publication is the property that actually
matters and it survives the split.

TEST-INFRA NOTE: this makes the E2E sibling's required-CI status (B-2026-07-31-44) safe
again; the ambiguity the entry called "the expensive kind" is resolved in favour of a real
defect.
tracker: src/codegen/coro.rs (emit_coro_park_suspend: active-span snapshot hoisted above coro.save/register_fd)

title: FRESH-TEMP twin of B-2026-08-02-25's match-arm leg: a heap-BOXED Option/Result payload bound out of a `match mk() { Some(r) => .. }` arm runs its Drop BODY against the binding's reconstructed COPY, not the box, so a body that MUTATES a heap field (`self.buf.clear()`) frees the buffer while the box keeps the stale pointer and the scope-exit box drop frees it again
detail: REPRO (probe b225/as_e, 20 iterations, exit 134 under glibc and 20 invalid frees under valgrind): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` with `impl Drop for Full { fn drop(mut ref self) { if self.buf[0] < 0 { println(self.buf[0]); } self.buf.clear(); } }`, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(i) { Option.Some(r) => { n = n + r.buf.len(); } ... }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. The interpreter is correct; AOT double-frees.  MECHANISM, and it is exactly the one B-2026-08-02-25's fix had to avoid on the NAMED route. `bind_pattern_values` reconstructs a boxed payload into a struct-VALUE alloca -- a copy of the box's `{ptr,len,cap}` -- and the fresh-temp arm of `is_boxed_optres_drop_payload` registers `__karac_dropbodies_only_<T>` over THAT alloca. The box, not the binding, still owns the payload's memory. A read-only Drop body is harmless there, but a mutating one writes to the wrong storage: `clear()` frees `buf.data` and zeroes the COPY's cap, the box's words are untouched, and `karac_drop_Option_Full` -> the payload's memory drop frees the same pointer a second time.  NOT A REGRESSION -- stash-proven identical before and after the B-2026-08-02-25 fix (which touched only the named-source route). It went unnoticed because no test paired a fresh-temp match arm with a MUTATING Drop body: `asan_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fire_once` has the mutating body but its fresh-temp cases hold the Option without matching on it, and every E2E pin in this family uses a read-only `println` body, which cannot witness the class.  FIX SHAPE IS KNOWN, by symmetry with the closed leg: run the walk against the BOX. The named route does this by re-registering the source's own `__karac_dropelems_opt_*` action (slot + walker sampled by `scrutinee_armed_payload_bodies_action`) under the binding's name. A fresh temp has no named source to sample, but `compile_match` does stage the scrutinee -- thread that staged slot to the bind site the way `freshtemp_enum` / `freshtemp_inline_res` are already threaded, then instantiate `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn` from the scrutinee's Option/Result te and register THAT over the staged slot under the binding's name. The `__karac_dropelems_` prefix also satisfies `fire_due_user_drops`' NLL gate, so the timing comes along for free.  ORACLE NOTE: parity diffing DOES see this one (AOT aborts, `karac run` prints the answer), and so does valgrind/LSan. What no oracle in the suite saw is the input -- a fresh-temp arm over a mutating body. Worth a drop_fuzz corpus entry: mutating Drop bodies are under-represented against every payload-position axis, not just this one.  FIXED (2026-08-04, c89192f) exactly along the fix shape this row predicted. `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` now RETURNS the `__freshtemp_boxed_scrut` alloca it stages; `freshtemp_payload_bodies_action` resolves the scrutinee's Option/Result instantiation (the span table first, then the fn-return / pop-family derivation `track_discarded_optres_payload_bodies` already used), instantiates `emit_optres_payload_user_drop_bodies_fn`, and hands the `(slot, walker)` pair to the SAME re-homing branch B-2026-08-02-25 added for the named route. So the bind site now has ONE code path fed by one field, and the two routes cannot drift: whichever supplies the pair, the walk runs against a slot holding the box pointer rather than against the arm binding's reconstructed copy.  FALLBACK IS THE OLD BEHAVIOR, deliberately: any missing ingredient -- no staged slot (non-boxed, non-fresh, or a borrow scrutinee), no resolvable instantiation, or a payload that runs no user Drop -- leaves the previous bodies-only-over-the-copy registration in place, so nothing outside the boxed fresh-temp shape can move.  VERIFIED by pre/post stash attribution over two probe sets. Of 7 fresh-temp probes (b226/f1-f7) exactly 5 change, every one from a double-free ABORT to correct output: bare match, if-let, let-else, boxed `Result` past its wider 5-word area, and `while let Some(r) = v.pop()` (the one shape whose type comes from the pop-family derivation rather than the fn-return table). The other two are CONTROLS and are byte-identical -- a borrow scrutinee (`m.get(k)`, whose payload aliases the map's storage) and a non-consuming `Some(_)` arm. Of the 35 probes from the named-route slice exactly ONE changes -- `as_e`, which is this bug. All 6 fixed probes are vg=0.  A THIRD DEFECT fell out of the control: the `Some(_)` probe leaks 32 bytes, stash-proven identical before and after, filed as B-2026-08-04-3 (a wildcard payload leaves `inner_struct_name` empty so the box drop is box-only). It is kept OUT of this row's ASan pin so LSan cannot misattribute it there.  ORACLE NOTE, and the reason this outlived the leg that shares its root cause: the read-only `println` Drop bodies every E2E pin in this family uses cannot witness the class at all -- they touch no heap, so copy-vs-box is unobservable. Both new pins mutate on purpose. That is also the generalizable gap: mutating Drop bodies are under-represented in the corpus against every payload-position axis, which is worth a drop_fuzz entry independent of this row.
fix: c89192f (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box, both stash-proven RED -- the E2E aborts before flushing any output (`left: ""`) and the ASan pin reports a double-free at exit 23)

title: A heap-BOXED Option payload bound by a consuming match arm and then MOVED -- into a struct literal, or out as the match's tail value -- double-frees under `karac build` while the interpreter is correct; read-only Drop body, both named and fresh-temp scrutinees
detail: REPROS, all with `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` (4 words, so BOXED at Option's 3-word area) and a READ-ONLY `impl Drop for Res { fn drop(mut ref self) { println(f"drop {self.id} {self.name}") } }` -- the body touches no heap, so this is NOT the mutating-body class of B-2026-08-04-1.  (1) probe b225/p5, move into a struct literal: `let o: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); match o { Option.Some(r) => { let w = W { r: r }; println(w.r.id); } ... }` -- interp `got 5 / drop 5 eeeee5 / end`, AOT `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, exit 134.  (2) probe b225/p6, the binding escapes as the match's VALUE: `let r2 = match o { Option.Some(r) => r, Option.None => Res { .. } }; println(r2.id);` -- same split, same abort.  (3) probe b225/p5t, the FRESH-TEMP spelling of (1) (`match mko() { .. }`) -- same abort, so the defect is not specific to a named source.  CONTROLS that pin the boundary: with an INLINE payload (`struct Res { name: String }`, 3 words) shape (1) is fully correct on both backends (probe p5i), so BOXING is the discriminator. Shape (2) with an inline payload is a DIFFERENT and milder defect (probe p6i): AOT prints a spurious leading `drop ` with an EMPTY NAME before the real body -- a stale-slot read rather than a double-free -- which looks like the same move-out bookkeeping gap seen from the inline side and is probably worth fixing in the same pass.  PRE-EXISTING, and measured as such: identical output before and after the B-2026-08-02-25 match-arm fix (542d7d7) on all four probes.
