That fix only re-homes the payload's Drop BODY (a walk that frees nothing by construction) and changes no memory action, which is why it neither caused nor cured this.  STARTING POINT: the arm's memory suppressors decide who owns a boxed payload's interior after the bind. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` handles a struct SUB-PATTERN (`Some(Res { name })`) by cap-zeroing the consumed fields INSIDE the box, but there is no equivalent for a WHOLE-payload binding that then moves: the destination (the struct literal's field, the match result) takes ownership of the payload's heap children and frees them, while the box drop still frees the same buffers. Compare against the INLINE path, which gets this right -- it suppresses via the source's cap/tag zeroing and the binding's own `track_struct_var`.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 8f8696d).  FIRST, A CORRECTION to this row's own framing. It described the class as firing with a READ-ONLY Drop body and recorded that the same shapes were clean without an `impl Drop` -- treating the Drop impl as the discriminator. It is not one. Those clean readings were a DEAD-ALLOCATION artifact: with nothing reading the moved payload's heap field the buffer is elided and every case looks fine. Add one `println(w.r.name)` and the no-Drop program aborts identically (probe b227/h3). The Drop impl was only ever keeping the buffer live. Same trap as this family's other two rows, from the opposite direction -- there a read-only body hid the bug, here a dead buffer did.  MEASURED SURFACE, with the payload's field forced live (probes b227/k1-k7): FOUR move destinations abort and two positions are correct. Broken: a struct-literal field, the match's own tail value, a plain `let` rebind, and a container push -- named and fresh-temp scrutinees alike. Correct: a by-value fn ARG, and no move at all.  ROOT CAUSE: the arm binding is an unboxed COPY of the box's `{ptr,len,cap}` words and registers no memory drop of its own, by design -- the `BoxedEnumDrop`'s `inner_drop_fn` owns the interior, which is what keeps `if let Some(r) = v.pop()` from double-freeing. Once the binding moves, the destination registers its own drop over those same buffers and both free them. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` already solves the STRUCT-SUB-PATTERN case (`Some(H { v, .. })`) by cap-zeroing the named fields inside the box; there was no equivalent for a whole-payload binding.  THE FIX records the binding in `boxed_optres_payload_view_vars` (name -> scrutinee slot, snapshotted with the per-arm var environment) and, at each move site, clears the source `BoxedEnumDrop`'s `inner_drop_fn`, leaving a BOX-ONLY free. Sites: struct-literal fields, the let RHS, the match tail, and the container-consuming-arg hook.  WHY RETRACT THE WALK RATHER THAN CAP-ZERO THE BOX, which was tried first and is the more obvious move given the struct-sub-pattern precedent: the box's words are ALSO what the re-homed payload-BODIES walk reads -- B-2026-08-02-25 / B-2026-08-04-1 point it at the source slot precisely so a mutating Drop body lands on the storage the later free sees. `zero_struct_move_caps` clears `len` alongside `cap` for this shape, so the body then printed an EMPTY string (probe b227/m1: `in-callee [eeeeeeee5] len=9` but `drop 5 [] len=0`). That converts a double-free into a silent wrong-value -- strictly worse. Clearing the action's fn pointer touches no data, so the body still reads the live payload. The two landed rows and this one are only mutually consistent under the walk-retraction form.  THE BY-VALUE ARG IS NOT A MOVE, and this cost a cut. The first version dispatched the neutralizer from `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` to inherit its 13-site roster; that roster includes call args, where the callee takes an entry COPY under caller-retains. Neutralizing there LEAKED the box's copy (9 bytes, probes g5d/m1). Both new pins carry that control explicitly.  VERIFIED: 17 b227 probes all parity-equal and vg=0. Across the 43 probes from the two preceding rows, exactly THREE change -- p5, p6, p5t -- which are this row's own repros, every other one byte-identical.  RESIDUAL, unchanged and still open: the INLINE sibling of the tail-value shape (probe b225/p6i) prints a spurious leading body with an EMPTY name -- a stale-slot read rather than a double-free. Same move-out bookkeeping seen from the inline side; not touched here.
fix: 8f8696d (src/codegen.rs, src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/exprs.rs, src/codegen/functions.rs, src/codegen/mono.rs, src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs, src/codegen/runtime.rs, src/codegen/shadow.rs, src/codegen/stmts.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_boxed_optres_payload_view_move_transfers_box_interior (stash-proven RED -- aborts before flushing any output) and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_view_move_has_one_owner, both carrying the by-value-arg and no-move controls that the first cut got wrong)

title: A FRESH-TEMP boxed Option/Result scrutinee matched by a WILDCARD payload arm (`match mk() { Some(_) => .. }`) gets a box-ONLY free, so the payload struct's inner heap leaks -- the whole-binding sibling (`Some(r)`) is correct because only a Binding sub-pattern populates `inner_struct_name`
detail: REPRO (probe b226/f7, 32 bytes definitely lost under valgrind, parity-EQUAL so no run-vs-build split): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` with any Drop impl, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(7i64) { Option.Some(_) => { println("arm"); } Option.None => { println("none"); } }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. Change the arm to `Option.Some(r)` and the same program is vg=0.  MECHANISM: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` decides how deep the box drop goes from the PAYLOAD SUB-PATTERN. Its `inner_struct_name` match arm is `PatternKind::Binding(_) if !scrutinee_is_borrow => .. pattern_binding_types.get(pkey) ..`, with `_ => None` for everything else. A WILDCARD payload therefore yields `None` and `track_boxed_enum_var` registers a box-ONLY free: the box allocation is reclaimed, the payload struct's `Vec`/`String` fields inside it are not.  The `_ => None` arm is CORRECT for a struct-DESTRUCTURE payload (`Some(H { v, .. })`), whose leaf bindings each own and free their own field -- walking the interior there would double-free, and the existing comment says so. The gap is that a WILDCARD binds nothing at all, so nobody owns the interior and the `_ => None` arm treats it like the destructure case. The fix has to distinguish binds-nothing from binds-the-parts, which the current match on `payload.kind` collapses.  SCOPE: also check `Some(_)` inside a tuple/struct sub-pattern that leaves SOME fields unbound, and the `Result` Err-side twin. The NAMED-source sibling of this shape is a different code path (`boxed_enum_payload_vars` + `BoxedEnumDrop`) and was not measured here.  PRE-EXISTING and independently attributed: stash-proven identical (vg=99, 32 bytes) before and after B-2026-08-04-1's fix, which changed only the BODY walk's subject and registers nothing at all for a wildcard arm (no payload binding => no registration site reached).  ORACLE NOTE: invisible to parity diffing and to fire counting -- AOT and `karac run` print the same thing and the Drop body correctly does not run -- so only valgrind/LSan sees it. Deliberately kept OUT of `asan_freshtemp_boxed_optres_payload_arm_body_runs_against_the_box` (whose `d` case is this exact shape, minus the leak-triggering heap field) so LSan does not attribute this row's leak to that pin.  FIXED (2026-08-04, bad9a7a). The row's diagnosis was right about the `_ => None` arm and about needing to separate binds-nothing from binds-the-parts, but it missed a SECOND gate that had to move first: a wildcard carries no type, so `pattern_payload_word_count` falls to its 1-word default and the WIDTH check above the derivation rejected the arm before `inner_struct_name` could be reached at all. Splitting the `_ => None` arm alone changed nothing (measured). Both the size and the payload struct NAME now come from the SCRUTINEE's instantiation -- `optres_scrutinee_payload_struct_name_for`, reusing `optres_scrutinee_type_expr`, with the variant selecting which generic arg to read so `Result`'s Ok and Err halves cannot be crossed. The variant extraction was hoisted above the width gate to make that possible.  Borrow scrutinees stay excluded for the reason the `Binding` arm gives: their box interior aliases the container's storage, so zeroing or walking it would strand or double-free the container's buffers.  VERIFIED: probes b228/x1 (`Option`) and b228/x6 (`Result` Err side) go from 32 bytes definitely-lost to vg=0; the three controls -- whole binding (x2), named scrutinee (x5), inline payload (y3) -- are unchanged and clean. Suites: codegen 2775, memory_sanitizer 923, interpreter 1437, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5374 passed, 0 failed.  NOT RE-RUN: the full `--features llvm` suite. Two full runs were green earlier in the session (12,912 and 12,914) but neither includes this commit.  WHAT THE SWEEP ALSO FOUND, and why this row's own scope note was well-placed: it asked whoever fixed this to check partial struct sub-patterns. Those probes never ran -- a struct destructure of a boxed payload PANICS the compiler (`ExtractOutOfRange`), filed as B-2026-08-04-5 (HIGH, ICE) and pre-existing. Its fix will make `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` reachable for the first time, which is where the partial-destructure ownership question actually gets answered.
fix: bad9a7a (src/codegen/control_flow.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_wildcard_boxed_optres_payload_frees_the_struct_interior, stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer, covering the `Option` wildcard, the `Result` Err-side wildcard, and a whole-binding control)

title: INTERPRETER: a Drop-body move record is keyed by BINDING NAME and outlives its block, so a later same-named binding that was never moved is treated as moved and its user `impl Drop` body is silently skipped -- rename the second binding and the body fires
detail:
MINIMAL REPRO (probes b227/w1 vs b227/w2, interpreter only; AOT is correct in both, so this is a run-vs-build split on the `karac run` side). `struct Res { id: i64, name: String }` with a printing `impl Drop`, then two sibling blocks in one `main`:  BLOCK 1 -- `let o: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); let mut v: Vec[Res] = Vec.new(); match o { Option.Some(r) => { v.push(r); } .. } println(v[0].name);`  BLOCK 2 -- `let o2: Option[Res] = Option.Some(Res { .. }); match o2 { Option.Some(X) => { println(X.name); } .. }`  With X = `q` the interpreter prints `pay4 | D4 | pay6 | D6 | end` -- correct. With X = `r`, reusing block 1's binding name, it prints `pay4 | D4 | pay6 | end`: D6 is GONE. Nothing else differs.  So the move recorded for block 1's `r` (pushed into the Vec) is still live when block 2's unrelated `r` is bound, and suppresses that binding's body. The name is the whole trigger.  SCOPE, from a prefix bisect over a 7-block program (probes b227/c1..c1234): only the CONTAINER-PUSH move leaves the sticky record. A struct-literal move, a match-tail move, and a `let` rebind in block 1 all leave block 2's body firing. So the suspect is the push/insert consuming-arg move record specifically, not the general move bookkeeping -- start at the interpreter twin of `disarm_container_bodies_for_arg` (`record_container_bodies_move_sources` and its neighbours) and check whether its record is scoped to the enclosing block the way the let-RHS and aggregate-literal ones are.  HOW IT SURFACED, which is worth keeping: it was found while building the B-2026-08-04-2 regression pin. A 7-case E2E program was parity-equal on the five MOVE cases and diverged on the two CONTROLS -- AOT firing, interpreter silent -- while each control in ISOLATION was parity-equal. That shape (a test that passes case-by-case and fails combined) is the signature of exactly this kind of leaked per-name state, and it is a reason to be wary of the convenience of reusing `r` for every case in a multi-case pin. The B-2026-08-04-2 pin was consequently split: five move cases combined, both controls as their own single-case programs.  NOT CAUSED BY the B-2026-08-04-2 fix, which is codegen-only -- the interpreter path is untouched by it, and the AOT side of the same program is correct.

── FIXED 168c887 ──

The entry's suspicion was right and its pointer landed on the exact line. The
interpreter's move-out sets are keyed by BINDING NAME with no scope component,
so every site that rebinds a name has to RE-ARM it —
`rearm_container_bodies_for_name` exists for precisely that. `StmtKind::Let`
called it, `StmtKind::Assign` called it, and a MATCH ARM did not. One call
added at the arm's bind site (`interpreter/pattern_match.rs`, right after
`bind_pattern`) closes it.

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly as filed. Two programs differing only in the second
arm's binding name:

    second binding `q`   interp: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end   aot: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end
    second binding `r`   interp: pay4 D4 pay6 end      aot: pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end
                                          ^^ D6 gone

After the fix both spellings print `pay4 D4 pay6 D6 end` on interp and AOT.

WHY IT WAS ONLY THE CONTAINER-PUSH MOVE, which the entry's prefix bisect had
already narrowed and which this explains: the let-RHS and aggregate-literal
move recorders run at sites that also REBIND, so their records were re-armed
incidentally by the `let` path. The push/insert consuming-arg record is made
inside a match arm, which had no re-arm at all, so its record was the only one
that could outlive its block.

THE TEST PINS BOTH SPELLINGS, not just the broken one
(`tests/interpreter.rs::match_arm_rebinding_a_moved_name_still_runs_its_drop_body`).
Pinning only the reused-name case would pass against a fix that broke the
distinct-name control, and asserting one output would not express the actual
invariant, which is that the two must be EQUAL — a binding's name must not
change observable drop behaviour.

WORTH KEEPING from the entry, because it generalises past this bug: the defect
surfaced as a 7-case E2E that was parity-equal case-by-case and diverged only
when the cases were COMBINED. A test that passes in isolation and fails in
combination is the signature of leaked per-name interpreter state, and it is a
standing argument against reusing one convenient binding name across the cases
of a multi-case pin.

title: ICE: destructuring a heap-BOXED Option/Result payload with a STRUCT sub-pattern (`match o { Some(Full { name, buf }) => .. }`) panics the compiler with `ExtractOutOfRange` -- `build_extract_value` runs against the Option aggregate instead of the deboxed payload
detail: REPRO (probes b228/y1 named scrutinee, b228/y2 fresh temp -- BOTH panic, so it is not a scrutinee-shape gap): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` (6 words, BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area), then `match o { Option.Some(Full { name, buf }) => { println(name); println(buf.len()); } Option.None => {} }`.  `karac build` aborts with `thread panicked at src/codegen/pattern_binding.rs: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ExtractOutOfRange` -- a compiler CRASH on a well-typed program, not a diagnostic. `karac check` is clean, so nothing warns first.  CONTROL (probe b228/y3): the same destructure over an INLINE payload (`struct Narrow { name: String }`, 3 words) compiles and runs clean on both backends. BOXING is the discriminator, as everywhere else in this family.  SITE: the `PatternKind::Struct` arm of `bind_pattern_values`. An earlier branch handles the INLINE payload by extracting the enum aggregate's payload WORDS and reconstructing each field; a boxed payload falls past it to the plain struct-destructure fallback, which does `build_extract_value(sv, idx, "field")` with `sv` still being the `Option` aggregate `{tag, w0, w1, w2}` and `idx` a field index into `Full`. The fallback assumes `scrut` is already the payload struct value. The boxed path never deboxes -- w0 holds the box POINTER, and the fields have to be loaded through it.  NOTE that `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` exists and is written specifically for this shape (it cap-zeroes the consumed fields INSIDE the box so the box drop skips them). That suppressor is therefore unreachable today for a whole-struct destructure of a boxed payload: codegen panics before it can matter. Whoever fixes the debox should check that the suppressor then does the right thing, and that the partial form (`Some(Full { name, buf: _ })`, probe b228/x4, same panic) leaves the UNBOUND field owned by the box.  PRE-EXISTING and independently attributed: the same panic reproduces with `src/` checked out at e51d795, this session's base commit (same site, line 1320 there vs 1401 at 604f765 -- the shift is purely from insertions above it).  HOW IT SURFACED: while probing the wildcard-payload leak (B-2026-08-04-3), whose row asked whoever fixes it to also check partial struct sub-patterns. Those probes never got as far as running.  DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION (2026-08-04, same day, before any fix attempt). This row's SITE paragraph says the boxed path "never deboxes". That is too strong and would send the next attempt down the wrong road. Reading the code, the debox machinery is all present and looks like it should fire for this shape:  (1) `reconstruct_payload_value` has an explicit debox arm gated on `want > field_words.len() && !field_words.is_empty()` -- it inttoptrs word 0, loads `pattern_payload_llvm_type(sub_pat)` through it, and re-splits via `coerce_to_payload_words`.  (2) `pattern_payload_word_count` HAS a `PatternKind::Struct` arm that returns the named struct's full LLVM word count (added for the "Undefined variable" class), so `want` should be 6 for `Full`, not the 1-word default.  (3) `pattern_payload_llvm_type` HAS a matching `PatternKind::Struct` arm, so the load should produce a real `Full` value.  With all three in place `want`(6) > `field_words.len()`(3) ought to hold and the Struct bind arm ought to receive a 2-field `Full` StructValue, on which `build_extract_value(sv, 0|1)` is in range. It panics anyway, so ONE of those three is not doing what its code reads like for this scrutinee -- e.g. `field_words` arriving longer than 3, `want` resolving to something small because the path segment is not found in `struct_types` at that point, or this Struct sub-pattern reaching `bind_pattern_values` by a route that never calls `reconstruct_payload_value` at all.  START BY INSTRUMENTING rather than by adding a debox: print `want`, `field_words.len()` and the incoming `scrut` type at the Struct arm for probe b228/y1. The answer is which of the three is lying, and the fix follows from that. Adding a second debox path without knowing would likely double-load.  ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-08-04, instrumented per the note above; partial fix written, measured, then REVERTED unfinished -- nothing landed). It is a NAME COLLISION, not a debox gap at all. `variant_pattern_enum_name` resolves a bare single-segment path by searching variant names across every known enum INCLUDING THE PRELUDE'S, and the prelude declares `enum ChannelError { Full, .. }`. So the user's `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }`, destructured as `Full { name, buf }`, resolves to `Some("ChannelError")`. Measured directly: `[B5] reconstruct kind=Struct["Full"] want=1 field_words=3 enum_name=Some("ChannelError") in_struct_types=Some(true)`.  BOTH payload-sizing arms then take their enum branch, miss `enum_layouts` for `ChannelError`, and fall to their defaults -- `pattern_payload_word_count` to 1 and `pattern_payload_llvm_type` to i64. With `want`=1 the debox predicate `want > field_words.len()` (1 > 3) is FALSE, so no debox happens; `coerce_to_payload_words` builds a `{ i64 }`, and the Struct bind arm's `build_extract_value(sv, 1)` on a 1-field aggregate is the `ExtractOutOfRange`. Every step of the earlier diagnosis-correction was right that the debox machinery is fine -- it simply never gets asked.  This is the same CLASS as B-2026-08-03-5 (a user type whose name collided with a generic enum's PARAMETER name gained a phantom Drop walker). Renaming the struct to anything the prelude does not use as a variant name makes the program compile, which is the one-line bisect.  PARTIAL FIX, measured but NOT landed: adding a `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct(path)` predicate (single segment AND present in `struct_types`) and guarding the enum branch of BOTH sizing arms with it moves `want` from 1 to 6 and makes the debox fire (`[B5] want=6 fw=3`). The ICE PERSISTS at the same bind site even so, so there is a SECOND consumer downstream still handing a `{ i64 }` -- or re-deriving the wrong type -- after reconstruction. Next step is to re-print the Struct arm's incoming `scrut.get_type()` with the two sizing arms fixed: if it is still `{ i64 }`, the reconstruction path for a Struct sub-pattern is not rebuilding the aggregate; if it is a proper `Full`, the panic has moved to a different index computation.  The two-arm guard is a prerequisite either way and is the right shape -- it just is not sufficient alone. Whoever picks this up should reapply it first, then instrument the bind site.  ALSO WORTH CHECKING once it compiles: `variant_pattern_enum_name` is consulted from many other sites, so the same prelude-variant collision may mis-route decisions beyond these two. A user `struct Full`, `Empty`, `Closed` (or any other prelude variant name) is the general hazard, and a targeted audit of that fn's callers is probably worth more than this one ICE.  THIRD AND FINAL NARROWING (2026-08-04, measured, still not landed). With the two-arm guard applied so `want`=6 and the debox fires, the Struct bind arm STILL receives `{ i64 }`: `[B5-bind] Full scrut=StructType("{ i64 }")`. So `reconstruct_payload_value` is not packing the deboxed words back into the payload struct's aggregate -- it has an explicit `PatternKind::Tuple` arm that rebuilds a tuple element-by-element, and NO `PatternKind::Struct` counterpart, so a struct sub-pattern falls through to the single-word default no matter how many words the debox produced.  THE FIX IS THEREFORE TWO PARTS, both needed, neither sufficient alone: (1) the `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct` guard on both sizing arms, so `want` and the LLVM type are right and the debox runs; and (2) a `PatternKind::Struct` arm in `reconstruct_payload_value` that packs `field_words` into the struct's LLVM aggregate field-by-field, mirroring the Tuple arm right above it (walk the struct's field types, slice the words per field width, `insertvalue` each). With both, the bind arm receives a real 2-field `Full` and the extract is in range.  Everything above was measured on probe b229/y1 with temporary instrumentation; nothing was committed. The remaining work is writing part (2), then the usual verification -- and note the INLINE control (b228/y3) already works, so whatever the new arm does must leave the non-boxed path byte-identical.  CORRECTION TO THE PRECEDING PARAGRAPH (same session, on further reading): part (2) is NOT "add a `PatternKind::Struct` arm to `reconstruct_payload_value`". One effectively exists already -- `binding_is_struct` there is explicitly true for a `PatternKind::Struct` whose path names a `struct_types` entry (the slice-3t 1-word-struct case), and with the sizing guard in place `want_words` is 6, so the `(want_words <= 1 || field_words.len() <= 1) && !binding_is_struct` single-word gate is NOT taken and control reaches the multi-word struct-building path below it.  So the remaining defect is INSIDE that multi-word struct-building path: with `want`=6, the debox firing and the single-word gate bypassed, the Struct bind arm still receives `{ i64 }` (measured: `[B5-bind] Full scrut=StructType("{ i64 }")`). Read that path next -- it is the code immediately after the `want_words` gate in `reconstruct_payload_value` -- and find where it derives the aggregate type it builds into. The suspicion is that it re-derives from something that still resolves `Full` through the enum-variant route rather than from `pattern_payload_llvm_type`, in which case the guard needs applying at a third site; but that is UNVERIFIED and should be measured, not assumed.  Part (1) -- the `struct_pattern_path_is_user_struct` guard on both sizing arms -- remains verified and necessary: it demonstrably moves `want` from 1 to 6. Reapply it first.  AUDIT of `variant_pattern_enum_name`'s callers (2026-08-04, read-only; this is the broader item the row asked for).  COLLISION SURFACE. The fn never consults `struct_types` at all. Its order is: qualified `E.V` -> the match scrutinee's enum hint -> ANY enum carrying that variant name, preferring user enums but FALLING BACK TO SEEDED ones. So a bare name that is a user STRUCT resolves to a prelude enum whenever no user enum claims it. The seeded variant names, from the 14 enums registered in `declarations.rs` (`seeded_enum_names`), are: AlreadyExists, Array, Bool, Display, Env, Equal, Full, Greater, IncompleteSequence, Int, InteriorNul, Interrupted, InvalidByte, InvalidUtf8, Less, None, NotFound, NotPresent, NotUnicode, Null, Number, Object, Other, PermissionDenied, Some, String, Timeout, UnexpectedEof. Several are entirely plausible user struct names -- `Display`, `Object`, `Number`, `Int`, `Timeout`, `NotFound`, `Full`, `Other`, `Env`.  17 CALL SITES, classified:  (a) CONFIRMED HARMFUL -- the six inside `pattern_payload_word_count` (3 arms) and `pattern_payload_llvm_type` (3 arms). These recurse over SUB-patterns, so `Some(Display { .. })` reaches them, and a mis-resolve silently yields the 1-word / i64 default. That is this row's ICE.  (b) NARROW BY VARIANT NAME -- `compile_match`'s scrutinee-shape derivations and `set_scrutinee_shape_flags_for_pattern` (5 sites) only act on the answer when it is literally "Option" or "Result", so they can only misfire for a user type named `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Err`. Implausible but not impossible, and the failure would be a wrong payload-area/boxing classification -- i.e. the same memory-corruption family this session spent the day on, not a crash.  (c) SELF-CORRECTING BY ACCIDENT -- `bind_pattern_values` (1 site) takes the enum branch but then looks up `enum_variant_struct_field_names(enum, variant)`, which returns None for a unit variant, so it falls through to the struct path. Right answer, wrong reason; a seeded enum that ever gains a STRUCT variant of the same name would turn this into a silent mis-bind.  (d) GATED ON A SUBSEQUENT LOOKUP -- the four freshtemp/shared-enum trackers (`materialize_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee`, `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee`, `track_freshtemp_shared_option_scrutinee`, `drop_freshtemp_enum_scrutinee_on_miss`) each require the resolved name to pass a further test (an Option/Result area, a `shared_types` entry, a drop-kind layout) that a mis-resolve fails, so they decline rather than misfire. Declining is a LEAK on the safe side, not a corruption -- but it means a user `struct Full` silently loses its box tracking, which is exactly the shape of B-2026-08-04-3.  RECOMMENDATION, which supersedes this row's two-site guard: put the struct preference INSIDE `variant_pattern_enum_name`, not at the call sites. One site instead of six, and it fixes classes (a) and (d) together. Restrict it to `PatternKind::Struct` (leave TupleVariant and Binding alone -- a bare `Int(v)` tuple-variant pattern must still resolve through the scrutinee hint) and place it AFTER the qualified and scrutinee-hint checks, so `match tok { Int(v) => .. }` with both `enum Token { Int }` and `struct Int` in scope keeps binding to `Token`. A `PatternKind::Struct` whose single-segment path names a `struct_types` entry is unambiguously a struct destructure -- there is no syntax where it means a unit variant.  NOT DONE HERE: the audit is read-only. No code changed.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 9908f6a). The final narrowing above was right that the collision is the whole story, and WRONG about where the third site was: the multi-word struct-building path in `reconstruct_payload_value` is fine. `reconstruct_payload_value` never reached it -- the `enum_layout_type_for_variant_pattern` branch ABOVE the single-word gate returns early, and it resolves through `variant_pattern_enum_and_tag`, a SECOND copy of the same bare-name scan that `variant_pattern_enum_name` has. `ChannelError`'s unit-only layout is literally `{ i64 }`, which is exactly the aggregate the bind arm was measured receiving. Guarding one resolver and instrumenting downstream of the other is why the earlier attempts kept finding the same `{ i64 }` in a new place.  SHIPPED SHAPE, per the audit's recommendation: one predicate, `struct_pattern_names_a_user_struct` -- a `PatternKind::Struct` whose single-segment path names a `struct_types` entry and whose name the match scrutinee's own enum does not claim -- consulted from THREE sites rather than guarding six callers: both resolvers (after their qualified and scrutinee-hint checks) and the arm-CONDITION guard in `compile_match`. That third site was not in the audit and had to be found by probing: it uses `enum_tag_for_variant`, a third bare-name lookup with no struct awareness, so with only the two resolvers guarded a plain `struct Item` scrutinee matched by `Item { a }` (with `enum Holder { Item { .. } }` in scope) stopped ICE-ing and started tag-comparing the struct's first field against `Holder.Item`'s tag, falling through every arm and returning junk -- an ICE traded for a SILENT WRONG ANSWER. Probe b230/y6a; the fix covers it, and b230/y6b (the same bare name over a scrutinee that IS the enum) proves the scrutinee-hint escape keeps the variant reading.  The `PatternKind::Struct` restriction is deliberate and load-bearing: a bare `Int(v)` TupleVariant pattern must still resolve through the scrutinee hint when a `struct Int` is in scope, and no syntax spells a unit variant as `Name { .. }`.  AUDIT CLASSES (a) and (d) are both closed by this -- the six sizing-arm callers and the four freshtemp/shared trackers all go through one of the two resolvers. Class (b) (the five Option/Result-literal comparisons) and class (c) (`bind_pattern_values`' self-correcting lookup) were assessed as safe and are unchanged.  VERIFIED on probes b230/y1..y10 and t1..t3: named scrutinee, fresh temp, `Result`'s Err half, partial destructure (`buf: _` and `..`), if-let, while-let over `Vec.pop`, the INLINE 3-word control, a plain-struct scrutinee, and all three collision tiers -- every one correct, AOT/interp parity-EQUAL, valgrind 0. Targeted suites green.  SUPPRESSOR NOTE, answering this row's own question: with the debox now firing, `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` is reachable for the first time and the leaf bindings own the interior exactly once -- pinned under ASAN/LSan.  RESIDUAL FOUND AND FILED SEPARATELY (B-2026-08-04-6): a FRESH-TEMP scrutinee whose struct destructure leaves the `Vec` field UNBOUND leaks that buffer. Kept OUT of the ASAN pin so LeakSanitizer does not attribute it there.
fix: 9908f6a (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs; pins codegen.rs::e2e_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_deboxes and ::e2e_struct_pattern_wins_over_a_same_named_enum_variant, both stash-proven RED with the exact `ExtractOutOfRange` ICE, their interpreter oracles interpreter.rs::test_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_deboxes and ::test_struct_pattern_wins_over_a_same_named_enum_variant, and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_owns_the_interior_once for the ownership side the debox made reachable)

title: A FRESH-TEMP boxed Option/Result scrutinee destructured by a PARTIAL struct sub-pattern (`match mk() { Some(Full { name, buf: _ }) => .. }`) leaks the unbound `Vec` field's buffer -- the box drop stays box-ONLY for any struct destructure, which is right when every field is bound and wrong when some are not
detail: REPRO (probes b230/p1, p2, p3 -- 32 bytes definitely lost under valgrind each, parity-EQUAL so no run-vs-build split): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }`, `fn opt(i: i64) -> Option[Full] { return Option.Some(mk(i)); }`, and `match opt(4i64) { Option.Some(Full { name, buf: _ }) => { println(name); } Option.None => {} }`. `Full` is 6 words, so it is BOXED at Option's 3-word payload area. The `..` spelling (`Full { name, .. }`, p2) and the `Result` Err-side twin (p3) leak identically.  CLEAN CONTROLS, which is what localizes it: the NAMED-scrutinee twin (p6 -- `let o: Option[Full] = ...; match o { ... }`) is vg=0; the FULL destructure from a fresh temp (p5) is vg=0; and the whole-binding form is vg=0. So it is specifically fresh-temp + partial.  MECHANISM: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` derives `inner_struct_name` from the payload sub-pattern. A `PatternKind::Struct` destructure falls into the `_ => None` arm and the free goes box-ONLY. That arm is CORRECT for a FULL destructure -- each leaf binding owns and frees its field, so walking the interior would double-free -- and it is what B-2026-08-04-3 deliberately left alone when it split the WILDCARD case out. A PARTIAL destructure is the third case neither answer fits: some fields are owned by bindings, the rest by nobody. Fixing it needs a FIELD-SELECTIVE walker (free exactly the unbound fields), not a whole-struct one -- that is why it is not a one-line extension of the wildcard arm.  THE "STRING IS CLEAN" ASYMMETRY IS AN ARTIFACT -- resolved, do not chase it. First pass observed that only an unbound `Vec` field leaks: probe p7 (`Full { name: _, buf }`, with a deliberately long f-string) and p9 (a 3-field `Two` with the middle `String` unbound) were both vg=0, which read like something already owning an unbound String. It does not. Valgrind's ALLOCATION COUNT gives it away: p5 (both fields bound) does 5 allocs, p7 does 3. The String was never allocated -- nothing in the whole program ever reads that field, so LLVM elides the malloc outright, and an allocation that does not happen cannot leak. This is the same dead-allocation false-negative that has misled this bug family twice before.  DECISIVE PROBE b230/p10: same shape, but the String is built by mutation (`String.new()` + two `push_str`, the second from an f-string) so the buffer is genuinely materialized, and the struct is padded to 6 words with scalars so boxing does not depend on the String's width. Result: 4 allocs / 3 frees, 76 bytes DEFINITELY LOST. An unbound `String` field leaks exactly like an unbound `Vec` field.  So the rule is uniform and the fix does not need a per-field-type carve-out: for a fresh-temp scrutinee, EVERY field the struct pattern leaves unbound is unowned. A field-selective walker over the unbound set is the whole fix. Corollary for whoever writes it: any probe here MUST force the allocation (mutate the buffer, or read it) or a broken fix will measure clean.  MECHANISM CONFIRMED, and it explains the named-vs-fresh split exactly: the NAMED path already handles this. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure` walks the struct pattern's fields and skips any `field: _` sub-pattern with the comment "the box keeps that field" -- so bound fields get their cap zeroed inside the box and unbound ones stay owned by the box's inner-struct walker. That suppressor bails at its first line for a fresh temp, because it requires `ExprKind::Identifier` for the scrutinee. The fresh-temp side has no equivalent: `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` decides whole-interior vs box-only from the sub-pattern KIND alone and has no third option. Porting the named path's per-field decision to the fresh-temp tracker is the shape to aim for.  PRE-EXISTING in the sense that matters: the shape did not COMPILE before 9908f6a (it ICE'd -- B-2026-08-04-5), so this leak has never shipped in a working program. It is nonetheless a genuine gap in the box-drop ownership model, not a regression from that fix, which changed only name resolution.  ORACLE NOTE: invisible to parity diffing and to fire counting -- AOT and `karac run` print the same thing -- so only valgrind/LSan sees it. Deliberately kept OUT of `memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_boxed_optres_payload_struct_destructure_owns_the_interior_once` (whose partial case is the clean NAMED-scrutinee twin) so LSan does not attribute this row's leak to that pin.  SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while verifying B-2026-08-04-5's fix, which is what made the shape compilable and therefore measurable at all -- and which is what B-2026-08-04-3's scope note predicted would happen.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 7ecdec0). Shipped as the shape this row's own mechanism note pointed at: the NAMED path's per-field split, ported to the fresh temp rather than reinvented. `suppress_boxed_payload_struct_destructure`'s body is now shared; a fresh-temp entry point takes the box slot `track_freshtemp_boxed_enum_scrutinee` already stages (the same `__freshtemp_boxed_scrut` alloca B-2026-08-04-3 started returning), and the tracker gained a `PatternKind::Struct` arm that walks the WHOLE interior. The two halves meet in the middle: the suppressor cap-zeroes every BOUND field inside the box before the walk can reach it, so per field the binding frees what it took and the box frees the rest. All-fields-bound degenerates exactly to the old box-only behavior -- every cap zeroed, walk is a no-op -- which is what makes the tracker arm safe to apply unconditionally rather than only to partial patterns.  ONE TIGHTENING BEYOND THE ROW, and it is UNPROVEN: the disarm condition was `Wildcard`-only, so a field the pattern merely TESTS (`Full { name: "x", buf }`) was disarmed with nothing taking ownership -- a leak by the same argument. It now asks whether the sub-pattern binds anything, via a codegen-local `pattern_binds_anything` mirroring the `use_classifier` one. This is a correctness tightening on BOTH paths, but probe b230/p11 (a literal-test on a String field, named scrutinee) is vg=0 at base too, so no program was found where the old condition observably leaked. Recorded as reasoning, not as a measured fix.  VERIFIED: 25 probes (b230/p1..p11, t1..t3, y1..y10) -- all correct, AOT/interp parity-EQUAL, valgrind 0. The four that leaked at base are the load-bearing ones: p1 (`buf: _`), p2 (`..`), p3 (`Result` Err side) at 32 bytes each, and p10 (the non-elidable String half) at 76. Suites: codegen 2777, memory_sanitizer 925, interpreter 1440, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5381 passed, 0 failed.  THE PIN CARRIES THIS ROW'S PROBE-HYGIENE WARNING IN ITS FIXTURE, not just its comment: both `String`s are built by MUTATION and every bound field is read, because an unread field's malloc is elided outright (5 allocs vs 3, measured) and an elided allocation cannot leak. A lazier fixture passes against a completely broken fix. Stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer at 19,200 bytes.
fix: 7ecdec0 (src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs, src/codegen/control_flow.rs; pins memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_freshtemp_boxed_payload_partial_destructure_owns_every_field, stash-proven RED under LeakSanitizer at 19,200 bytes, covering `field: _`, `..`, the String half, the `Result` Err side, and an all-fields-bound control for the double-free direction)
4c52d82 (src/cli.rs; no new test -- the 36 pre-existing `tests/cli.rs` cases were the RED signal and are the pin: 524 passed / 36 failed before, 560 passed / 0 failed after)
title: EVERY project-mode `karac build` fails immediately: it opens the PACKAGE NAME as a source path (`error: cannot read 'solo'`), so a manifest-driven build cannot run at all -- 36 tests/cli.rs cases fail on main
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while running the full suite to verify B-2026-08-03-12. Not caused by that
change -- `tests/cli.rs` fails 524 passed / 36 failed identically with and without it (the
change was stashed and the suite re-run to confirm).

REPRODUCTION, by hand, four lines:

    mkdir -p /tmp/p/src
    printf '[package]\nname = "solo"\n' > /tmp/p/kara.toml
    printf 'fn main() {}\n'              > /tmp/p/src/main.kara
    cd /tmp/p && karac build
    error: cannot read 'solo': No such file or directory (os error 2)

That fixture is copied verbatim from
`test_build_offline_no_deps_project_succeeds_without_vendor`, so it is the contract the suite
itself asserts.

BLAST RADIUS IS ALL OF PROJECT MODE, not the offline path the failing test names:

    karac build              -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac build --offline    -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac build --release    -> cannot read 'solo'
    karac check              -> "missing file argument"   (separate: project mode unsupported)

`strace` confirms the literal package name is opened relative to CWD, once:

    openat(AT_FDCWD, "solo", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT

so the manifest IS found and parsed -- `solo` is its `[package] name` -- and the failure is
downstream, where the package name reaches a slot expecting a source path. The message comes
from `read_source` (src/cli.rs:911), which `process::exit(1)`s, so the build dies before any
compilation. Arg parsing is NOT at fault: with no positional the parser correctly produces
`Command::BuildProject` (src/cli/args.rs, `match file { Some(f) => Build, None =>
BuildProject }`). The read site is deeper than `cmd_build_project`'s prologue; that is where
to start.

WHY HIGH: project mode is the manifest-driven build path -- the only way to compile a
multi-file package -- and it is not degraded but completely non-functional, on the default
invocation, with an error that names a package rather than a path so it reads as user error.

NOT BISECTED. Main advanced by roughly sixty commits during this session and rebuilding at
candidate parents was not affordable here; `fac3bf2` ("honor -o/--out for executable builds")
is the nearest suspect by area, but its subject is an OUTPUT path while this is a READ, so
treat it as unverified. Bisecting is the first thing worth doing.

Related: B-2026-08-03-12 (the entry whose verification run surfaced this).

FIXED (2026-08-04, 4c52d82) -- and BISECTED, which this row asked for first. The suspect named above (`fac3bf2`, `-o`/`--out` handling) is NOT it; the row's own instinct that an OUTPUT-path change is the wrong shape for a READ failure was right. The introducing commit is d166203 (B-2026-08-03-9, the `map_value_clone_reinsert` lint), same day.

MECHANISM. That lint's checks and its fix-it rewrite both reproduce the author's own spelling by span, so it genuinely needs the source text. It got it by adding `let source = read_source(&self.filename);` to the TAIL of `Pipeline::typecheck` -- which is why the read site is "deeper than `cmd_build_project`'s prologue" as the row predicted: it is not in `cmd_build_project` at all, it is in the shared Pipeline that `run_multi_file_codegen` drives. That function hand-constructs its Pipeline with `filename: mf.name.clone()` over a super-program stitched from every module, so `filename` is the package NAME by design. `read_source` hard-exits on any IO error, hence the single `openat(AT_FDCWD, "solo")` the row's strace caught and the immediate death.

THE FIX. The text was already in hand and being discarded -- `Pipeline::new(filename, source)` receives it. It is now kept on the struct as `source: Option<String>` and the lint reads that instead of touching the filesystem: correct, and one fewer full-file read per typecheck. Project mode passes `None` and the lint sits out; slicing spans against a stand-in string would have been worse than not running.

KNOWN GAP, deliberate and noted at the field: `map_value_clone_reinsert` does not run in project mode. It never has -- before d166203 the lint did not exist, and after it the build died -- so this is a coverage follow-up, not a regression. Running it project-wide needs the per-module source texts threaded to the super-program pipeline.

VERIFIED: this row's own four-line fixture builds and runs; `tests/cli.rs` goes 524 passed / 36 failed -> 560 passed / 0 failed. No new test -- the 36 cases were already the right pin.

PROCESS NOTE, the more transferable lesson and a second vote for what this row already observed: the tests that caught this ALREADY EXISTED and already covered the shape. Nothing new was needed. The gap was that `tests/cli.rs` went unrun between d166203 and here -- a session doing contained codegen work runs codegen / memory_sanitizer / interpreter, and `cli` is not in that set. Both sessions that hit this found it the same way: a full suite run for an unrelated reason. A green targeted run is evidence about its targets, not about the tree.

CROSS-SESSION NOTE: filed by one session and fixed by another working the same open list; the two reproductions were independent and identical.

fix: e94e6bd9 (slice 1, intra-function converging+base skip) + 55f3d4a3 (slice 2, length pin survives passing the Vec to a free function). Residual callee-side gap split to B-2026-08-05-6.
title: Bounds-check elimination fails for the CONVERGING two-pointer loop `while lo <= hi { v[base+lo] ... v[base+hi] }` when the index carries a base offset — the flat-2D / row-major scan shape. Isolated on kata #246 (strobogrammatic two-pointer over a flat Vec[u8] corpus of N*LEN bytes): kara keeps 2 per-iteration checks that clang -O3 does not, costing 1.28x on the kata and 1.93x on a work-identical minimal probe. Neither ingredient alone breaks BCE — base+ascending, base+descending, converging-without-base, and even both-ends-from-ONE-ascending-IV all elide cleanly; only the combination of a base offset with a converging two-IV guard defeats it.
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: LeetCode #246 Strobogrammatic Number, bench lane; found while root-causing the kata's residual 1.30x vs C. Filed after the hypothesis recorded in the #246 README (kara-katas 4645548) was CONFIRMED by disassembly + a controlled experiment.

EVIDENCE 1 - the two loops are isomorphic except for bounds checks. Both binaries fully inline is_strobogrammatic into main (x86 container, karac AOT KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 vs clang -O3 -march=x86-64-v3). kara's punch loop is 21 instructions, C's is 15. The 6-instruction excess is EXACTLY 2 x (lea; cmp $0x9c400; jae <panic>) - i.e. 100% bounds checking; every other instruction matches one-for-one, including the 5-way rotate map, which LLVM table-izes identically in both (movzbl digit; add $0xd0; cmp $0x9; ja; bt <mask 0x343>; jae; table load). So this is NOT a rotate-map, string-layout, or codegen-quality gap - the earlier suspects (5-way if-chain not table-ized; scattered String corpus) were both ruled out.

EVIDENCE 2 - controlled experiment pins the cost. Added Kara-equivalent bounds checks to the C mirror (absolute index base+lo / base+hi, unsigned compare against total length, branch to abort). clang compiles that to a loop instruction-for-instruction ISOMORPHIC to kara's (21 insns, same order; only register allocation and the rotate table's element width differ). hyperfine 80 runs, min: C 65.1ms, C+bounds-checks 83.2ms (1.28x), kara 83.0ms (1.28x). kara is statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE from equal-safety C - so on this kata karac's codegen is at clang -O3 parity once safety is equalized, and the whole residual gap is the missing BCE.

EVIDENCE 3 - minimal probes isolate the exact trigger. Five variants, identical corpus (Vec.filled(20000*32), LCG-filled, loop-carried acc*131 sink so nothing hoists), differing ONLY in the scan loop; count of `cmp $0x9c400` (the length constant) in main:
  A  base+ASCENDING      `while lo < len { v[base+lo] }`                                -> 0 checks  (BCE fires)
  B  base+CONVERGING     `while lo <= hi { v[base+lo]; v[base+hi] }`                    -> 2 checks  (BCE FAILS)
  C  CONVERGING, no base `while lo <= hi { v[lo]; v[hi] }`                              -> 0 checks  (BCE fires)
  D  base+DESCENDING     `while hi >= 0 { v[base+hi] }`                                 -> 0 checks  (BCE fires)
  E  base, both ends from ONE ascending IV `while lo+lo < len { v[base+lo]; v[base+len-1-lo] }` -> 0 checks (BCE fires)
E is the decisive one: it performs the SAME memory accesses as B, at the same base offset, with the same trip count, and returns the SAME value (-607711579) - it differs only in deriving both indices from a single ascending induction variable instead of two converging ones. E: 28.1ms, B: 54.2ms => the missing BCE alone costs 1.93x on a work-identical program. (#246 shows only 1.28x because its loop body does more per iteration, diluting the check.)

WHY THE EXISTING MACHINERY MISSES IT. B-2026-06-16-1 covers binary-search `mid`; the canonical forward `j < v.len()` is covered (probe A, and #246's own fill loop, both elide); B-2026-07-17-1 (6474a73) added bce_length_pin.rs `compute_descending_skips` for the descending in-place rolling-DP shape (probe D elides). The uncovered case is the CONVERGING guard: two independent monotone IVs whose relation to the length is established only jointly (lo <= hi <= len-1, base = i*STRIDE, i < N, v.len() == N*STRIDE). The descending skip proves `k <= k_init < B_pin <= len` for a SINGLE index whose init is linear in an enclosing loop var; here `hi`'s bound is the co-moving `lo`, and the indexed expression is the SUM `base + hi` rather than a bare loop var, so neither the UpperBound guard path nor the monotone-assume tier produces a usable fact. NOTE the sum matters independently: probe C (converging, bare index) DOES elide, so a converging guard alone is fine - it is `base + {lo,hi}` under a converging guard that fails. FIX DIRECTION: extend the length-pin skip to the row-major shape - when v's length is pinned to N*STRIDE (Vec.filled / a counted fill), the offset is `i*STRIDE` with the enclosing loop bounding `i < N`, and an inner index j satisfies `0 <= j <= STRIDE-1` (from a converging or counted guard), then `base + j <= (N-1)*STRIDE + STRIDE-1 = N*STRIDE-1 < len` by the same linear-normal-form cancellation compute_descending_skips already uses. Push UpperBound facts for BOTH indices through the existing asserted_index_bounds channel. Soundness-critical (a wrong skip is an OOB): needs the full codegen-E2E + memory_sanitizer x86 AND arm64 gates.

BREADTH: this is the flat/row-major 2D array traversal shape (matrix scans, fixed-stride record buffers, per-row palindrome and two-pointer checks), so it recurs well beyond #246 - #246's own CONSTRUCTION loop (`corpus[base+lo] = ...; corpus[base+hi] = ...`) is the same shape and also keeps its checks (5 total `cmp $0x9c400` sites in main: 3 in construction, 2 in the punch loop). NOT a correctness issue - the checks are sound, just not elided. NOT worked around in the kata: #246 stays written as the natural converging two-pointer; probe E is diagnostic evidence only and must NOT be taken as a kata rewrite.

── FINDING 484c2c9 (row stays OPEN; the entry's FIX DIRECTION needs one correction) ──

REPRODUCED EXACTLY AS FILED, on this x86 container: probe B keeps 2
`cmp $0x9c400` sites in the punch loop, probe E keeps 0, and both print the
same value on the same corpus — so the two are work-identical and the checks
are the whole difference, as the entry says.

THE CORRECTION IS ABOUT WHERE THE FIX CAN GO. The entry's FIX DIRECTION is to
extend `compute_descending_skips`'s length-pin reasoning to the row-major
shape, pushing UpperBound facts through `asserted_index_bounds`. That works for
a scan written INLINE — and #246's own CONSTRUCTION loop is exactly that, so 2
of its 5 checks are reachable this way (the inner converging pair; the third
construction check is `corpus[base + pos]` with `pos = (state/65536) % len`,
which needs modulo-range reasoning, not this). It cannot reach the punch loop,
which is the 1.28x the entry is actually about:

    fn is_strobogrammatic(corpus: ref Vec[u8], base: i64, len: i64) -> bool {
        let mut lo = 0i64;
        let mut hi = len - 1i64;
        while lo <= hi { ... corpus[base + lo] ... corpus[base + hi] ... }
    }

`corpus`, `base` and `len` are all PARAMETERS. There is no fill loop, no
enclosing counter, and no length pin in this function — and `base + lo <
corpus.len()` is not intra-procedurally TRUE. It holds only because every
caller passes `base = k*len` with `k < n` and `corpus.len() == n*len`. Every
analysis in `bce_length_pin.rs` runs per-function over `func.body`, so no
amount of extending it reaches this. Closing the punch loop needs an
inter-procedural fact (a callee precondition `base + len <= corpus.len()`
discharged at call sites), which is a different and much larger piece of work
than the entry scopes.

AND LLVM WILL NOT DO IT EITHER — the entry's own EVIDENCE 2 already proves
this, though it does not draw the conclusion. Adding Kara-equivalent bounds
checks to the C mirror produced a loop ISOMORPHIC to kara's, 21 instructions,
checks intact. That is clang -O3 with full visibility after inlining, declining
to eliminate them. So the "help LLVM see it" route is closed by the entry's own
measurement, and probes A/C/D/E elide because LLVM handles THOSE shapes (no
pin/skip of ours fires on any of them — `Vec.filled` produces no length pin,
and `lo <= hi` is not a guard `control_flow_bce.rs` reads a fact from), not
because it would handle this one given a nudge.

Stated precisely, because it is easy to overclaim from: a further C probe here
showed `__builtin_assume` on the two induction variables (`lo >= 0`,
`hi <= len-1`, `lo <= len-1`) does NOT recover the elision. That result is
weaker than it looks and is not itself evidence about the inlined case — the
probe function was `noinline`, so `base` was unconstrained and the checks were
genuinely necessary there. It rules out "IV-level assumes alone are enough",
nothing more. EVIDENCE 2 remains the load-bearing measurement.

ONE PREREQUISITE THE ENTRY DOES NOT MENTION: neither the kata nor the probes
would be reachable by the row-major skip as the machinery stands, because both
allocate with `Vec.filled(n * len, ..)` and `vec_length_lower_bounds` only
recognises `Vec.new()` / `Vec.with_capacity(..)` plus a counted PUSH fill. A
`Vec.filled(N, x)` length lower bound is a small, independently sound addition
and is a precondition for any of this firing on the shapes that motivated the
entry.

ALSO NOTE the affine limit: `base = i * stride` and `B_pin = n * stride` are
products of two identifiers, which `bound_to_linear` refuses (it is affine, not
polynomial). The cancellation the entry describes only closes if `stride` folds
to a literal first — true in #246 (`let len = 32i64`) and in the probes, but it
means constant-folding let-bound scalars is part of the work, not an
optimisation of it.

SCOPE RESTATED, then: the reachable win here is the INLINE row-major scan
(#246's construction loop, matrix/record-buffer scans written in one function),
not the kata's headline 1.28x. Worth doing, and worth filing under its real
scope rather than the entry's current framing.

METHOD NOTE, since it cost real time: timing this shape is corpus-size
dependent in a way that inverts the result. At n=400000 (12.8 MB, memory-bound)
probe B with 2 checks measured FASTER than probe E with none — the checks are
free when the loop is waiting on DRAM. The entry's 1.93x is a cache-resident
measurement (640 KB), and only that regime is informative about BCE.

PARTIAL FIX LANDED (e94e6bd9) — the intra-function shape now elides BOTH halves; the
reported kata does NOT yet benefit, and this entry stays OPEN for that reason.

WHAT NOW ELIDES. `bce_length_pin.rs::compute_converging_skips` recognises the
row-major converging shape {`Vec.filled(E, _)` or counted fill pinning
`v.len() >= B_pin`} + {enclosing `while i < N` / `for i in 0..N` bounding
`i <= u_max`} + {`let base = E_base(i)` linear and unwritten in the inner body}
+ {inner `while lo <= hi` / `lo < hi` with `hi` monotone non-increasing and
`lo`'s only writes trailing clean increments}, and proves
`B_pin - (E_base + hi_init)[i := u_max] >= 1` by the same linear-normal-form
cancellation `compute_descending_skips` uses. It pushes a NEW
`AssertedIndexBound::SumIndexBound { base_var, idx_var, vec_var, lower_proven }`
through the existing `asserted_index_bounds` channel — new because the index is
a SUM of two variables and so never decomposes into the bare-index /
constant-offset shape `UpperBound` is keyed on. `index_bounds_already_proven`
matches it in either operand order, covering reads and index-assign targets
through the one choke point.

TWO GATES ARE LOAD-BEARING AND BOTH ARE NEW HERE. (1) `lo`'s increments must
come AFTER every mention of `lo` in the body: unlike the descending case
(`k <= k_init` holds regardless of ordering), an ascending index stepped BEFORE
its use can exceed the bound the `lo <= hi` guard established, so skipping the
check there would be an OOB. (2) The LOWER half additionally needs the mirrored
gate on `hi` (a lower bound on a shrinking value is only valid before it
shrinks) plus a non-negative row origin, proven by evaluating `E_base + lo_init`
at the counter's MINIMUM. Both halves are gated independently: a body that steps
`hi` early still gets the upper skip and keeps the sign check.

CONST FOLDING WAS REQUIRED, not an optimisation. The row extent is typically
`let n = ..; let len = ..` literals, and `n * len` is NOT affine in `{n, len}`,
so `bound_to_linear` fails closed on the identity. `int_const_bindings`
substitutes integer-literal `let`s that are bound exactly once, never assigned,
and never mut-used, which makes the products affine. Note `stmt_writes_bound`
reports a `let x = ..` binding as a write to `x` — correct for its
"unwritten AFTER this point" use, but it rejects every candidate here, so the
scan uses a statement-VALUE-only variant (`mut_used_anywhere`).

MEASURED. A work-identical probe (single function, `Vec.filled(20000*32)`,
loop-carried sink): punch loop 17 -> 14 instructions, both bounds checks gone
(the surviving `jo`s are Kāra's overflow checks, which are equal-safety and
stay); 47.4ms -> 39.4ms = 1.20x, hyperfine 60 runs. Upper-only was 15
instructions / 1.12x, so the lower half is worth roughly half the win here.
`KARAC_BCE_CONV_SKIP=0` restores the checks exactly (A/B lever + escape hatch,
mirroring `KARAC_BCE_DESC_SKIP`).

WHY #246 ITSELF IS UNCHANGED (measured, not assumed — still 5 `cmp $len` sites
in `main`, output unchanged at 325454619). Two independent blockers:

  (a) The PUNCH loop lives in the callee `is_strobogrammatic(corpus, base, len)`.
      Inside it there is genuinely no local fact relating `base` to
      `corpus.len()`, so no intraprocedural analysis can prove the bound — this
      needs either interprocedural facts or loop predication (hoisting one
      widened check to the preheader, which changes WHERE a panicking program
      panics and so needs the IRCE-style safe-prefix split to stay
      semantics-preserving). karac's BCE analyses are per-function by
      construction, and the shape still fails post-inline: the hand-inlined
      probe reproduced the gap before this fix, which is why the fix exists at
      all.

  (b) The CONSTRUCTION loop IS the intra-function shape and would qualify, but
      the length pin refuses it: `vec_readonly_after` disqualifies any Vec that
      appears as a function ARGUMENT, and #246 passes `corpus` to
      `is_strobogrammatic`. Verified by isolation — adding a single read-only
      `fn peek(c: ref Vec[u8]) -> i64` call to the otherwise-firing probe puts
      both checks back. Relaxing that gate looks tractable (an argument NOT
      `mut`-marked cannot be a `mut ref` param per design.md Feature 4 Part 1.5,
      so it cannot resize; an owned-param move would make any later index site
      a use-after-move the ownership checker already rejects) but it is a
      SHARED gate the ascending and descending pins also rely on, and the
      construction loop runs once against the punch loop's 100 passes, so it
      would not move the kata's number. Deliberately not taken here.

So the honest scope of this fix: it closes the shape for programs that keep the
buffer local to the function that walks it, and leaves #246's own measurement
where it was. Kata README updated to say exactly that.

TESTS. 13 analysis unit tests (3 positive incl. index-assign targets, 10
negatives covering each gate one at a time — reordered step, non-monotone `hi`,
written `base`, row wider than the pin, counter rewritten before the inner loop,
unpinned/resized Vec, mutated bound identifier, plain single-index loop); 3
lower-half tests pinning the two halves as independently gated; 2 IR wiring
tests (skip fires -> NO `vidx.` block at all; reordered variant -> combined
check survives); 1 ASAN E2E with ODD-width rows and an exact-size corpus so
`base + hi_init` must land on the final element, reading AND writing every cell.
Every negative goes through a `mutate` helper that asserts its anchor matched —
a silently-missed `.replace()` had made one negative a vacuous pass during
development, which is the failure mode these tests exist to prevent.

2026-08-05 SECOND SLICE — blocker (b) CLEARED, blocker (a) REFUTED AS A PIPELINE FIX.

(b) FIXED: the length pin now tolerates the Vec being passed to a function. `vec_len_stable_after` used to route through `vec_readonly_after`, which disqualifies ANY occurrence of `v` that is not an index base or a `.len()`/`.is_empty()` receiver — so a single `is_strobogrammatic(corpus, base, len)` anywhere in the function killed the pin for every index site in it. It now routes through a relaxed twin (`expr_vec_len_stable`) that additionally accepts `v` as an UNMARKED argument to a FREE-FUNCTION call. Soundness rests on design.md Feature 4 Part 1.5: a free-function call writes the `mut` marker on any argument whose place-expression root is a fresh owned binding when the callee's parameter is `mut ref T` / `mut Slice[T]`, and every pinned `v` is exactly such a binding (introduced by `let v = Vec.new() / with_capacity() / filled()` in the same function — never a `mut ref` binding being forwarded, which is the one case the spec lets through unmarked). So a `mut ref` callee is impossible without the marker (and marked args are refused), a `ref` callee cannot resize, and an owned callee MOVES `v`, making any later index a use-after-move the ownership checker already rejects. METHOD-call arguments are deliberately NOT relaxed: method calls never write the marker (same design.md section), so an unmarked method argument proves nothing about the parameter's mode — pinned by a negative test. The ascending pin path (`compute_vec_length_pins`) still uses the STRICT `vec_readonly_after` and is byte-identical.

Effect on kata #246: bounds-check sites in `main` 5 -> 3 (the construction loop's `corpus[base+lo] = ..` / `corpus[base+hi] = ..` pair now elides; the third construction site is the corruption step OUTSIDE the converging loop and keeps its check). Output unchanged at 325454619. Wall clock 42.8ms -> 42.0ms = 1.02x, INSIDE NOISE and expected: construction runs once against the punch loop's 100 passes. So the kata's headline 1.28x is STILL unchanged — the value of this slice is unblocking the pin for the general 'hand the buffer to a helper' shape, not this measurement.

(a) STILL OPEN, and one candidate cheap fix is now RULED OUT. LLVM ships IRCE (inductive range-check elimination) and it is NOT in the `default<O2>` pipeline karac runs, so enabling it looked like a one-line win for the callee-side loop. Tested directly on #246's pre-opt IR with opt-18: `default<O2>` versus `default<O2>,function(loop-simplify,lcssa,irce),default<O2>` produce BYTE-IDENTICAL assembly (same md5, same 8 `$640000` compares). IRCE does not match this shape — the index is a SUM `base + j` and `j`'s range is fixed jointly by two co-moving IVs, not by one affine IV against a loop-invariant bound. So the remaining callee-side gap needs interprocedural facts or IRCE-style loop VERSIONING (a checked and an unchecked copy chosen by one preheader test — semantics-preserving, unlike naive predication which would move where a panicking program panics). Recorded so the pipeline-flag idea is not re-derived.

Tests added this slice: 3 analysis unit tests (fires through an unmarked free-function call; refuses a `mut`-marked argument; refuses a method argument). Both converging test helpers now assert the mutated source PARSES — a mutation that fails to parse yields no skips and would make every negative a vacuous pass, the same failure mode the `mutate` anchor assert exists for. Full `--features llvm` suite green: 101 binaries, 12,980 passed, 0 failed, 0 skips (codegen 2785, memory_sanitizer 929, par_codegen 229); clippy and fmt clean.

CLOSED 2026-08-05 (e94e6bd9 + 55f3d4a3). The shape this entry NAMES is done: a
converging two-pointer over a base-offset index, `while lo <= hi { v[base+lo];
v[base+hi] }`, now elides BOTH halves, including when the buffer is handed to a
helper function. Probe B — the entry's own repro — goes from 2 checks to 0, its
punch loop from 17 instructions to 14, and runs 1.20x faster. Kata #246's
CONSTRUCTION loop, the second shape the entry called out, goes from 3 check
sites to 1; the survivor is `corpus[base + pos]` with `pos = (state/65536) %
len`, which needs modulo-range reasoning and is a different problem.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. Kata #246's headline 1.28x vs
equal-safety C is UNCHANGED by both slices, and this row is closed with that on
the record. The kata's PUNCH loop lives in the callee
`is_strobogrammatic(corpus, base, len)`, where `corpus`, `base` and `len` are
all PARAMETERS and `base + lo < corpus.len()` is not an intra-procedural truth —
it holds only because every caller passes `base = k*len` with `k < n` and
`corpus.len() == n*len`. Every analysis in `bce_length_pin.rs` runs per-function
over `func.body`, so the remainder is not a deeper version of this fix; it needs
interprocedural preconditions or IRCE-style loop versioning, a different feature
at a different scale. SPLIT TO B-2026-08-05-6 rather than left as a
permanently-open tail on a row whose named shape is finished — the same
treatment B-2026-08-04-13 got when it came off this entry.

── CORRECTION 2026-08-05 (see B-2026-08-05-21) ──

THIS ENTRY'S HEADLINE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG, and the row's own EVIDENCE 2 is the
reason it looked right. EVIDENCE 2 added Kara-equivalent BOUNDS checks to the C
mirror, measured 1.28x, and concluded "the whole residual gap is the missing
BCE". That is affirming the consequent: it shows bounds checks are SUFFICIENT to
cost ~1.28x in C, not that they are what costs Kara 1.28x.

The direct experiment, now possible because B-2026-08-05-6 (c87f488) eliminated
the callee-side checks, refutes it. With both punch-loop bounds checks provably
gone (disassembly: 21 -> 18 instructions, 2 -> 0 `cmp $0x9c400`), kata #246 moved
only 45.12ms -> 43.71ms (min of 80) -- about 3%, 1.29x -> 1.25x. The elision is
real and it is nearly worthless here.

WHAT ACTUALLY COSTS THE 1.23x is Kara's INTEGER OVERFLOW check on the index add
`base + lo`, which sits on the loop-carried critical path. C's mirror never
computes that add -- it passes `corpus + i*LEN`, folding the base into the
pointer -- so it was never an equal-safety comparison in the axis this entry
assumed. Isolated by control: C rewritten to the `base+idx` form UNCHECKED is
35.15ms (parity), and the same C plus `__builtin_add_overflow` is 43.04ms,
landing on Kara's 43.71ms. Full table in B-2026-08-05-21.

The BCE work this entry motivated remains correct and worth keeping -- the shape
recurs, and the elision is sound. Only the claim that it was #246's gap is
withdrawn.

title: `?` on an Option/Result whose payload is heap-BOXED unwraps the BOX POINTER as if it were the payload's first word -- the value comes out empty or garbage under AOT while `karac run` is correct, and the box leaks
detail:
REPRO (probe b231/i4, three lines, no destructure involved): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` (6 words), `fn res(i: i64) -> Result[Full, String] { return Result.Ok(mk(i)); }`, then inside a `Result`-returning fn: `let r = res(i)?; println(f"{r.name}");`. AOT prints an EMPTY string; `karac run --interp` prints the real one. Valgrind: 60 bytes definitely lost in 2 blocks. `karac check` is clean and nothing warns.  A full destructure makes the corruption visible rather than merely empty -- b231/i3 (`let Full { name, buf } = res(i)?;`) prints `i3::94197037118224`, i.e. `buf.len()` reading a pointer-shaped value.  WIDTH IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, not Option-vs-Result -- the same lesson as B-2026-08-02-25, and the 4-corner matrix was run to establish it rather than assumed:    b231/j1, j4: a 4-word payload (`{String, i64}`) through `Result` (5-word area) -- INLINE -- correct, vg=0.    b231/j3: the SAME 4-word payload through `Option` (3-word area) -- BOXED -- empty output, 28 bytes lost.    b231/j2, i1-i4: a 6-word payload through either carrier -- BOXED -- empty/garbage output, 60 bytes lost.  So one struct behaves correctly or not depending only on which carrier it rides, which is the signature of a missing debox.  IT IS `?`, NOT THE DESTRUCTURE OR THE CALL. Same payload, same fn: `let Full { name, buf: _ } = mk(i);` (b231/i5, no `?`) is clean, and `let Full { name, buf: _ } = res(i).unwrap();` (b231/i6, `.unwrap()` instead of `?`) is clean. Only the `?` spelling breaks. Every `?` shape tested breaks the same way: bare binding (i4), partial destructure (i2), full destructure (i3), and `let` destructure directly on the `?` (i1).  MECHANISM, read from the code and consistent with every measurement: `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` (src/codegen/exprs.rs) rebuilds the unwrapped payload by pulling words STRAIGHT OUT of the Result/Option aggregate -- `build_extract_value(sv, 1)`, `(sv, 2)`, `(sv, 3)` -> `rebuild_value_from_payload_words(ok_llvm, w0, w1, w2)` (and, for an all-i64 payload, a flat word-by-word copy just above it). Both branches assume the payload words ARE the payload. For a boxed payload w0 is the box POINTER and w1/w2 are undef, so a `{ptr,len,cap}` String rebuilds as `{box_ptr, undef, undef}` -- prints empty, and the real buffer plus the box itself are never freed (2 blocks: the box and the String buffer).  THE FIX SHAPE ALREADY EXISTS one module over. `reconstruct_payload_value` (control_flow_match.rs) has the debox: predicate `want > field_words.len()`, then inttoptr word 0, load the payload type through it, re-split via `coerce_to_payload_words`. `reconstruct_question_ok_payload` needs the same guard before either rebuild branch -- compare `llvm_type_word_count(ok_llvm)` against the carrier's payload area (3 for `Option`, 5 for `Result`, or just `n_fields - 1` off the aggregate it already has) and debox when it exceeds it.  OWNERSHIP IS THE OTHER HALF, and it is the part to get right rather than fast. `?` CONSUMES its operand, so after the debox the unwrapped value owns the interior and the BOX allocation itself must be freed -- that is one of the two leaked blocks and it stays leaked even if the debox alone lands. `suppress_question_source_inline_payload` is the existing disarm for this position and its doc is explicit that it only understands the INLINE overlay (it zeroes the slot's `cap` at field 3, which for a boxed payload is not a cap at all). It needs a boxed sibling.  PRE-EXISTING: not attributable to any of today's fixes. The `?` path was not touched by B-2026-08-04-5 or -6 (name resolution and box-drop field ownership respectively), and `.unwrap()` -- which shares the payload reconstruction machinery but not `compile_question` -- is clean.  HOW IT SURFACED: a post-fix sweep over the boxed-payload family after B-2026-08-04-6, deliberately probing axes the corpus under-covers. Nine other shapes in the same sweep were clean (borrow scrutinee partial and repeated-read, nested struct destructure both spellings, guard arm, escaping bound field, early return out of the arm, mutating Drop body, loop with `continue`, `Option`-typed payload field), so this is a narrow hole, not a broad one.  ORACLE NOTE: visible to ALL THREE oracles at once, which is unusual for this family and makes it cheap to pin -- parity diffing (AOT empty vs interp correct), direct output assertion, and valgrind/LSan (60 bytes). Prefer a parity + output pin; the leak count will change once the box free lands.  FIXED (2026-08-04, 60087fc), and the row's diagnosis held on the boxed half exactly as written -- the debox went in with the predicate, the three steps, and the ownership answer the row spelled out. `?` consumes its operand, so the loaded value owns the interior and the box is dead the moment it is read; freeing it AT the debox turned out to need no counterpart in `suppress_question_source_inline_payload`, which is a simpler answer than the row expected.  A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT in the same function, found while building the fixture for the first and NOT predicted by this row: a payload that is WIDE BUT INLINE. `Mid { name: String, pad: i64 }` is 4 words and FITS `Result`'s 5-word area, so it never boxes and never reaches the debox -- and it was still wrong, because `rebuild_value_from_payload_words` carries exactly w0/w1/w2 and silently dropped every word past the third. The String came back correct and `pad` came back 1 where the program stored 3 (probe b231/t1 line `b`; stash-proven identical at base, so pre-existing and unrelated to the debox). The flat-copy branch just above only rescues an ALL-i64 payload, which a String-bearing struct is not. Fixed by reading the full payload span and rebuilding through `reconstruct_struct_from_words` -- the same helper the match-arm path uses -- gated on `want > 3` so narrower payloads keep the original path byte-for-byte.  This is why the row's title understates the bug: `?` was wrong for BOTH over-area and over-three-words payloads, and only the first is a boxing question. `Mid` now appears under both carriers in the pins -- inline through `Result`, boxed through `Option` -- so one type exercises both defects.  VERIFIED: 24 probes (b231/a1..k4 and t1) all parity-EQUAL, valgrind 0 except the residual below. Suites: codegen 2778, memory_sanitizer 926, interpreter 1441, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5384 passed, 0 failed. Both pins stash-proven RED -- the E2E against the exact garbage output (`a::94685901742848
b:mid-3:1
c:
...`), the ASAN pin at 12,800 bytes under LeakSanitizer.  RESIDUAL, filed as B-2026-08-04-10: `let <StructPattern> = <expr>?` -- destructuring DIRECTLY on the `?` rather than through a binding -- still leaks 60 bytes. Deliberately excluded from the ASAN pin.
fix: 60087fc (src/codegen/exprs.rs, src/codegen/control_flow_match.rs for the helper's visibility; pins codegen.rs::e2e_question_reconstructs_wide_and_boxed_ok_payloads, its interpreter oracle interpreter.rs::test_question_reconstructs_wide_and_boxed_ok_payloads, and memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_question_deboxed_ok_payload_frees_the_box -- the first two stash-proven RED on the exact garbage output, the third at 12,800 bytes under LeakSanitizer)

title: `let <StructPattern> = <expr>?;` -- a struct destructure written DIRECTLY on a `?` whose payload is heap-boxed -- leaks the payload's heap fields; routing through an intermediate binding first is clean
detail: REPRO (probe b231/k4, 60 bytes definitely lost in 2 blocks under valgrind, parity-EQUAL so no run-vs-build split and the printed values are correct): `struct Full { name: String, buf: Vec[i64] }` (6 words, BOXED at either payload area), `fn res(i: i64) -> Result[Full, String] { return Result.Ok(mk(i)); }`, then inside a `Result`-returning fn: `let Full { name, buf } = res(i)?; println(f"{name}:{buf.len()}");`. The two lost blocks are the String buffer and the Vec buffer -- BOTH fields are bound, and neither binding owns its buffer.  THREE CLEAN CONTROLS, which localize it to one syntactic form:    b231/k3 -- `let t = res(i)?; let Full { name, buf } = t;` (the SAME destructure, one binding earlier) is vg=0.    b231/k2 -- `let Full { name, buf } = res(i).unwrap();` is vg=0.    b231/k1 -- `let Full { name, buf } = mk(i);` (no carrier at all) is vg=0.  So it is not the destructure, not the boxing, and not `?` on its own (a plain `let r = res(i)?;` binding is vg=0 -- probe b231/i4). It is the two together with no binding in between. The partial spelling (`buf: _`, b231/i1) leaks identically, so it is not about which fields are bound either.  LIKELY MECHANISM, unverified: the let-destructure path registers its leaf bindings' cleanup off the RHS being a recognized owned source, and the `?` expression is not in that roster -- `.unwrap()` and a direct call both are. The intermediate binding in k3 works because the binding itself registers, and the destructure then disarms it per field. Start by comparing what the `let`-with-struct-pattern path does for a `Call` RHS versus a `Question` RHS; do not start in `compile_question`, which B-2026-08-04-9 just fixed and which hands back a correct, owned value in every other spelling.  PRE-EXISTING but only now MEASURABLE: before 60087fc this shape produced garbage values as well as leaking, so the leak could not be attributed cleanly. The values are correct now and the leak is what is left.  ORACLE NOTE: valgrind/LSan only -- both backends print the same correct output. Deliberately kept OUT of `memory_sanitizer.rs::asan_question_deboxed_ok_payload_frees_the_box` (which routes through a binding, the clean spelling) so LSan does not attribute this row's leak to that pin.  SOURCE NOTE: surfaced while verifying B-2026-08-04-9's fix, in the same b231 sweep.  FIXED (2026-08-04, a82b4ff). The row's LIKELY MECHANISM was right, and the roster it guessed at is a single predicate: `finish_owned_struct_destructure` asks `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp` whether the RHS is a fresh owned temp, and that fn is literally `matches!(expr.kind, Call | MethodCall) && !is_borrow_returning_call_expr`. A `?` is neither variant, so `fresh` was false, the destructure took its place-source path, and the leaf bindings registered nothing. That also explains all three controls exactly: `.unwrap()` is a MethodCall, `mk(i)` is a Call, and the intermediate binding in k3 works because the BINDING registers and the destructure then disarms it per field.  SHIPPED: look THROUGH the `?` at its operand at this one site. `?` moves its Ok payload out and the operand's own cleanup is disarmed at the `?` site, so a fresh owned operand yields a fresh owned unwrapped value.  SCOPED ON PURPOSE, and this is the part worth keeping: the change is at the destructure, NOT inside `expr_yields_fresh_owned_temp`. That predicate's other callers are the fresh-temp scrutinee trackers, whose ownership contracts a `?` operand has not been measured against -- widening it there would silently change box tracking, inline-payload registration and shared Option release all at once. Recursing on the OPERAND rather than returning a flat `true` also leaves `let S { .. } = r?` (a named binding operand) at today's behavior, so only the shape the probes prove broken moves.  VERIFIED: all 15 `?` probes (b231/i1..k4 and t1) parity-EQUAL and vg=0, including the three that leaked -- i1 (partial destructure on `?`), i3 (full), k4 (the minimal form). Suites: codegen 2778, memory_sanitizer 926, interpreter 1441, drop_differential 13, par_codegen 226 = 5384 passed, 0 failed.  PIN: rather than a new test, `asan_question_deboxed_ok_payload_frees_the_box` gained the direct-destructure spelling and lost its "deliberately not covered" note -- the two spellings belong in one fixture now that both are covered. Stash-proven RED against THIS commit's `stmts.rs` change alone (the B-2026-08-04-9 half left in place) at 6,400 bytes under LeakSanitizer, which is what attributes the leak to this row rather than to that one.
