CORRECTION 1 -- THERE IS NO STRING/VEC ASYMMETRY. Every "String fields are
freed correctly" measurement in this row, including the third pass's "the
String path is genuinely correct, not a latent UAF", was taken at -O2, where
LLVM DELETES the dead String allocation outright. "No leak" meant "nothing was
allocated". Proof, same program built both ways, 200 iterations:

    payload      -O2 total allocs   -O0 definitely lost
    String       40 (baseline)      8,000 B in 200 blocks    <- 40 B/call
    Vec          240                19,200 B in 200 blocks   <- 96 B/call

The Vec allocation survives -O2 and the String one does not, and that is the
entire origin of the "asymmetry". The KARAC_ASAN_ALLOC_AUDIT=1 harness flag
catches this class directly and should be the FIRST thing run on any fixture in
this area: four of five probes written for this pass reported the 3-allocation
BASELINE, i.e. they asserted nothing while reading green.

CORRECTION 2 -- THE ARGUMENT FORM IS IRRELEVANT. The row had leg B needing a
FRESH TEMP, with `let r = mk(); take(r)` clean. That let-bound probe used a
callee that MATCHES. With an ignoring callee the let-bound form leaks exactly as
the temp does (19,200 B / 200 blocks). The real variable was always the CALLEE
BODY, never the argument form.

THE RULE, measured at -O0 over 200 iterations (blank = all heap blocks freed):

    shape                                       str payload   vec payload
    fresh temp, callee never destructures       LEAK          LEAK
    let-bound,  callee never destructures       LEAK          LEAK
    fresh temp, callee matches                  clean         clean
    let-bound,  callee matches                  clean         clean
    discarded (`mk();`)                         clean         clean
    inline `match mk() { .. }`                  clean         clean
    `let r = mk();` and never used              clean         clean

SCOPE -- it is the two BUILT-IN enums, not enums in general. By-value param,
callee ignores it, -O0, 200 iterations:

    param type                      verdict
    Vec[String]                     clean
    S { b: Vec[String] } (struct)   clean
    user enum W.Full(S)             clean
    Option[S] / Option[Vec[..]]     LEAKS
    Result[S,E] / Result[Vec,E]     LEAKS

MECHANISM, both sides identified, each confirmed by a measurement rather than by
reading:

  1. The CALLER retracts. `let r = mk();` never used is CLEAN, so the caller
     does register a drop for a let-bound Result local. Adding `take(r)` makes
     it leak, so passing it as an argument retracts that drop.

     CORRECTED WHILE FIXING (this attribution was wrong when first written, and
     naming the wrong emitter mattered because the fix hangs off which one it
     is). The retraction is NOT the cap-zeroing
     `suppress_inline_result_payload_cleanup_for_moved_arg` -- that one fires
     only at container-insert destinations (`v.push(r)`, `m.insert(k, r)`) and
     at a `let p = o;` rebind, never at a plain call. Reading `main`'s emitted
     IR for the two programs shows what actually happens:

         %r1 = load { i64 x 6 }, ptr %r
         store { i64 x 6 } zeroinitializer, ptr %r      <- the WHOLE slot
         call void @take({ i64 x 6 } %r1)

     `suppress_inline_option_result_binding_move` (`src/codegen/call_dispatch.rs`,
     under `!borrow_skip && !call_arg_flows_into_return`) zeroes the ENTIRE
     slot, tag included. The caller's overlay drop is still emitted and still
     runs -- it just reads tag 0, takes the `Err`/`None` arm and frees nothing.
     That one emission causes BOTH this leak and B-2026-08-12-1's wrong-variant
     read, and its own comment states the invariant it depends on: the
     whole-slot zero "is a MOVE, and it only balances when some other frame
     takes the box over". For a plain call, nobody did.

  2. The CALLEE bails. `make_aggregate_param_callee_owned_inst`
     (`src/codegen/param_own.rs`, the `if layout.is_shared || type_name ==
     "Option" || type_name == "Result" { return false }` arm) leaves both
     built-ins on caller-retains. A user ENUM falls through to the entry
     deep-copy + `track_enum_var` path, which is exactly why the user-enum row
     of the scope table is clean.

  So for a plain call the destination does NOT take ownership, the caller's
  retraction is unbacked, and nothing owns the payload. When the callee MATCHES,
  the arm binding becomes an owned local and drops it -- which is the whole
  reason the match column reads clean, and why this row spent three passes
  believing the match was irrelevant.

  This also corrects the THIRD pass's reading of `mk`. Both the String and Vec
  producers emit the SAME move barrier (`store i64 0` into the source local's
  cap word right after copying it into the payload) and the same `cap > 0`-
  guarded cleanup, which that barrier then skips. `mk` is symmetric and correct;
  the KARAC_TRACE_CLEANUP registration it printed is emitted but never runs. The
  producer does not lose the buffer -- the caller/callee boundary does.

FIX DESIGN. The two sides must move in LOCKSTEP; landing either alone is worse
than the leak.

  * TAKE: callee-owned via ENTRY DEEP-COPY (the #14 model user enums already
    use) AND drop the caller-side retraction for a plain-call argument. Then the
    caller frees its original, the callee frees its copy, and `take(r); take(r)`
    is correct on both counts. This ALSO fixes B-2026-08-12-1. Needs a deep copy
    for Option/Result payloads; `option_payload_struct_or_enum_copyable` and
    `result_payload_struct_enum_copyable` already exist in param_own.rs, so the
    predicates are there and the copy emitters are the work.

  * REJECTED -- own-by-transfer (B-2026-08-05-33's pattern: register the drop
    with no copy, in lockstep with the caller's existing retraction). It fixes
    the leak, survives `take(r); take(r)` (the second pass arrives cap-zeroed so
    the guard skips), and is far smaller. But it turns `take(r); <use r>` into a
    USE-AFTER-FREE: the move-checker deliberately does not reject use-after-move
    (param_own.rs, "Why not move-by-default"), so that program compiles today
    and merely reads a corrupted value. Trading a bounded leak for a UAF is the
    same bad trade the first three passes declined.

  * REJECTED -- caller-retains only (gate the retraction, leave the callee
    alone). The callee's match still frees the payload, so the caller's restored
    drop would double-free every matching callee -- the whole clean column of
    the matrix above.

STILL NOT FIXED, but the reason has changed and the old blocker is GONE. The
first three passes declined because adding a Vec free without knowing what freed
the String risked a double free. That premise is void: nothing freed the String
either. What remains is scope, not risk-of-the-unknown -- the fix is the
entry-deep-copy slice above, both halves together, in the same subsystem as the
open B-2026-08-11-29 SEGV.

    interp   45517  45517 200  3000000000

`karac check` passes. A bare comparison on the same element (`h16.px[0] >
40000u16`) is CORRECT, so the stored value is fine -- it is the widening cast
that goes wrong. The same `Vec` named by a LOCAL (`v[0] as f64`) is also
correct, on both backends. Only the field-reached container is affected.

WHY. `compile_cast` is not at fault: it branches on `source_is_unsigned` and
picks zext or sext correctly. The flag arrives false. `expr_is_unsigned_int`
resolves its `Index` arm only when the container is an `ExprKind::Identifier`,
through `var_elem_type_exprs` -- a table keyed by VARIABLE NAME, which has
nothing to say about struct fields. `holder.px[i]` therefore fell past it to
the signed default. The neighbouring `FieldAccess` arm already knew how to
resolve a field's declared type (receiver type name -> field index -> field
TypeExpr); the Index arm simply never used it, and needs one extra step
afterwards, because the field's own path is `Vec`, whose last segment is not a
uint name -- the element type lives in `generic_args`.

HOW IT PRESENTED, which is the part worth recording. A calibration master dark
is a `Vec[u16]` held in a struct. Every pixel above 32767 read back negative, so
`light - dark` ADDED about 65536 at exactly the hot pixels calibration exists to
remove, and the calibrated stack measured 1.4x WORSE than the uncalibrated one
with hot pixels rising rather than falling. That is a plausible symptom of a
badly written calibrator, and two rounds went into correcting the synthetic
generator's physics first -- one of which WAS a genuine error on my side (the
generator vignetted the dark current, which the optics never touch). The
compiler only became the suspect when the arithmetic stopped fitting any correct
calibrator: 46761 - 45517 must be 1244, and a result of 65535 requires the
subtrahend to be -20019.

WHY HIGH: silent wrong numbers with no diagnostic from any phase, in a shape --
a numeric buffer held in a struct -- that any numerical program reaches
immediately. The AOT/interp split is what makes it expensive, since `--interp`
reports the program correct.

FIXED. All three widths are pinned in the regression test rather than just the
u16 that surfaced it: each has a distinct wrap point, one arm covers them all,
and a fix that handled only u16 would leave the others silently broken. The
test is confirmed to fail without the fix with exactly the pre-fix values.

fix:
FIXED by c081b16.

The match arm's struct-payload binding is now admitted when the struct's only
non-duplicable heap is a `Map`/`Set` HANDLE, so it registers the
`track_struct_var` that frees it.

WHY IT WAS EXCLUDED, and why the exclusion was one condition too wide. The
`is_inline_optres_struct_payload` arm (pattern_binding.rs, B-2026-07-10-3) exists
for exactly this class -- "the struct's inner heap was owned by NOBODY and
leaked" -- but gates on `aggregate_param_copy_supported_struct`, which is FALSE
for a Map/Set field because the entry copy cannot duplicate a side-table handle.
Copy-supported and drop-supported come apart here: the synthesized struct drop
DOES free a Map field, which is why the same struct let-bound directly
(`let s = mk();` over `fn mk() -> S`) was already leak-clean. The arm needs the
FREE, not the copy, so the new predicate `struct_heap_copyable_or_handle` admits
a direct handle field and nothing else -- a nested struct still has to be fully
copy-supported, so the widening is exactly the measured case.

Nobody else owned it: the consuming arm zeroes the scrutinee's payload words
unconditionally (`respl.suppress.w1..w3`, read off the emitted IR for this
shape), so the `Result`'s own payload drop finds a null handle and frees
nothing. valgrind: 14,400 B direct plus 105,600 B indirect over 200 iterations,
the whole map from `karac_map_new`.

THREE CONDITIONS NARROW IT, and each was forced by a test rather than chosen:

  * the arm must only BORROW the binding. An arm that moves it on
    (`Ok(s) => take(s)`) hands ownership to the move machinery, whose
    source-zeroing clears Vec/String CAPS and not a side-table handle -- so a
    drop registered here is never retracted and the handle is freed twice. That
    is B-2026-08-11-29's SEGV, and its pin
    (`test_e2e_result_struct_wrapper_moved_to_callee_and_its_controls`) caught
    the over-fire immediately. Needed a new per-ARM flag,
    `pattern_binding_arm_only_borrows`; every neighbouring flag is per-match,
    but this is a property of the arm body.
  * the scrutinee must not be a FRESH OWNING TEMP (`match mk() { .. }`). That
    temp keeps its own payload cleanup, so the shape was already clean and a
    drop here is a second owner -- caught by the same pin's `inline_use` control.
  * the scrutinee must not be an OWNED PARAM, which is the case the surrounding
    comment's use-after-free warning is about: a non-copy-supported payload
    leaves an owned param on caller-retains, so freeing the binding there would
    turn a status-quo leak into a UAF on `sink(e); use(e)`.

VERIFIED at KARAC_OPT_LEVEL=0 under valgrind over 200 iterations: the row's
repro and every shape in its matrix are clean -- `Map` and `Set` fields,
`Option` and `Result` wrappers -- and the controls that were already clean stay
clean (bare `Result[Map,E]` with no struct, the struct with no enum wrapper, the
inline match, and the let-bound-unused form). `#[ignore]` lifted on
`asan_let_bound_result_map_field_leaks_on_match`.

title: `tests/codegen.rs`'s E2E harness ran `resolve` and `typecheck` only to feed `lower` and DISCARDED their errors, so the suite stayed green on 40 programs `karac check` rejects and `karac build` exits 1 on -- codegen pinned as working what no user can compile (`Set.clear`, `Vec.iter_mut`, `Column.range`, `Vec.collect`, the `Unit` type, `CStr.from_ptr` pointer mutability). detail: SOURCE NOTE: found while investigating B-2026-08-11-34 (the harness rejecting source the CLI accepts). This is the same divergence pointing the other way -- a false PASS -- and it is the one that reproduced. -- MEASURED over the whole `tests/codegen.rs` suite (2905 tests, instrumented run): 40 programs reached codegen with a resolve or typecheck error. Spot-checked end to end on the CLI: `test_e2e_set_clear`'s program gets `error[typecheck]: no method 'clear' on type 'Set'` from `karac check` (exit 1) and `karac build` exits 1 on the identical source, while the E2E test was green. -- TWO POPULATIONS, wanting opposite fixes, both enumerated with their diagnostics in `CHECK_GATE_GRANDFATHERED`. (1) REAL FRONT-END GAPS (10): codegen implements something the front end rejects, so the pinned shape is uncompilable by any user -- `Set.clear`, `Vec.iter_mut`, `Column.range`, a re-`collect` of a `Vec` terminal, `undefined type 'Unit'` (x2, the union corpus), `CStr.from_ptr` const-vs-mut, an Option-shaped user enum vs the builtin, arithmetic on an unbounded type param, a non-`mut` shared-struct field write. Each is worth its own row. The 40 existing offenders are grandfathered by test name with their diagnostics, so the gate lands strict for NEW tests while the backlog is triaged -- the posture the ownership gate set. -- ONE PROGRAM WAS FIXED RATHER THAN GRANDFATHERED: `test_e2e_iter_chain_reduce_float_and_narrow_int_payload` called `.max()`/`.min()` on a `Vec[f64]`, which B-2026-08-11-15 (the same author, days earlier) made a type error; its reduce legs -- the row's actual subject -- are untouched and the max/min legs now go through the `F64` wrapper. That is the gate catching a shape a compiler change had silently orphaned, which is the whole point of it. -- VERIFIED NON-VACUOUS by negative control: an un-grandfathered test whose program calls `Set.clear` FAILS with `[check-gate] ... program fails karac check (0 resolve + 1 type error(s)) ... type 1:46: no method 'clear' on type 'Set'`. Suite green at 2905 passed / 0 failed with the gate live. -- NOT COVERED, deliberately: only `run_program_capturing_inner` is gated. The ~1000-fixture `tests/memory_sanitizer.rs` harness and the other 51 codegen-invoking harnesses in `tests/codegen.rs` are not, and a separate measured divergence in the same file is untouched -- 46 of those 52 harnesses never run `desugar_program` and 47 never run `expand_gated_stdlib_imports`, so they resolve the RAW parse tree and compile a different program than `karac build` does.

fix:
FIXED by 3e8d8fa9 -- and the row's nondeterminism has a mundane explanation that
is worth more than the fix: the leak is DETERMINISTIC, and LeakSanitizer was the
unreliable part.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS. `cur = stats[j].region` cap-zeroes the source so the
element's owner stops freeing it (B-2026-08-11-25's fix) -- which leaves whatever
`cur` held BEFORE with no owner at all. `trigger_eager_free` (src/codegen/stmts.rs,
the Assign arm) frees the target's displaced buffer and classifies every other
transferring RHS -- a moved alias, a fresh ref, the `mk().s` fresh-temp staging, a
bare `v[i]` -- but had NO arm for a field moved out of a deeper place. A
`FieldAccess` matches none of them, so the displaced buffer was orphaned once per
execution of the assignment.

So the row's reading was right in substance: the assignment-path cap-zeroing did
trade the double free for a leak, in exactly the mode the fixture's comment
predicts. What it could not see is that the leak arrives through the DISPLACED
TARGET rather than the moved source, which is why it is invisible to the value
pins and why the repair is an added free rather than a narrowed suppression.

WHY IT LOOKED NONDETERMINISTIC. The fixture's max-by-revenue loop overwrites
`best_region` only when the running max improves -- twice across its 40 elements
-- so exactly ONE buffer is displaced per run. One leaked pointer left behind in a
stale stack slot reads to LSan as still-reachable, and whether that slot survives
depends on what ran before it in the process. Under valgrind, which reports
`definitely lost` from the same tree on every run, it is 8 bytes in 1 block,
every time. That also explains the direction of the flake the row found puzzling
(green in the full parallel suite, red standalone): it is not scheduling, it is
stack residue.

It did not reproduce for me at all -- 15 standalone runs green, the full suite
green, KARAC_PAR_WORKERS 1/2/4/8/16 all green, and green on the row's own tree
(9789448) at three runs. `cannot reproduce` would have been the wrong conclusion:
valgrind found it immediately on the first try.

BISECTED to the leg rather than guessed: of the fixture's three assignments, the
`out = cat[0].region` and `got = vs[0].xs` legs are clean and only the loop leaks,
and the leak scales exactly with the overwrite count (6 iterations -> 5 blocks, 11
-> 10). Two controls stay clean and bound the shape: `cur = <fresh String>` and
`cur = s.region` where `s` is a plain local. It is the deeper-place branch only.

THE ALIAS GUARD, which is the part worth reading. The naive fix -- add the arm --
is WORSE than the bug. This arm is the only one whose RHS can alias the slot it
overwrites: after the first `cur = box[0].s` the source is cap-zeroed INTO `cur`,
so a second execution of the same assignment reads a place that now aliases `cur`
itself, and freeing "the old value" frees the buffer about to be stored back.
Measured with the arm unguarded: correct content on the first read, garbage on
the second, two invalid reads under valgrind. `zero_vec_slot_header_if_aliases`
compares the two pointers and zeroes len/cap when they match, so the cap-gated
free and the len-gated element walks all no-op -- one icmp and two selects on a
path that already loads the header.

PINS, and why the existing one could not do this job. The sibling ASAN fixture
leaks one block, which is what LSan misses -- keeping it and adding a line would
have re-created the same blind spot.
`asan_place_field_move_assign_overwrite_no_leak` overwrites 200 times, past any
reachability accident: 3088 bytes in 193 allocations pre-fix, clean post-fix.
`test_e2e_repeated_place_field_move_assign_reads_correctly` pins the guard with a
CONTENT read, because `.len()` comes from the header and reads correctly off a
dangling pointer -- a length-only pin would have seen nothing.

Corrected while here, as the row asked: the sibling fixture's stale
B-2026-08-11-33 cross-reference (an id collision from 2026-08-11) now reads -25,
and its "the loop is here to make such a leak accumulate" comment now says
plainly that it does not, and points at the fixture that does.

REMAINDER, split out as B-2026-08-12-13 rather than buried here: assigning twice
from the same already-moved place still leaks that one buffer, because both
source and target end up cap-zeroed and neither frees it. That is unchanged from
before this fix (it leaked the same 8 bytes then), and strictly better than the
pre-B-25 double free -- but it is a live defect, and `karac check` accepts the
program.
title: `asan_vec_element_field_move_by_assignment_no_double_free` is red on main with a LeakSanitizer leak, and NONDETERMINISTICALLY so: green in the full parallel suite run, red standalone, on one unchanged tree. It is the un-ignored regression pin from 970dadf (B-2026-08-11-25) and fails in exactly the over-broad-repair mode its own comment predicts, so the assignment-path cap-zeroing looks to have traded the double free for a per-iteration leak.
tracker: Regression pin from 970dadf (B-2026-08-11-25). NOT caused by 19d0e9a (B-2026-08-11-30) -- verified by stash-and-rebuild.
detail:
`asan_vec_element_field_move_by_assignment_no_double_free` in
`tests/memory_sanitizer.rs` is NOT `#[ignore]`d and fails with a LeakSanitizer
leak on current main. It is the regression pin commit 970dadf landed with its
own fix (B-2026-08-11-25, "cap-zero a moved-out heap field on the ASSIGNMENT
path too"), and the failure is precisely the mode that test's own comment warns
about:

    "the repair is to stop the owner freeing, so an over-broad version turns the
     double free into a per-iteration leak, which the value pins in
     tests/codegen.rs cannot see. The loop is here to make such a leak
     accumulate rather than hide."

IT IS NOT DETERMINISTIC, which is the reason this is filed rather than simply
handed back to that fix. Observed today on ONE unchanged source tree (the
pushed main, 9789448):

    full `cargo test --features llvm --test memory_sanitizer`   1039 passed / 0 failed   GREEN
    ... later, same commit, same command                        1038 passed / 1 failed   RED
    standalone, `-- <name> --test-threads=1`, three runs        RED, RED, RED

So it is green-flaky in the full parallel run and red standalone. A test that
can report green while the leak is present is the more dangerous half of this:
CI's memory-sanitizer job runs the full suite, so this can pass there and hide
the leak.

NOT CAUSED BY THE OPTION/RESULT PARAM OWNERSHIP FIX (B-2026-08-11-30, 19d0e9a).
Verified by stashing that change, rebuilding, and re-running both standalone and
full: identical failure with and without it. The fixture contains no
`Option`/`Result` parameter at all.

WHERE TO START: the harness runs fixtures with auto-par ENABLED, and
nondeterministic ASAN outcomes under auto-par are a known shape in this ledger
(B-2026-08-11-27 was a nondeterministic auto-par miscompile). Re-running the
fixture with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 to see whether the flake disappears is the first
thing to try; if it does, the question is the leak's dependence on scheduling
rather than the assignment-path cap-zeroing itself.

Note also that the fixture's doc comment cites B-2026-08-11-33, but that row is
about a `#[derive(Eq)]` struct temporary and this test is the B-2026-08-11-25
assignment-path pin -- a stale cross-reference from the id collisions of
2026-08-11, worth correcting when this is picked up.

Bisected the difference to the test rather than the change by stashing the fix, rebuilding and re-running -- identical failure with and without it, and the fixture has no Option/Result param. Then ran it standalone three times (red every time) against one green full-suite observation, which is what establishes the nondeterminism.

fix: a827a7f (route the `==` operator for a Vec-carrying struct to the existing TYPE-directed `emit_eq_fn_for_struct` via a new `try_compile_struct_eq_typed` in src/codegen/expr_ops.rs, gated by `struct_has_vec_field_deep`; the shape-directed field walk stays for every other struct)
tracker: `compile_struct_eq` in src/codegen/expr_ops.rs — the per-field recursion compares a `Vec` field by its `{ptr,len,cap}` words instead of element-wise; the interpreter's `value_compare` Array arm does compare contents
title: SILENT WRONG ANSWER (run-vs-build): `#[derive(Eq)]` equality over a struct with a `Vec[String]` field reports NOT EQUAL in both compiled backends for two vectors whose CONTENTS are equal, while the interpreter correctly reports equal. Measured on one program: `S { v: a } == S { v: b }` with both vectors holding \"abcd\" gives interp `true`, JIT `false`, AOT `false`. It is a FALSE NEGATIVE only -- differing contents correctly give `false` on all three -- so the failure mode is a comparison that silently never matches. NARROW AND MEASURED: a `Vec[i64]` field is CORRECT on all three (`true`), and a plain `String` field is CORRECT on all three, so it is specific to a Vec of HEAP elements. Reproduces with two struct LOCALS, no temporaries and no `ref` params, so it is independent of B-2026-08-11-24 / -33 (which are leaks in the same lowering's neighbourhood and cannot change a boolean).
detail:
SOURCE NOTE: found while building the over-fire matrix for B-2026-08-11-33 (fixed in 23e5d66) -- a control that compared a struct with a `Vec[String]` field returned `false` where it should have returned `true`, with ASAN clean. The leak work is unrelated: it registers a drop AFTER the comparison result is computed, and the divergence reproduces with plain locals where none of that machinery runs. -- THE FOUR-ROW MEASUREMENT, one program, interp vs JIT: `Vec[String]` field with EQUAL contents -> true / FALSE (wrong); `Vec[String]` field with DIFFERING contents -> false / false (right, accidentally); `Vec[i64]` field with equal contents -> true / true (right); plain `String` field with equal contents -> true / true (right). So scalar-element Vec fields and direct String fields both work, and only a heap-element Vec field is wrong. -- LIKELY CAUSE: `compile_struct_eq` recurses per field through `compile_binop`, which for a Vec-shaped field almost certainly compares the `{ptr,len,cap}` triple rather than dispatching to an element-wise comparator. Two independently built vectors have different `ptr`, hence always unequal; a `Vec[i64]` field presumably survives because it routes to a different path (that asymmetry is worth understanding before fixing, since it may indicate the correct dispatch already exists and is simply not reached for heap elements). The recursive `karac_cmp_Vec_String` comparator built for `Vec[Vec[String]].sort()` (B-2026-06-30-15) is the obvious thing to reuse. -- WHY THIS IS HIGH: equality that silently never matches is the worst shape of wrong answer -- no diagnostic, no crash, correct-looking output, and it degrades gracefully into 'the lookup just never finds anything'. A dedup, a cache-hit test, a `contains`-style scan or an assertion over any struct carrying a `Vec[String]` is silently broken under `karac build` while passing under `karac run --interp`, which is also the worst possible split for the Mend loop. -- NOT COVERED BY THE 3-BACKEND ORACLE in the usual way: interp and codegen DISAGREE here, so a differential test WOULD catch it; there simply was no test comparing a struct with a Vec field. Worth checking whether the same gap covers `Vec[Vec[i64]]` and `Map`/`Set`-valued fields when fixing.
 -- FIXED 2026-08-12 in a827a7f. -- THIS ROW'S OWN FILING UNDERSTATED THE BUG AND MISREPORTED ITS DIRECTION; corrected here by measurement, because acting on the filed characterization would have led to the wrong fix and a false sense of the blast radius. Filed as "false negative only, never a false positive" with "`Vec[i64]` is CORRECT on all three". Both are wrong. On scalar elements it is a FALSE POSITIVE machine: `I { v: [7] } == I { v: [263] }` was TRUE (263 = 0x107, identical low byte) and `I { v: [1,2] } == I { v: [1,3] }` was TRUE (the two bytes compared are element 0's low bytes). The filing's `Vec[i64]` control used [7] vs [7] and [7] vs [8], which differ in the FIRST BYTE and so happen to be the two cases the broken compare gets right. An equality that wrongly MATCHES is far worse than one that wrongly misses: a dedup silently merges distinct values and a cache returns a wrong hit, with no diagnostic. -- ROOT CAUSE, which the filing guessed correctly: `compile_struct_eq` recurses per field through `compile_binop`, and that dispatches on LLVM SHAPE. A `Vec` field and a `String` field are both `{ptr, len, cap}`, so Vec fields were handed to `compile_string_binop`, a byte compare of `len` bytes. For a String `len` IS the byte count and the compare is right; for a Vec `len` is the ELEMENT count, so it read the first `len` bytes of the element buffer and ignored the rest. That single fact predicts every measured row: scalar elements alias on their low bytes (false positives), and `Vec[String]` elements compare the low bytes of two distinct heap POINTERS (false negatives). -- THE FIX WAS ALREADY WRITTEN, ONCE. `emit_eq_fn_for_struct` dispatches per field on the declared TypeExpr and sends a `Vec[T]` field to `karac_eq_Vec_<T>` — length first, then element-wise, recursing through the dispatcher so heap elements compare by content. B-2026-06-20-15 built exactly that to fix exactly this bug in the HASHING path (`Set[Vec[T]]` dedup). The `==` OPERATOR simply never picked it up, so the same defect survived in the other half of the equality surface for two months. Worth generalizing: when a bug is fixed for containers, check the operator, and vice versa. -- GATED to structs carrying a Vec directly or through a nested struct field (`struct_has_vec_field_deep`, depth-capped), so every other struct keeps the inline field walk and this cannot regress the common case. -- TEST: ten shapes asserted against `karac run --interp`, which was correct throughout — both false positives, genuine equality, genuine difference, a LENGTH mismatch, both `Vec[String]` directions, `!=` as the exact negation, and a Vec-free struct as a control for the path left untouched. -- KNOWN ADJACENT, not covered: a `Vec[Vec[i64]]` struct FIELD is rejected upstream (before codegen), so the nested-container case could not be exercised here; `Map`/`Set`-valued fields were not tested and should be checked by whoever next touches this dispatch.
